one_liner: Helical 是一个面向单细胞与转录组学的生物基座模型开放框架，集成 Geneformer、scGPT、UCE、Tahoe-x1 等细胞大模型，支持微调与虚拟实验，高度契合虚拟细胞与细胞系统建模方向。

## 是什么
Helical 是一个开源的 Python 框架，旨在构建用于生物发现的虚拟 AI 实验室。它提供统一的接口来访问多种最新的生物基础模型（Bio Foundation Models），涵盖基因组学、转录组学和单细胞数据模态。Helical 简化了从模型访问、微调到计算机模拟实验的整个生命周期，使研究人员能够轻松地利用这些模型进行下游任务。

## 亮点
- **统一 API**：为所有集成模型提供一致的 Python 接口，降低使用门槛。
- **模型集成丰富**：集成了多种主流生物基础模型，包括 Geneformer、scGPT、UCE、TranscriptFormer、Cell2Sentence、Tahoe-x1、Helix-mRNA、Mamba2-mRNA、HyenaDNA、Caduceus、Evo2 等，覆盖 RNA 和 DNA 模态。
- **持续更新**：仓库持续更新，不断集成新模型和基准测试。
- **社区支持**：提供 Slack 频道和 GitHub Issues 支持，鼓励社区贡献。
- **可扩展性**：支持自定义模型和流程，便于用户针对自己的数据集进行实验。

## 为何对本课题有用
Helical 直接服务于虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型、生物大语言模型、Bio Agent 课题。它提供了：
- **单细胞基础模型**：如 Geneformer、scGPT、UCE、Tahoe-x1 等，可用于细胞嵌入、基因嵌入、细胞类型注释、扰动预测等任务，是构建虚拟细胞模型的核心组件。
- **空间组学支持**：虽然 README 未明确提及空间组学，但通过集成模型和统一接口，可以扩展处理空间转录组数据。
- **生物大语言模型**：如 Cell2Sentence 基于 Gemma 架构，Helix-mRNA 是 mRNA 基础模型，可用于序列生成和功能预测。
- **Bio Agent 基础**：框架的模块化设计允许将模型嵌入到自动化分析流程中，支持构建生物智能体。

## 怎么用
- **安装**：推荐使用 conda 创建 Python 3.12 环境，然后 `pip install helical`。如需 GPU 支持，可指定 CUDA 版本安装。
- **主入口**：通过 Python 导入 `helical` 包，使用 `Helical` 类或直接实例化具体模型类（如 `Geneformer`、`scGPT`）。
- **示例**：仓库提供多个 Jupyter Notebook 教程，如 `Quick-Start-Tutorial.ipynb`、`Tahoe-x1-Tutorial.ipynb`、`Cell2Sen-Tutorial.ipynb` 等，可直接在 Colab 中运行。
- **数据格式**：单细胞模型通常接受 AnnData（`.h5ad`）格式，DNA 模型接受 FASTA 格式，具体取决于模型。
- **GPU 需求**：需要 GPU 和 CUDA 支持，特别是使用 flash-attn 或 mamba-ssm 时。
- **测试**：`ci/tests/` 目录包含单元测试，可用于验证安装和调试。

## 核心 idea
Helical 的核心思想是提供一个**统一、模块化的接口层**，将多种异构的生物基础模型封装成一致的 API，从而降低研究人员使用这些模型的门槛，并促进模型之间的比较和组合。这种抽象使得用户无需关心底层模型的具体实现细节，即可快速进行下游任务实验，同时框架的持续更新保证了模型的时效性。

## 可搬移点
- **模型封装层**：`helical/models/base_models.py` 中的基类定义了统一的模型接口，可以借鉴其设计模式，将自定义模型封装成类似结构，便于集成到现有流程。
- **数据预处理工具**：`helical/utils/` 中的数据处理和下载工具（如 `downloader.py`）可以独立使用，用于处理单细胞数据。
- **微调模块**：`helical/models/fine_tune/` 中的微调头（fine-tuning heads）可以解耦，用于自定义分类或回归任务。
- **许可证**：仓库整体采用 AGPL-3.0 许可证（需确认），但各模型可能有自己的许可证，需分别确认。

**可迁移性评估**：Helical 的模块化设计支持逐步替换，可以将其中的模型类或工具函数导入到自定义 Pipeline 中，但需注意依赖关系（如 torch、anndata 等）。

# What is Helical ? Helical builds the Virtual AI Lab for Biological Discovery. This open framework provides access to state-of-the-art Bio Foundation Models across genomics, transcriptomics, and single-cell data modalities. Helical simplifies the entire lifecycle of applying Bio Foundation Models — from model access to fine-tuning and in-silico experimentation. With Helical's open-source framework, you can: • Leverage the latest Bio Foundation Models through a simple Python interface • Run example notebooks for key downstream tasks • Customize models and workflows for your own datasets and experiments This repository is continuously updated with new models, benchmarks, and utilities. Join us in shaping the next generation of AI-powered biology. Let’s build the most exciting AI-for-Bio community together!
![Workflow](https://github.com/helicalAI/helical/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)   ![Workflow](https://github.com/helicalAI/helical/actions/workflows/github-code-scanning/codeql/badge.svg)   [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-available-brightgreen)](https://helical.readthedocs.io/)   [![PyPI version](https://badge.fury.io/py/helical.svg)](https://badge.fury.io/py/helical)   ![GitHub contributors](https://img.shields.io/github/contributors/helicalAI/helical)  
## What's new? ### Tahoe-x1 We have integrated the Tahoe-x1 foundation model for single-cell RNA-seq data. This transformer-based model can extract both cell and gene embeddings from raw count data and supports attention weight extraction for interpretability. Try it out with our [comprehensive tutorial notebook](./examples/notebooks/Tahoe-x1-Tutorial.ipynb)! ### Cell2Sentence-Scale We have integrated the new Cell2Sentence-Scale models which use cell sentences as input and are based on the Gemma language model architecture (2B and 27B models available in quantised versions too). You can use this model for embeddings and perturbation prediction. Follow our notebook tutorial [here](./examples/notebooks/Cell2Sen-Tutorial.ipynb). ### New Larger Geneformer Models We have integrated the new Geneformer models which are larger and have been trained on more data. Find out which models have been integrated into the Geneformer suite in the [model card](./helical/models/geneformer/README.md). Check out the our notebook on drug perturbation prediction using different Geneformer scalings [here](./examples/notebooks/Geneformer-Series-Comparison.ipynb). ### TranscriptFormer We have integrated [TranscriptFormer](https://github.com/czi-ai/transcriptformer) into our helical package and have made a model card for it in our [Transcriptformer model folder](helical/models/transcriptformer/README.md). If you would like to test the model, take a look at our [example notebook](examples/notebooks/Geneformer-vs-TranscriptFormer.ipynb)! ### 🧬 Introducing Helix-mRNA-v0: Unlocking new frontiers & use cases in mRNA therapy 🧬 We’re thrilled to announce the release of our first-ever mRNA Bio Foundation Model, designed to: 1) Be Efficient, handling long sequence lengths effortlessly 2) Balance Diversity & Specificity, leveraging a 2-step pre-training approach 3) Deliver High-Resolution, using single nucleotides as a resolution Check out our blog post to learn more about our approach and read the model card to get started. ## Installation We recommend installing Helical within a conda environment with the commands below (run them in your terminal) - this step is optional: ``` conda create --name helical-package python=3.12.13 conda activate helical-package ``` To install the latest pip release of our Helical package, you can run the command below: ``` pip install helical ``` ***Note*** Sometimes Torch is not installed as the CUDA compiled version (e.g. on different architectures) which is why you need to manually install Helical with GPU support, run the command below (or install pytorch with cuda first and then install helical): ``` pip install helical --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cuXXX (replace XXX with your cuda version, e.g. 130 for cuda 13.0) ``` To install the latest Helical package, you can run the command below: ``` pip install --upgrade git+https://github.com/helicalAI/helical.git ``` Alternatively, clone the repo and install it: ``` git clone https://github.com/helicalAI/helical.git pip install . ``` ###Flash Attention Support To enable Flash Attention (required by some models), run the command below: ``` pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation ``` **Important** Make sure that your Pytorch CUDA Version matches your system CUDA version, especially when using flash-attn. ###Mamba-SSM Model Installation [Optional] To install mamba-ssm and causal-conv1d use the command below: ``` pip install helical[mamba-ssm] ``` or in case you're installing from the Helical repo cloned locally: ``` pip install .[mamba-ssm] ``` As a no-compile alternative on CUDA 13 / torch 2.10 / Python 3.12 (Linux x86_64), install the prebuilt accelerator wheels (mamba-ssm, causal-conv1d, flash-attn) on top of helical: ``` pip install . pip install -r requirements_cuda.txt ``` ### Development Installation To install the test and lint tooling (pytest, pytest-cov, pytest-mock, nbmake, black), use the `dev` extra: ``` pip install .[dev] ``` ###Evo2 Model Installation To install Evo2 Specifically, follow the instructions in the [evo-2 model card](helical/models/evo_2/README.md). ### Tahoe-X1 Model Installation To install Tahoe-X1 do the following after installing helical: ``` pip install helical[tahoe] ``` ## Notes on the installation: - Make sure your machine has GPU(s) and Cuda installed. Currently this is a requirement for the packages mamba-ssm and causal-conv1d. - The package `causal_conv1d` requires `torch` to be installed already. First installing `helical` separately (without `[mamba-ssm]`) will install `torch` for you. A second installation (with `[mamba-ssm]`), installs the packages correctly. - If you have problems building `mamba-ssm` from source, install the prebuilt `.whl` files instead. The set matching this release (CUDA 13 / torch 2.10 / Python 3.12, Linux x86_64) is pinned in [`requirements_cuda.txt`](./requirements_cuda.txt): ``` pip install -r requirements_cuda.txt ``` Choose a different wheel from the [mamba releases page](https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba/releases) if your cuda / torch / python version differs, e.g.: ``` pip install https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba/releases/download/v2.3.2.post1/mamba_ssm-2.3.2.post1+cu13torch2.10cxx11abiTRUE-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl ``` ### Singularity (Optional) If you desire to run your code in a singularity file, you can use the [singularity.def](./singularity.def) file and build an apptainer with it: ``` apptainer build --sandbox singularity/helical singularity.def ``` and then shell into the sandbox container (use the --nv flag if you have a GPU available): ``` apptainer shell --nv --fakeroot singularity/helical/ ``` ### RNA models: - [Helix-mRNA](https://helical.readthedocs.io/en/latest/model_cards/helix_mrna/) - [Mamba2-mRNA](https://helical.readthedocs.io/en/latest/model_cards/mamba2_mrna/) - [Geneformer](https://helical.readthedocs.io/en/latest/model_cards/geneformer/) - [scGPT](https://helical.readthedocs.io/en/latest/model_cards/scgpt/) - [Universal Cell Embedding (UCE)](https://helical.readthedocs.io/en/latest/model_cards/uce/) - [TranscriptFormer](https://helical.readthedocs.io/en/latest/model_cards/transcriptformer/) - [Tahoe-x1](https://helical.readthedocs.io/en/latest/model_cards/tahoe/) ### DNA models: - [HyenaDNA](https://helical.readthedocs.io/en/latest/model_cards/hyena_dna/) - [Caduceus](https://helical.readthedocs.io/en/latest/model_cards/caduceus/) - [Evo 2](https://helical.readthedocs.io/en/latest/model_cards/evo_2/) ## Demo & Use Cases To run examples, be sure to have installed the Helical package (see Installation) and that it is up-to-date. You can look directly into the example folder above and download the script of your choice, look into our [documentation](https://helical.readthedocs.io/) for step-by-step guides or directly clone the repository using: ``` git clone https://github.com/helicalAI/helical.git ``` Within the `examples/notebooks` folder, open the notebook of your choice. # TranscriptFormer


Overview of TranscriptFormer pretraining data (A), model (B), outputs (C) and downstream tasks (D).

**Authors:** James D Pearce, Sara E Simmonds*, Gita Mahmoudabadi*, Lakshmi Krishnan*, Giovanni Palla, Ana-Maria Istrate, Alexander Tarashansky, Benjamin Nelson, Omar Valenzuela, Donghui Li, Stephen R Quake, Theofanis Karaletsos (Chan Zuckerberg Initiative) *Equal contribution ## Description TranscriptFormer is a family of generative foundation models representing a cross-species generative cell atlas trained on up to 112 million cells spanning 1.53 billion years of evolution across 12 species. The models include three distinct versions: - **TF-Metazoa**: Trained on 112 million cells spanning all twelve species. The set covers six vertebrates (human, mouse, rabbit, chicken, African clawed frog, zebrafish), four invertebrates (sea urchin, C. elegans, fruit fly, freshwater sponge), plus a fungus (yeast) and a protist (malaria parasite). The model includes 444 million trainable parameters and 633 million non-trainable parameters (from frozen pretrained embeddings). Vocabulary size: 247,388. - **TF-Exemplar**: Trained on 110 million cells from human and four model organisms: mouse (M. musculus), zebrafish (D. rerio), fruit fly (D. melanogaster ), and C. ele- gans. Total trainable parameters: 542 million; non-trainable: 282 million. Vocabulary size: 110,290. - **TF-Sapiens**: Trained on 57 million human-only cells. This model has 368 million trainable parameters and 61 million non-trainable parameters. Vocabulary size: 23,829. TranscriptFormer is designed to learn rich, context-aware representations of single-cell transcriptomes while jointly modeling genes and transcripts using a novel generative architecture. It employs a generative autoregressive joint model over genes and their expression levels per cell across species, with a transformer-based architecture, including a novel coupling between gene and transcript heads, expression-aware multi-head self-attention, causal masking, and a count likelihood to capture transcript-level variability. TranscriptFormer demonstrates robust zero-shot performance for cell type classification across species, disease state identification in human cells, and prediction of cell type specific transcription factors and gene-gene regulatory relationships. This work establishes a powerful framework for integrating and interrogating cellular diversity across species as well as offering a foundation for in-silico experimentation with a generative single-cell atlas model. For more details, please refer to our manuscript: [A Cross-Species Generative Cell Atlas Across 1.5 Billion Years of Evolution: The TranscriptFormer Single-cell Model](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.25.650731v2) ## Installation Transcriptformer requires Python >=3.11. Instruction below is based on [*uv* package manager (install instruction here)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/). ### Install from PyPI ```bash # Create and activate a virtual environment uv venv --python=3.11 source .venv/bin/activate # On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate # Install from PyPI uv pip install transcriptformer ``` ### Install from source ```bash # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/czi-ai/transcriptformer.git cd transcriptformer # Create and activate a virtual environment with Python 3.11 uv venv --python=3.11 source .venv/bin/activate # On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate # Install in development mode uv pip install -e . ``` ### Requirements Transcriptformer has the following core dependencies: - PyTorch (<=2.5.1, as 2.6.0+ may cause pickle errors) - PyTorch Lightning - anndata - scanpy - numpy - pandas - h5py - hydra-core See the `pyproject.toml` file for the complete list of dependencies. ### Hardware Requirements - GPU (A100 40GB recommended) for efficient inference and embedding extraction. - Can also use a GPU with a lower amount of VRAM (16GB) by setting the inference batch size to 1-4. - **Multi-GPU support**: For faster inference on large datasets, use multiple GPUs with the `--num-gpus` parameter. - Recommended for datasets with >100k cells - Scales batch processing across available GPUs using Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) - Best performance with matched GPU types and sufficient inter-GPU bandwidth ## Using the TranscriptFormer CLI After installing the package, you'll have access to the `transcriptformer` command-line interface (CLI), which provides easy access to download model artifacts, download training datasets, and run inference. ### Downloading Model Weights Use the CLI to download model weights and artifacts from AWS S3: ```bash # Download a specific model transcriptformer download tf-sapiens transcriptformer download tf-exemplar transcriptformer download tf-metazoa # Download all models and embeddings transcriptformer download all # Download only the embedding files transcriptformer download all-embeddings # Specify a custom checkpoint directory transcriptformer download tf-sapiens --checkpoint-dir /path/to/custom/dir ``` The command will download and extract the following files to the `./checkpoints` directory (or your specified directory): - `./checkpoints/tf_sapiens/`: Sapiens model weights - `./checkpoints/tf_exemplar/`: Exemplar model weights - `./checkpoints/tf_metazoa/`: Metazoa model weights - `./checkpoints/all_embeddings/`: Embedding files for out-of-distribution species #### Available Protein Embeddings Out of the box, there are 24 species with protein embeddings available for download with the command: `transcriptformer download all-embeddings`. Models come with their respective training species embeddings. | Scientific Name | Common Name | TF-Metazoa | TF-Exemplar | TF-Sapiens | Notes | |-----------------|-------------|------------|-------------|------------|-------| | *Homo sapiens* | Human | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Primary training species | | *Mus musculus* | Mouse | ✓ | ✓ | - | Model organism | | *Danio rerio* | Zebrafish | ✓ | ✓ | - | Model organism | | *Drosophila melanogaster* | Fruit fly | ✓ | ✓ | - | Model organism | | *Caenorhabditis elegans* | C. elegans | ✓ | ✓ | - | Model organism | | *Oryctolagus cuniculus* | Rabbit | ✓ | - | - | Vertebrate | | *Gallus gallus* | Chicken | ✓ | - | - | Vertebrate | | *Xenopus laevis* | African clawed frog | ✓ | - | - | Vertebrate | | *Lytechinus variegatus* | Sea urchin | ✓ | - | - | Invertebrate | | *Spongilla lacustris* | Freshwater sponge | ✓ | - | - | Invertebrate | | *Saccharomyces cerevisiae* | Yeast | ✓ | - | - | Fungus | | *Plasmodium falciparum* | Malaria parasite | ✓ | - | - | Protist | | *Rattus norvegicus* | Rat | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | | *Sus scrofa* | Pig | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | | *Pan troglodytes* | Chimpanzee | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | | *Gorilla gorilla* | Gorilla | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | | *Macaca mulatta* | Rhesus macaque | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | | *Callithrix jacchus* | Marmoset | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | | *Xenopus tropicalis* | Western clawed frog | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | | *Ornithorhynchus anatinus* | Platypus | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | | *Monodelphis domestica* | Opossum | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | | *Heterocephalus glaber* | Naked mole-rat | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | | *Petromyzon marinus* | Sea lamprey | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | | *Stylophora pistillata* | Coral | - | - | - | Out-of-distribution | **Legend:** - ✓ = Species included in model training data - \- = Species not included in model training (out-of-distribution) ### Generating Protein Embeddings for New Species The pre-generated embeddings cover the most commonly used species. If you need to work with a species not included in the downloaded embeddings, you can generate protein embeddings using the ESM-2 models. **Note**: This is only necessary for new species that don't have pre-generated embeddings available for download. For detailed instructions on generating protein embeddings for additional species, see the [protein_embeddings/README.md](protein_embeddings/README.md) documentation. ### Downloading Training Datasets Use the CLI to download single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from the CellxGene Discover portal: ```bash # Download human datasets transcriptformer download-data --species "homo sapiens" --output-dir ./data/human # Download multiple species datasets transcriptformer download-data --species "homo sapiens,mus musculus" --output-dir ./data/multi_species # Download with custom settings transcriptformer download-data \ --species "homo sapiens" \ --output-dir ./data/human \ --processes 8 \ --max-retries 3 \ --no-metadata ``` The `download-data` command provides the following options: - `--species`: Comma-separated list of species to download (required). Common species names include: - "homo sapiens" (human) - "mus musculus" (mouse) - "danio rerio" (zebrafish) - "drosophila melanogaster" (fruit fly) - "caenorhabditis elegans" (C. elegans) - `--output-dir`: Directory where datasets will be saved (default: `./data/cellxgene`) - `--processes`: Number of parallel download processes (default: 4) - `--max-retries`: Maximum retry attempts per dataset (default: 5) - `--no-metadata`: Skip saving dataset metadata to JSON file **Note:** You can also use the module directly for programmatic access: ```python # Direct module usage python -m transcriptformer.data.bulk_download --species "homo sapiens" --output-dir ./data/human ``` **Downloaded Data Structure:** ``` output_dir/ ├── dataset_metadata.json # Metadata for all downloaded datasets ├── dataset_id_1/ │ ├── full.h5ad # Raw dataset in AnnData format │ └── __success__ # Download completion marker ├── dataset_id_2/ │ ├── full.h5ad │ └── __success__ └── ... ``` Each dataset is downloaded as an AnnData object in H5AD format, containing raw count data suitable for use with TranscriptFormer models. The metadata JSON file contains detailed information about each dataset including cell counts, tissue types, and experimental conditions. ### Running Inference Use the CLI to run inference with TranscriptFormer models: ```bash # Basic inference on in-distribution species (e.g., human with TF-Sapiens) transcriptformer inference \ --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \ --data-file test/data/human_val.h5ad \ --output-path ./inference_results \ --batch-size 8 # Inference on out-of-distribution species (e.g., mouse with TF-Sapiens) transcriptformer inference \ --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \ --data-file test/data/mouse_val.h5ad \ --pretrained-embedding ./checkpoints/all_embeddings/mus_musculus_gene.h5 \ --batch-size 8 # Extract contextual gene embeddings instead of cell embeddings transcriptformer inference \ --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \ --data-file test/data/human_val.h5ad \ --emb-type cge \ --batch-size 8 # Multi-GPU inference using 4 GPUs (-1 will use all available on the system) transcriptformer inference \ --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \ --data-file test/data/human_val.h5ad \ --num-gpus 4 \ --batch-size 32 ``` You can also use the CLI to run inference on the ESM2-CE baseline model discussed in the paper: ```bash transcriptformer inference \ --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \ --data-file test/data/human_val.h5ad \ --model-type esm2ce \ --batch-size 8 ``` ### Advanced Configuration For advanced configuration options not exposed as CLI arguments, use the `--config-override` parameter: ```bash transcriptformer inference \ --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \ --data-file test/data/human_val.h5ad \ --config-override model.data_config.normalize_to_scale=10000 \ --config-override model.inference_config.obs_keys.0=cell_type ``` To see all available CLI options: ```bash transcriptformer inference --help transcriptformer download --help transcriptformer download-data --help ``` ### CLI Options for `inference`: - `--checkpoint-path PATH`: Path to the model checkpoint directory (required). - `--data-file PATH`: Path to input AnnData file (required). - `--output-path DIR`: Directory for saving results (default: `./inference_results`). - `--output-filename NAME`: Filename for the output embeddings (default: `embeddings.h5ad`). - `--batch-size INT`: Number of samples to process in each batch (default: 8). - `--gene-col-name NAME`: Column name in AnnData.var containing gene identifiers (default: `ensembl_id`). - `--precision {16-mixed,32}`: Numerical precision for inference (default: `16-mixed`). - `--pretrained-embedding PATH`: Path to pretrained embeddings for out-of-distribution species. - `--clip-counts INT`: Maximum count value (higher values will be clipped) (default: 30). - `--filter-to-vocabs`: Whether to filter genes to only those in the vocabulary (default: True). - `--use-raw {True,False,auto}`: Whether to use raw counts from `AnnData.raw.X` (True), `adata.X` (False), or auto-detect (auto/None) (default: None). - `--embedding-layer-index INT`: Index of the transformer layer to extract embeddings from (-1 for last layer, default: -1). Use with `transcriptformer` model type. - `--model-type {transcriptformer,esm2ce}`: Type of model to use (default: `transcriptformer`). Use `esm2ce` to extract raw ESM2-CE gene embeddings. - `--emb-type {cell,cge}`: Type of embeddings to extract (default: `cell`). Use `cell` for mean-pooled cell embeddings or `cge` for contextual gene embeddings. - `--num-gpus INT`: Number of GPUs to use for inference (default: 1). Use -1 for all available GPUs, or specify a specific number. - `--oom-dataloader`: Use the OOM-safe map-style DataLoader (uses backed reads and per-item densification; DistributedSampler-friendly). - `--n-data-workers INT`: Number of DataLoader workers per process (default: 0). Order is preserved with the map-style dataset and DistributedSampler. - `--device`: Specific device to use (`auto`, `cpu`, `cuda`, `mps`). `auto` (default) defualts to `cuda` falling back on `cpu`. - `--disable-compile-block-mask`: Disable block mask compilation (useful for CPU/debugging) - `--config-override key.path=value`: Override any configuration value directly. ### Input Data Format and Preprocessing: Input data files should be in H5AD format (AnnData objects) with the following requirements: - **Gene IDs**: The `var` dataframe must contain an `ensembl_id` column with Ensembl gene identifiers - Out-of-vocabulary gene IDs will be automatically filtered out during processing - Only genes present in the model's vocabulary will be used for inference - The column name can be changed using `model.data_config.gene_col_name` - **Expression Data**: The model expects unnormalized count data (raw counts) and will look for it in the following order: 1. `adata.raw.X` (if available) 2. `adata.X` This behavior can be controlled using `model.data_config.use_raw`: - `None` (default): Try `adata.raw.X` first, then fall back to `adata.X` - `True`: Use only `adata.raw.X` - `False`: Use only `adata.X` - **OOM-safe Data Loading**: - To reduce peak memory usage on large datasets, enable the OOM-safe dataloader: ```bash transcriptformer inference \ --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \ --data-file ./data/huge.h5ad \ --oom-dataloader \ --n-data-workers 4 \ --num-gpus 8 ``` - This uses a map-style dataset with backed reads and per-row densification. It is compatible with `DistributedSampler`, so multiple workers are safe and ordering is preserved. - **Count Processing**: - Count values are clipped at 30 by default (as was done in training) - If this seems too low, you can either: 1. Use `model.data_config.normalize_to_scale` to scale total counts to a specific value (e.g., 1e3-1e4) 2. Increase `model.data_config.clip_counts` to a value > 30 - **Cell Metadata**: Any cell metadata in the `obs` dataframe will be preserved in the output No other data preprocessing is necessary - the model handles all required transformations internally. You do not need to perform any additional normalization, scaling, or transformation of the count data before input. ### Output Format: The inference results will be saved to the specified output directory (default: `./inference_results`) in a file named `embeddings.h5ad`. This is an AnnData object where: **For cell embeddings (`--emb-type cell`, default):** - Cell embeddings are stored in `obsm['embeddings']` - Original cell metadata is preserved in the `obs` dataframe - Log-likelihood scores (if available) are stored in `uns['llh']` **For contextual gene embeddings (`--emb-type cge`):** - Contextual gene embeddings are stored in `uns['cge_embeddings']` as a 2D array (n_gene_instances, embedding_dim) - Cell indices for each gene embedding are stored in `uns['cge_cell_indices']` - Gene names for each embedding are stored in `uns['cge_gene_names']` - Original cell metadata is preserved in the `obs` dataframe - Log-likelihood scores (if available) are stored in `uns['llh']` #### Contextual Gene Embeddings (CGE) Contextual gene embeddings provide gene-specific representations that capture how each gene is contextualized within the cell sentence. Unlike cell embeddings which are mean-pooled across all genes, CGEs represent the individual embedding for each gene as computed by the transformer. Example usage: ```bash # Extract contextual gene embeddings transcriptformer inference \ --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \ --data-file test/data/human_val.h5ad \ --emb-type cge \ --output-filename cge_embeddings.h5ad ``` To access CGE data in Python: ```python import anndata as ad import numpy as np # Load the results adata = ad.read_h5ad("./inference_results/cge_embeddings.h5ad") # Access all contextual gene embeddings cge_embeddings = adata.uns['cge_embeddings'] # Shape: (n_gene_instances, embedding_dim) cell_indices = adata.uns['cge_cell_indices'] # Which cell each embedding belongs to gene_names = adata.uns['cge_gene_names'] # Gene name for each embedding # Get all gene embeddings for the first cell (cell index 0) cell_0_mask = cell_indices == 0 cell_0_embeddings = cge_embeddings[cell_0_mask] cell_0_genes = gene_names[cell_0_mask] # Get embedding for a specific gene in the first cell gene_mask = (cell_indices == 0) & (gene_names == 'ENSG00000000003') if np.any(gene_mask): gene_embedding = cge_embeddings[gene_mask][0] # Returns numpy array else: gene_embedding = None # Gene not found in this cell ``` For detailed configuration options, see the `src/transcriptformer/cli/conf/inference_config.yaml` file. ## Contributing This project adheres to the Contributor Covenant code of conduct. By participating, you are expected to uphold this code. Please report unacceptable behavior to opensource@chanzuckerberg.com. ## Reporting Security Issues Please note: If you believe you have found a security issue, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@chanzuckerberg.com. ## Citation If you use TranscriptFormer in your research, please cite: Pearce, J. D., et. al. (2025). A Cross-Species Generative Cell Atlas Across 1.5 Billion Years of Evolution: The TranscriptFormer Single-cell Model. bioRxiv. Retrieved April 29, 2025, from https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.25.650731v2

## 是什么

PerturbGen 是一个生成式基础模型，在超过 1 亿个单细胞转录组上训练，用于预测沿细胞轨迹的扰动响应。它解决了预测细胞如何随时间在状态之间转变以及扰动如何破坏这些转变的问题。该模型能够预测在源状态的遗传扰动如何塑造下游状态、改变基因程序并修改跨时间（例如分化或疾病进展）的轨迹。

## 亮点

- **大规模预训练**：在超过 1 亿个单细胞转录组上训练，具备强大的泛化能力。
- **动态轨迹预测**：不同于仅预测静态扰动响应的方法，PerturbGen 能预测沿细胞轨迹的扰动效应，捕捉早期扰动对后期状态的重新配置。
- **多功能下游应用**：支持三种应用：预测指定目标状态的基因表达、通过基因嵌入聚合识别上下文特异性基因程序、以及进行 in silico 扰动分析以构建扰动图谱（PIPs）。
- **工程化设计**：提供 Poetry 依赖管理、Docker 容器化、多 GPU 训练支持（DDP 和 DeepSpeed），以及离线 wandb 日志记录，便于复现和扩展。
- **预训练模型可用**：通过 Hugging Face 提供预训练 checkpoint，便于直接使用。

## 为何对本课题有用

PerturbGen 直接对齐本课题方向（虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型）。它提供了一个生成式基础模型的实例，专门用于单细胞转录组数据，并预测扰动下的细胞状态转变。对于构建虚拟细胞模型，PerturbGen 展示了如何利用大规模单细胞数据预训练模型，并如何将扰动预测整合到轨迹分析中。其基因程序发现和扰动图谱（PIPs）方法可迁移到虚拟器官建模中，用于识别关键调控因子和细胞状态转变的驱动因素。此外，其代码结构（如模块化组件、训练流程）可作为开发类似生物基座模型的参考。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：克隆仓库后，使用 Poetry 创建环境（Python 3.11），运行 `poetry install`。依赖文件为 `pyproject.toml` 和 `requirements.txt`。
- **主入口**：命令行入口为 `perturbgen`（通过 `perturbgen.__main__:main`），支持训练、验证等子命令（如 `train-mask`、`train-count`）。
- **示例**：提供 Jupyter notebook（转换为 `.py` 文件）用于预处理、tokenization、推理和扰动分析，位于 `docs/examples/`。
- **数据格式**：输入为单细胞转录组数据（如 scRNA-seq），通过预处理和 tokenization 转换为模型输入；输出为预测的基因表达、基因嵌入和扰动响应。
- **硬件要求**：预处理和推理可在 CPU 上运行（建议 ≥32 GB RAM），训练需要 CUDA GPU（默认 batch size 64 时峰值显存约 13.8-15.8 GB，建议 24 GB 以上 GPU）。
- **测试**：`perturbgen/tests/` 包含单元测试和基准测试，可用于调试。

## 核心 idea

PerturbGen 的核心创新在于将扰动预测与细胞轨迹动态结合，通过生成式模型学习细胞状态转变的潜在表示，从而能够预测早期扰动对后续状态的级联效应。其方法学价值在于：利用大规模单细胞数据预训练一个通用模型，并通过任务特定的微调（如掩码建模、计数解码）实现多种下游应用，这为生物基座模型的构建提供了可复用的范式。

## 可搬移点

- **tokenization 模块**（`perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py` 和 `GF_tokenisation.py`）：将单细胞转录组转换为 token 序列，可解耦并用于其他单细胞模型。
- **Transformer 架构**（`perturbgen/Modules/transformer.py`）：核心生成模型，可替换或扩展以适应不同数据模态。
- **训练流程**（`perturbgen/Model/trainer.py` 和 `perturbgen/Perturb/trainer.py`）：包含掩码模型和计数解码器的训练逻辑，可借鉴其多阶段训练策略。
- **扰动推理逻辑**（`perturbgen/Perturb/transformer.py` 和 `val.py`）：实现扰动预测和验证，可迁移到自定义 Pipeline。
- **许可证**：MIT 许可证，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认具体文件（如依赖的 T_perturb 包）的许可证。

注意：以上可搬移点基于仓库结构推断，具体实现细节需查看源码。

# PerturbGen foundation model for dynamic cellular states

![PerturbGen overview](docs/architecture.png)

A major challenge in biology is predicting how cells transition between states over time and how perturbations disrupt these transitions. Although recent approaches can predict single-cell perturbation responses in silico, they cannot predict responses across dynamic cell trajectories—for example, how early perturbations reconfigure later cell states. **PerturbGen** is a generative foundation model trained on over 100 million single-cell transcriptomes that predicts perturbation responses along cellular trajectories. It predicts how genetic perturbation at a source state shapes downstream states, alters gene programs, and modifies trajectories across time (e.g., in differentiation or disease progression).

**Applications:** This framework supports three downstream applications (Fig. 1b). First, PerturbGen predicts gene expression at specified target states, allowing inference of intermediate and future cell states. Second, learned gene embeddings can be aggregated across biological covariates, such as time, lineage, or developmental stage, to identify de novo, context-specific gene programs beyond predefined pathway annotations. Third, PerturbGen enables in silico perturbation analysis by simulating genetic interventions across cellular states. Scaling these simulations across genes yields perturbation atlases in which perturbations with similar transcriptional effects cluster together. We define these clusters as PIPs, which facilitate systematic identification of established regulators and discovery of previously unrecognized drivers of cell state transitions.

## 1. Usage

First, clone the repo and change to the project directory.

```shell
git clone https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/Perturbgen.git
```

Install Poetry (one-time):
(wanna know what is poetry? have a look at https://python-poetry.org)
```shell
curl -sSL https://install.python-poetry.org | python3 -
```
Optional: alternative way to install poetry using pipx (https://pipx.pypa.io/stable/how-to/install-pipx.html)
```shell
pip install poetry
```

Create/install the environment and dependencies:
```shell
cd Perturbgen
poetry env use python3.11
poetry install
```

Activate the enviroment
```shell
source "$(poetry env info -p)/bin/activate"
```

## Hardware requirements

Preprocessing, tokenization, and inference notebooks run on CPU (a machine with
≥32 GB RAM is recommended for the larger datasets).

**Training requires a CUDA GPU.** With the tutorial default batch size of 64, the
peak GPU memory measured over a full training epoch on the LPS tutorial data is:

| Training stage | Peak GPU memory (batch size 64) |
|----------------|---------------------------------|
| Masking model  | 13.8 GB                         |
| Count decoder  | 15.8 GB                         |

Training at the default batch size therefore runs on **24 GB GPUs** (e.g. RTX
3090/4090) and larger. On 16 GB GPUs the count-decoder stage is close to the memory
limit; if you hit an out-of-memory (OOM) error, lower the batch size via the
`--batch_size` flag (or `batch_size=` in the Python API).

To reproduce the paper results exactly, keep the default batch size of 64. The training code
automatically uses all visible GPUs (`devices=-1`); multi-GPU runs use
DDP by default and DeepSpeed (ZeRO stage 2) is available via
`--parallel_distribution deepspeed`, which also reduces per-GPU memory.

### Experiment logging (Weights & Biases)

Training/inference log to [Weights & Biases](https://wandb.ai). Logging is
**offline by default**, so runs never hang on wandb authentication on machines
without internet access; offline runs can be uploaded later with `wandb sync`.
To log online instead, use either:

```shell
export WANDB_MODE=online         # affects all runs in the shell
# or pass the flag per run:
python -m perturbgen train-mask ... --wandb_mode online
```

Use `--wandb_mode disabled` to turn logging off entirely. Set
`--wandb_entity <your-team>` (or `WANDB_ENTITY`) to log to your own wandb
account rather than the default.

The project contains some jupyter notebooks, which were converted to python files
due to better handling in the repository.
These files end with `_nb.py` and can be converted back to a `.ipynb` file with
`jupytext`:

```shell
jupytext --to ipynb --execute <your_file>_nb.py
```
## Examples

For usage, see the [documentation](https://perturbgen.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorial.html) or the local notebooks:
- [Preprocessing and data curation](docs/examples/preprocessing_curation.ipynb)
- [Cell and gene embeddings (released checkpoint)](docs/examples/cell_gene_embeddings.ipynb)
- [Gene program discovery](docs/examples/gene_program_discovery.ipynb)
- [Train and perturb (Python API, end to end: perturb at 6 h, predict 10 h)](docs/examples/train_and_perturb.ipynb)
- [Perturbation (released IL1B model)](docs/examples/perturbation.ipynb)
- [Post-perturbation analyses](docs/examples/post_perturbation_analyses.ipynb)

See the Perturbation notebook for more explanation about how to perturb a gene or list of genes

## Documentation

Full documentation and tutorials are available at: [perturbgen.readthedocs.io](https://perturbgen.readthedocs.io/)

## Pretrained Checkpoints

The pretrained model checkpoint is available via Hugging Face:

👉 https://huggingface.co/lotfollahi-lab/PerturbGen/tree/main

⚠️ Note: The checkpoint in `pretraining_cohort/` is stored using Git LFS, and due to bandwidth limits, `git lfs pull` may fail with a 403 error.  
Please use the Hugging Face link above instead, and save the downloaded `.ckpt` file in `pretraining_cohort/` (keeping its file name): that is where training looks for the encoder by default, so no `--encoder_path` is needed.

## 是什么

ImmuneWorld 是一个单细胞 RNA 测序（scRNA-seq）基础模型，旨在模拟肿瘤免疫微环境的演化过程，并将其建模为自回归的细胞状态转移。该模型主要用于预测泛癌免疫治疗反应，同时支持扰动预测、轨迹推断、去卷积和免疫治疗响应评估等任务。它通过连续伪时间编码、轨迹感知注意力、癌症不变迁移、扰动条件生成、掩码基因重建和队列留出法响应建模等机制，实现对肿瘤免疫微环境动态演化的建模。

## 亮点

- **自回归细胞状态转移建模**：将细胞状态演化视为自回归过程，结合连续伪时间编码和轨迹感知注意力，能够捕捉细胞状态的时间动态。
- **多任务联合训练**：训练目标包括轨迹均方误差、掩码基因二元交叉熵和扰动结果误差，并采用梯度反转实现癌症域不变性，提升跨癌种泛化能力。
- **大规模预训练语料**：整合了 5.2M Human Cell Atlas 细胞、4.8M 肿瘤浸润免疫细胞（CELLxGENE）和 2.4M GEO Perturb-seq 细胞，总计 12.4M 细胞，覆盖 2,000 个高变基因词汇表。
- **高性能计算配置**：使用 12 层 Transformer、8 头注意力、每头学习时间衰减、SwiGLU 块，在 4×A100 80GB 上训练，约 72 小时完成，支持多 GPU 分布式训练。
- **全面的评估体系**：提供扰动（Pearson 相关）、轨迹（跨边界方向、动态时间规整）、去卷积（宏 F1）和免疫治疗（留一队列 ROC AUC）等评估指标，并报告了多种子统计结果。

## 为何对本课题有用

ImmuneWorld 直接属于「虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型」方向，其核心贡献在于：
- **模拟肿瘤免疫微环境演化**：通过自回归细胞状态转移，能够模拟免疫细胞在肿瘤微环境中的动态变化，为虚拟器官建模提供细胞级动态视角。
- **泛癌免疫治疗响应预测**：采用留一队列交叉验证，预测免疫治疗响应，为生物基座模型在临床预测任务中的应用提供范例。
- **可迁移的建模思路**：其连续伪时间编码、轨迹感知注意力、癌症不变迁移和扰动条件生成等机制，可迁移至其他单细胞/空间组学基础模型的构建，例如用于空间转录组的细胞状态演化建模。
- **多任务学习框架**：联合优化轨迹、基因重建和扰动预测，展示了如何将多种生物信息学任务整合进单一基础模型，对构建多功能生物大语言模型具有参考价值。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：训练命令为 `torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 -m immuneworld.commands.train --settings settings/pretraining.yaml`，入口脚本为 `code/immuneworld/commands/train.py`。
- **安装与依赖**：使用 `conda env create -f environment.yml` 创建环境，依赖包括 Python 3.10.8、PyTorch 1.13.1、CUDA 11.7、scanpy 1.9.1、scVelo 0.2.5 等；也可通过 Dockerfile 构建容器（基于 NVIDIA PyTorch 22.12 镜像）。
- **数据准备**：公共数据位置在 `datasets.txt` 中列出，预训练语料包括 HCA、CELLxGENE 和 GEO Perturb-seq 数据，需选择 2,000 个高变基因并归一化。
- **输入输出格式**：输入为单细胞表达矩阵（如 AnnData 格式），输出为细胞状态预测、扰动响应、轨迹和免疫治疗响应概率。
- **GPU 需求**：需要 4×A100 80GB GPU，约 288 GPU-hours，存储需求至少 3TB。
- **调试与评估**：评估模块位于 `code/immuneworld/assessment/`，包含 `metrics.py` 和 `streaming.py`，可用于计算扰动、轨迹、去卷积和免疫治疗指标；README 未提供具体单元测试，但可通过运行评估命令进行验证。

## 核心 idea

ImmuneWorld 的核心方法学洞察在于：将细胞状态演化建模为自回归的序列生成问题，通过连续伪时间编码和轨迹感知注意力，使模型能够学习细胞状态的时间依赖关系，并利用癌症不变迁移和扰动条件生成，实现跨癌种和扰动条件下的泛化预测。这种将时间动态显式编码进 Transformer 架构的方式，是其在免疫治疗响应预测中取得高 AUC（0.891）的关键。

## 可搬移点

- **连续伪时间编码模块**（`code/immuneworld/dynamics/temporal.py`）：该模块实现了时间衰减和伪时间编码，可解耦后用于其他单细胞轨迹建模或空间组学的时间动态分析。
- **轨迹感知注意力机制**（`code/immuneworld/dynamics/context.py`）：注意力机制中的轨迹感知部分可迁移至自定义的 Transformer 架构，用于增强对细胞状态序列的建模。
- **癌症不变迁移模块**（`code/immuneworld/dynamics/transfer.py`）：梯度反转实现域不变性的逻辑，可复用于跨数据集或跨癌种的泛化任务。
- **多任务损失函数**（`code/immuneworld/learning/objectives.py`）：联合优化轨迹 MSE、掩码基因 BCE 和扰动误差的损失组合，可借鉴用于设计多任务生物基础模型的训练目标。
- **数据流式处理**（`code/immuneworld/ingest/`）：数据加载和分割逻辑（如按扰动身份 80/10/10 分割、留一队列分割）可复用，确保评估的严谨性。
- **许可证**：README 未明确许可证，需确认。
readme:
# A single-cell RNA-sequencing foundation model simulates tumour immune microenvironment evolution to predict pan-cancer immunotherapy response

ImmuneWorld models tumour immune microenvironment evolution as autoregressive cell-state transitions. The release contains continuous pseudotime encoding, trajectory-aware attention, cancer-invariant transfer, perturbation-conditioned rollouts, masked-gene reconstruction, cohort-held-out response modelling, and the evaluation measures used for perturbation, trajectory, deconvolution, and immunotherapy tasks.

## Environment

The reference environment uses Python 3.10.8, PyTorch 1.13.1, CUDA 11.7, scanpy 1.9.1, and scVelo 0.2.5. The pinned stack targets the four-node accelerator configuration used for the main training run.

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate immuneworld
pip install --no-deps -e .
```

The container uses the NVIDIA PyTorch 22.12 image.

```bash
docker build -t immuneworld:1.0 .
```

## Data preparation

Public data locations are listed in `datasets.txt`. The pretraining corpus combines 5.2 million Human Cell Atlas cells, 4.8 million tumour-infiltrating immune cells from CELLxGENE, and 2.4 million GEO Perturb-seq cells. Norman, Adamson, Replogle K562, and Replogle RPE1 are excluded from the pretraining GEO subset. Training-only statistics select 2,000 highly variable genes and normalize every held-out partition without refitting.

Perturbation benchmarks use an 80/10/10 split by perturbation identity. Immunotherapy prediction uses leave-one-cohort-out folds across 14 cohorts and seven cancer types. Patient identifiers must not cross fold boundaries. Trajectory analysis uses the Pancreas, Dentate Gyrus, and Bone Marrow datasets distributed with scVelo.

## Training

The reference run uses 12 transformer layers, eight attention heads, a per-head learned temporal decay, SwiGLU blocks, batch size 128 per accelerator, four A100 80GB accelerators, and an effective batch size of 512. AdamW begins at `1e-4`, warms up for 5,000 steps, and follows cosine decay to `1e-6` for 200 epochs. The run takes approximately 72 hours and 288 GPU-hours. Three independent runs use seeds 42, 123, and 456.

```bash
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 -m immuneworld.commands.train --settings settings/pretraining.yaml
```

The objective is trajectory mean squared error plus masked-gene binary cross entropy and perturbation outcome error with weights 1.0, 0.5, and 0.3. Cancer-domain discrimination uses gradient reversal with weight 0.1.

## Evaluation

Perturbation reporting uses Pearson correlation for Norman, Adamson, K562, and RPE1. Trajectory reporting uses cross-boundary direction and dynamic time warping averaged over Pancreas, Dentate Gyrus, and Bone Marrow. Deconvolution reports macro F1 over eight immune populations. Immunotherapy evaluation reports leave-one-cohort-out ROC AUC with cohort and cancer summaries.

The reference aggregate results are Norman Pearson correlation `0.914 ± 0.008`, trajectory cross-boundary direction `0.881`, trajectory dynamic time warping `1.387`, deconvolution F1 `0.730 ± 0.019`, and immunotherapy response AUC `0.891 ± 0.014` over three seeds.

## Compute budget

The pretraining corpus contains 12.4 million cells represented over a 2,000-gene vocabulary. A complete run requires four A100 accelerators with 80GB memory each, approximately 72 wall-clock hours, and 288 GPU-hours. Data staging, normalized matrices, fold materialization, optimizer state, and run outputs require at least 3TB of local storage.

## 是什么

ODT (Organismal Digital Twin) 是一个面向涡虫再生的单细胞分辨率的时空基础模型框架。它通过五个顺序连接的阶段——自监督预训练、时空微调、再生基因发现、基因调控网络推断和虚拟切片重建——构建了涡虫的数字化孪生，用于发现再生调控基因。

## 亮点

- **端到端多阶段流水线**：从无标注 scRNA-seq 预训练到 3D 细胞类型注释、基因发现、GRN 推断和虚拟切片生成，形成完整的生物数字孪生闭环。
- **跨物种验证**：通过 BLAST 同源比对和系统发育谱系分析，增强基因发现的生物学可信度。
- **可复现的教程驱动**：提供 5 个 Jupyter Notebook 教程，覆盖从模型构建到可视化的每一步，便于复现和二次开发。
- **模块化代码结构**：`src/` 下按功能拆分（train, models, tools, visualize 等），便于局部替换和扩展。

## 为何对本课题有用

ODT 正是「虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型」方向的直接范例。它展示了如何将通用单细胞基础模型（Geneformer）适配到特定器官（涡虫）的时空动态，并进一步驱动下游任务（基因发现、GRN、虚拟切片）。其方法论可直接迁移到其他再生模型或虚拟器官构建，尤其是：
- 时空微调策略（PFM-ST）可借鉴用于整合空间转录组与时间序列数据。
- 扩散模型虚拟切片（SquiDiff）为缺失时间点的数据补全提供了生成式方案。
- SVM+跨物种验证的基因发现流程可复用于其他物种的调控基因筛选。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：`source/Tutorial 1-5.ipynb` 是主要入口，按顺序运行即可复现整个流程。
- **安装**：
  ```bash
  conda create -n ODT_main python=3.9
  conda activate ODT_main
  git clone --branch pr146_branch https://huggingface.co/ctheodoris/Geneformer
  cd Geneformer && pip install -e .
  cd /path/to/ODT-main && pip install -r requirements.txt
  ```
- **数据**：从 Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.21212543) 下载数据集，从 (10.5281/zenodo.21618496) 下载模型权重和 SquiDiff 结果（需 7-Zip 解压多卷压缩包）。
- **运行**：在 `tutorials` 目录下运行 Notebook，或访问在线文档 https://odt-main.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ 。
- **输入/输出**：输入为 scRNA-seq 和空间转录组数据（格式未在 README 中明确，但基于 Geneformer 应为 h5ad 或类似格式）；输出包括 3D 细胞类型注释、基因候选列表、GRN 边列表、虚拟切片表达谱。
- **GPU**：需要 GPU 加速（训练和推理均涉及深度学习模型）。

## 核心 idea

ODT 的核心方法学在于将基础模型（Geneformer）的上下文基因嵌入作为统一表示，通过时空微调注入空间和时间信息，从而让同一个嵌入空间同时支持基因发现、GRN 推断和生成式虚拟切片，实现了从静态单细胞图谱到动态器官数字孪生的跨越。

## 可搬移点

- **PFM-ST 双分支架构**（基因图注意力 + 动态空间查询）可解耦出来，用于其他空间组学数据的细胞类型注释。
- **SquiDiff 条件扩散模型**：其时间轨迹学习逻辑可独立移植，用于生成任意时间点的虚拟表达谱。
- **SVM + 跨物种验证流程**：可作为一个独立模块，用于任何基因筛选任务。
- **GRN 推断 MLP**：可替换为其他网络结构，但输入特征（基因嵌入 + 扰动响应）的设计思路可复用。
- **License**：README 未明确说明，需确认。

# ODT  ·  Organismal Digital Twin

Spatiotemporal foundation model-guided organismal digital twin for
regeneration-regulatory gene discovery in planarians.

---

## Overview

ODT models planarian regeneration at single-cell resolution through five
sequentially connected stages: self-supervised pretraining on unlabelled
scRNA-seq data, spatial-temporal fine-tuning for 3D cell-type annotation,
SVM-based regeneration gene discovery with cross-species BLAST validation,
MLP-driven gene regulatory network inference, and diffusion-model-based
virtual section reconstruction at unobserved timepoints.

---

## Workflow

**1.   Geneformer Pretraining**
  Masked-language-model pretraining on planarian single-cell transcriptomes
using the Geneformer framework. The resulting foundation model (PFM) learns
contextualised gene embeddings that generalise across downstream tasks.

**2.   PFM-T · Regeneration Gene Discovery**
  Gene embeddings extracted from the fine-tuned model are classified via
SVM with leave-one-out cross-validation, using experimentally validated
positive and negative gene sets as anchors. Predicted regeneration candidates
are then queried against the NCBI protein database via BLAST, and the
resulting homologues are mapped to taxonomic clades for phylogenetic profiling
and knowledge graph assembly.

**3.   PFM-ST · 3D Cell-Type Annotation**
  Spatial-temporal enhancement of the pretrained model with a
dual-branch architecture — gene graph attention coupled with dynamic spatial
query — trained on 2D spatial transcriptomics slices. Three-replicate ensemble
prediction with soft-voting is applied to 3D whole-mount planarian data across
seven regeneration timepoints, producing DBSCAN-denoised, publication-quality
3D renderings of nine cell types with eyespot landmark overlay.

**4.   GRN · Regulatory Network Construction**
  A three-hidden-layer MLP trained on concatenated gene embedding and
perturbation response vectors predicts pairwise regulatory relationships on a
seven-class ordinal scale from strong inhibition to strong activation.
Exhaustive scoring of all ~8.6 million gene pairs identifies high-confidence
directed edges for downstream network analysis and visualisation.

**5.   SquiDiff · Virtual Section Reconstruction**
  A conditional diffusion model learns the temporal trajectory of
transcriptional programmes in latent space. By encoding real cells and
decoding along a learned temporal direction, SquiDiff generates plausible
gene expression profiles at unobserved intermediate timepoints. The resulting
raw and simulated latent spaces are interrogated through t-SNE and diffusion
pseudotime projections, pairwise cell-type distance dynamics, river plots,
and dynamic network graphs.

---
## Installation

```
bash
# 1. Create and activate the conda environment
conda create -n ODT_main python=3.9
conda activate ODT_main

# 2. Clone the specified branch of Geneformer and install it
git clone --branch pr146_branch https://huggingface.co/ctheodoris/Geneformer
cd Geneformer
pip install -e .

# 3. Return to the project root directory (e.g., /home/wwd/ODT-main)
# Before running the scripts, replace the `CODE_PATH` variable in the first code block
# of each script with the absolute path to your local project directory.
cd /home/wwd/ODT-main   # Replace with your actual project path

# 4. Install the remaining dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Results

## 是什么

HEBI 是一个**层次化图基础模型 (hierarchical graph foundation model)**，专门用于**空间转录组学 (spatial transcriptomics)** 数据的分析。它能够在单次前向传播中，无需任何细胞类型或生态位 (niche) 注释，同时学习组织切片在**细胞 (cell)、原型 (prototype) 和生态位 (niche)** 三个层次上的表征。该模型在来自三个商业平台、包含 2300 万个细胞的 80 个成像切片上进行了预训练，并可通过零样本 (zero-shot) 或短期的持续适应 (continual adaptation) 迁移到未见过的切片。

## 亮点

*   **层次化表征学习**：通过一个统一的编码器，同时输出细胞级 (z0)、社区级 (z1) 和生态位级 (z2) 的嵌入，避免了为不同任务训练多个模型。
*   **直接读取生态位**：生态位 (niche) 的分配直接来自模型注意力层的 argmax，而非事后对嵌入进行聚类，这使得不同切片和平台间的生态位标签具有可比性，无需额外的批次校正步骤。
*   **强大的预训练与迁移能力**：在跨平台的大规模数据上预训练，支持零样本推理和持续适应两种模式，能快速适配新数据。
*   **多功能集成**：内置了基因调控网络 (GRN) 分析、细胞间通讯 (CCC) 评分和受监督的生态位预测等高级功能，使其成为一个全面的分析工具。
*   **工程化良好**：提供了清晰的命令行接口 (CLI) 和 Python API，支持分阶段运行，方便用户灵活探索不同的聚类和生态位分配设置。

## 为何对本课题有用

HEBI 与「虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型」课题**高度对齐**，是构建虚拟细胞/器官模型的核心组件。

*   **作为空间组学基座模型**：HEBI 本身就是一种生物基座模型，其预训练-微调/零样本迁移的范式，为构建更广泛的虚拟细胞模型提供了直接可用的架构和权重。
*   **提供多尺度表征**：其输出的细胞、社区、生态位三个层次的表征，是构建虚拟器官所必需的“零件”，可用于理解组织微环境、细胞间通讯和器官功能。
*   **支持下游任务**：其内置的 GRN 分析和 CCC 评分功能，为虚拟细胞模型提供了关键的“功能”维度，使其不仅能描述“是什么”，还能预测“如何工作”。
*   **可迁移的架构思路**：其层次化图神经网络 (Hierarchical GNN) 的设计，对于处理其他类型的生物组学数据（如多组学、时间序列）具有重要的借鉴意义。

## 怎么用

**主入口与运行命令**：

*   **预处理**：`hebi-preprocess --h5ad_dir <dir> --out_root <dir> --vocab_path <path> --k 5`
*   **推理**：`hebi-run --checkpoint_path <path> --data_dir <dir> --section_files <files> --h5ad_files <files> --vocab_path <path> --mode zero_shot`
*   **预训练**：`hebi-pretrain --config configs/pretrain.yaml`

**安装与依赖**：

*   依赖文件：`environment.yml` (conda) 和 `pyproject.toml` (pip)。
*   核心依赖：Python 3.11+, PyTorch 2.6.0, `torch_sparse`, `torch-geometric`, `scanpy`, `anndata`。
*   安装步骤：先安装 PyTorch 和 `torch_sparse`（需匹配 CUDA 版本），再通过 `pip install -e .` 安装 HEBI。

**输入/输出数据格式**：

*   **输入**：`.h5ad` 文件（AnnData 格式），包含基因表达矩阵和空间坐标。
*   **输出**：
    *   内存中的 AnnData 对象，包含 `adata.obsm['z0']`, `adata.obsm['z1']`, `adata.obsm['z2']` 三个嵌入矩阵。
    *   `adata.obs['prototypes']` 列，包含直接来自注意力的生态位分配。
    *   可选输出：聚类结果、生态位图、GRN 报告等。

**调试与示例**：

*   仓库提供了 Jupyter Notebooks（如 `notebooks/01_single_section_breast_cancer.ipynb`）用于复现论文中的分析，是理想的调试入口。
*   Python API 支持分阶段运行（`encode_sections`, `cluster_sections`, `assign_niches`），便于逐步调试。

## 核心 idea

HEBI 的核心洞察在于**通过一个层次化的图神经网络，将组织切片的表征学习与生态位的“可读”发现过程统一起来**。它不依赖于事后的嵌入聚类，而是将生态位定义为模型注意力机制的直接产物，从而实现了跨样本、跨平台的可比性，并避免了繁琐的批次校正。

## 可搬移点

*   **层次化编码器架构**：`hebi/model/` 目录下的 `hebi.py`, `hdse_hierarchy.py`, `hdse_level1.py` 等文件定义了核心的层次化图神经网络。其“细胞-原型-生态位”的层级设计思路，以及如何通过注意力机制直接输出生态位分配的逻辑，是**最值得解耦和移植**的核心模块。
*   **数据预处理流程**：`hebi/data/preprocess.py` 和 `hebi/data/graph.py` 中的空间 kNN 图构建、METIS 分区和归一化检测逻辑，可以独立提取出来，用于构建自定义的空间组学数据处理 Pipeline。
*   **推理 Pipeline**：`hebi/inference/pipeline.py` 中的 `encode_sections`, `cluster_sections`, `assign_niches` 函数设计清晰，可以逐步替换其中的聚类方法或生态位分配策略，以适配不同的下游任务。
*   **License**: MIT，允许自由使用、修改和分发，**可以放心移植**。

**注意**：README 未说明具体的模型参数量、训练细节（如损失函数权重）和硬件需求，这些信息可能需要查阅论文或源码进一步确认。

# HEBI **A hierarchical graph foundation model for spatial transcriptomics.** HEBI learns cell, prototype, and niche level representations of a tissue section in a single forward pass, without cell type or niche annotations. It is pretrained on 80 imaging-based sections spanning three commercial platforms and 23 million cells, and transfers to unseen sections either zero-shot or after a short continual adaptation.

Niches are read directly from the model's attention rather than by clustering an embedding afterwards, so niche labels are comparable across replicate sections and across platforms without a separate batch correction step. --- ## Installation HEBI needs Python 3.11+, PyTorch and `torch_sparse`. Both are built per CUDA version, so they are installed first, then the package. The commands below use PyTorch 2.6.0 with CUDA 12.4, the versions HEBI was developed with. For another CUDA version, or CPU only, change `cu124` in both URLs (e.g. `cu118`, `cu126`, `cpu`); see [pytorch.org](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/) and the [PyG install guide](https://pytorch-geometric.readthedocs.io/en/latest/install/installation.html). ### conda / mamba `environment.yml` installs PyTorch and `torch_sparse` through pip, since PyTorch is no longer published on its conda channel after 2.5. ```bash git clone https://github.com/roxana9/hebi.git cd hebi mamba env create -f environment.yml mamba activate hebi pip install -e . ``` ### pip ```bash # 1. PyTorch, matching your CUDA version pip install torch==2.6.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124 # 2. torch_sparse, a prebuilt wheel matching that PyTorch + CUDA build pip install torch_sparse -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-2.6.0+cu124.html # 3. HEBI git clone https://github.com/roxana9/hebi.git cd hebi pip install -e . ``` If `torch_sparse` starts compiling from source, the `torch-X+cuY` part of the `-f` URL does not match the installed PyTorch. Check it with `python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__)"`. Optional clustering backends: ```bash pip install -e ".[leiden]" # --cluster_method leiden pip install -e ".[mclust]" # --cluster_method mclust, also needs R + mclust ``` Check the install: ```bash hebi-run --help ``` --- ## Pretrained weights The pretrained checkpoint and the gene vocabulary are on Hugging Face: [huggingface.co/Roxana9/hebi](https://huggingface.co/Roxana9/hebi) | file | content | | --- | --- | | `hebi_hybrid_oldL0.pt` | pretrained HEBI weights | | `default_gene_vocab.json` | gene vocabulary used for pretraining | Download with the Hugging Face CLI: ```bash pip install -U huggingface_hub hf download Roxana9/hebi --local-dir weights/ ``` or from Python: ```python from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download ckpt = hf_hub_download("Roxana9/hebi", "hebi_hybrid_oldL0.pt") vocab = hf_hub_download("Roxana9/hebi", "default_gene_vocab.json") ``` Then pass them to `hebi-run`: ```bash hebi-run --checkpoint_path weights/hebi_hybrid_oldL0.pt \ --vocab_path weights/default_gene_vocab.json ... ``` Without a checkpoint, `--init random` trains from scratch on your own sections. --- ## Quick start Three steps: preprocess sections, run inference, read the outputs. ### 1. Preprocess Turns each `.h5ad` into a `.pt` section holding the expression matrix, the spatial kNN graph, and the METIS partition. ```bash hebi-preprocess \ --h5ad_dir data/my_sections/ \ --out_root processed/ \ --vocab_path default_gene_vocab.json \ --k 5 ``` `--k` is the spatial neighbourhood size and should suit the cell density of your data. The value used is recorded in each `.pt`. Normalisation is detected, not assumed. `log1p` is applied when the matrix is not already in log space; library-size normalisation is separate and opt-in via `--normalise`. The detected status is printed and stored, so a section's space is always recoverable. ### 2. Run ```bash hebi-run \ --checkpoint_path hebi_foundation.pt \ --data_dir processed/ \ --section_files section_1.pt section_2.pt \ --h5ad_files data/my_sections/section_1.h5ad data/my_sections/section_2.h5ad \ --vocab_path default_gene_vocab.json \ --mode zero_shot \ --init pretrained \ --n_cell_clusters 18 \ --cluster_method kmeans \ --seed 2025 \ --point_size 2 \ --output_dir results/ ``` Or put the same settings in a YAML file: ```bash hebi-run --config configs/starmap.yaml ``` ### 3. Outputs HEBI produces cell-level embeddings and niche assignments directly from its hierarchical encoder. Cell clusters are obtained by clustering the Level-0 embeddings, whereas niche assignments are derived directly from Level-2 attention without post-hoc clustering. **Generated figures** When plotting is enabled, `--output_dir` contains: ```text results/ └── z0_kmeans_18.* # Joint cell-level clustering across sections ``` The number in the filename corresponds to `--n_cell_clusters`. Prototype assignments are available directly from the model but are not yet plotted automatically by the CLI. **AnnData representations** For each section, the following results are available in memory: | Location | Key | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `adata.obs` | `prototypes` | Learned Level-2 niche assignments, obtained directly from the attention argmax | | `adata.obs` | `z0_kmeans_18` | Cell clusters obtained by jointly clustering Level-0 embeddings across sections | | `adata.obsm` | `z0` | Cell-level representations | | `adata.obsm` | `z1` | Community-contextualised cell representations | | `adata.obsm` | `z2` | Niche-level cell representations | The number of cell clusters is configurable through `--n_cell_clusters`. The number of learned niche prototypes is defined by the model architecture and checkpoint, not by the clustering parameters. **Note:** The current CLI does not automatically export the resulting AnnData objects as `.h5ad` files. ## Python API HEBI can be run through a single function or as separate stages, allowing users to explore different cell-clustering and niche-assignment settings without repeating model inference. ### Option 1: Complete pipeline ```python from hebi.inference.pipeline import run_hebi sections, ctx = run_hebi( checkpoint_path="hebi_foundation.pt", data_dir="processed/", section_files=["section_1.pt", "section_2.pt"], h5ad_files=["section_1.h5ad", "section_2.h5ad"], vocab_path="default_gene_vocab.json", mode="zero_shot", init="pretrained", n_cell_clusters=16, seed=2025, output_dir="results/", ) ``` ### Option 2: Run each stage separately **Step 1. Encode sections** ```python from pathlib import Path from hebi.inference.pipeline import encode_sections PROCESSED_DIR = Path("processed/") RESULTS_DIR = Path("results/") SECTION_FILES = ["section_1.pt", "section_2.pt"] SECTION_NAMES = ["Xenium", "MERSCOPE"] sections, ctx = encode_sections( checkpoint_path="hebi_foundation.pt", data_dir=str(PROCESSED_DIR), section_files=SECTION_FILES, h5ad_files=["section_1.h5ad", "section_2.h5ad"], vocab_path="default_gene_vocab.json", section_labels=SECTION_NAMES, mode="zero_shot", init="pretrained", grn=False, seed=2025, output_dir=str(RESULTS_DIR), ) ``` This stage generates three representations (`z0`, `z1` and `z2`) and the learned Level-2 prototype assignments. **Step 2. Cluster cell-level representations** ```python from hebi.inference.pipeline import cluster_sections written = cluster_sections( sections, ctx, n_cell_clusters=16, cluster_method="kmeans", ) ``` Cell clusters are obtained by jointly clustering Level-0 embeddings across sections. **Step 3. Assign and visualise niches** To obtain a user-specified number of spatial niches from the learned prototypes: ```python from hebi.inference.niches import assign_niches, plot_niches n_niches = 7 assign_niches( sections, ctx, PROCESSED_DIR, SECTION_FILES, n_niches=n_niches, section_names=SECTION_NAMES, cache_dir=RESULTS_DIR, ) plot_niches( sections, n_niches, SECTION_NAMES, out=RESULTS_DIR / "niches", ) ``` The model's Level-2 prototype assignments are obtained directly during the forward pass. The optional `assign_niches` step produces a user-defined number of niches without requiring the encoding stage to be repeated. **Accessing the learned representations** ```python from hebi.inference.cluster import KEY_PROTOTYPES adata = sections[0] cell_embeddings = adata.obsm["z0"] community_embeddings = adata.obsm["z1"] niche_embeddings = adata.obsm["z2"] # Direct Level-2 prototype assignments prototypes = adata.obs[KEY_PROTOTYPES] ``` The number of learned Level-2 prototypes is defined by the model architecture and checkpoint. The `n_niches` argument controls the requested number of niches in the subsequent assignment step. --- ## What else it does **Zero-shot or continual.** `--mode zero_shot` encodes with frozen weights; `--mode continual` adapts to the target sections first with the same self-supervised objective. **Gene regulatory networks.** `--grn` builds a heterogeneous gene-interaction graph from curated priors and co-expression, and learns an attention over it. Gives hub genes, edge salience, and niche-level regulatory activity. **Cell-cell communication.** `--grn_ccc` scores ligand-receptor communication between niches and writes a chord diagram plus the full interaction table. **Supervised niche prediction.** A linear head on the cell-level representation, trained by linear probing and optional fine-tuning, with sections held out whole so reported performance reflects generalisation to unseen sections. --- ## Pretraining To pretrain from scratch on your own corpus: ```bash hebi-pretrain --config configs/pretrain.yaml ``` The config carries the architecture, the optimisation settings, and the weights of the seven self-supervised loss terms. --- ## Documentation The Jupyter notebooks used to reproduce each analysis presented in the manuscript are available in the [`notebooks/`](notebooks/) directory. --- ## Citation Manuscript in preparation. --- ## Licence MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
