# Fine-tuning Geneformer and scGPT on readily-available GPUs Fine-tuning single-cell foundation models is usually performed on top-of-the-line GPUs such as the NVIDIA A100. Those are not just expensive: they are also hard to get. A100 instances are often capacity-constrained, so a job can wait for one, or fail to get one at all. This repo shows how to fine-tune these models on the **NVIDIA A10G and T4** instead: GPUs that cost far less and that you can usually get straight away (`ml.g5.xlarge` and `ml.g4dn.xlarge` on SageMaker). Every result below was trained on one of those two: Geneformer V1-10M and scGPT on a T4, Geneformer V2-104M on an A10G. Only the largest preset, Geneformer V2-316M, needs an A100 at full precision, and with 4-bit QLoRA it fits on an A10G too (see [QLoRA batch-size sweep](#qlora-batch-size-sweep-a10g-24-gb); that path is experimental). This project is a standalone system for fine-tuning on your own labeled scRNA-seq data, with **two backends**, selected by one config field: - **[Geneformer](https://huggingface.co/ctheodoris/Geneformer)**: a transformer pretrained on single-cell transcriptomes, using rank-value encoding. - **[scGPT](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scGPT)**: a generative pretrained transformer for single-cell data, using gene-vocab value binning. Both are used for **cell state classification** (e.g. cell-type annotation, disease classification). Geneformer also supports **gene classification**. The repo wraps each model's maintained training code behind one small, config-driven CLI, `scfm-ft` (**s**ingle-**c**ell **f**oundation **m**odel **f**ine-**t**uning; the Python package is `scfm_ft`), so you can go from an AnnData `.h5ad` (or `.loom`) file to a fine-tuned model + evaluation plots with one command per stage. The same `training` block and the same held-out metrics (`accuracy`, `macro_f1`) apply to both backends, so Geneformer and scGPT results on the same dataset are directly comparable. It also ships a ready-to-run **AWS pipeline** (CodeBuild → ECR → SageMaker) for training on a real GPU without a local GPU. See [Backends (Geneformer + scGPT)](#backends-geneformer--scgpt). **Results on the PBMC3k example** (cell-type classification, held-out cells): | Backend | Model | GPU | Accuracy | Macro-F1 | Evaluation | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Geneformer | V1-10M | T4 | 0.955 | 0.87 | single 80/10/10 split | | Geneformer | V2-104M | A10G | 0.96–0.97 | 0.94–0.95 | single 80/10/10 split | | scGPT | `scgpt-human` | T4 | 0.933 ± 0.012 | 0.889 ± 0.033 | 5-fold cross-validation, 4 seeds | Details: [Remote training on AWS](#remote-training-on-aws) and [scGPT backend](#scgpt-backend--remote-training). ## What it does ``` .h5ad / .loom ──tokenize──▶ tokenized dataset ──finetune──▶ fine-tuned model (Geneformer or scGPT, per model.backend) │ └──evaluate──▶ metrics + confusion matrix + UMAP ``` Three stages, each a CLI subcommand driven by one YAML config: | Stage | Command | Output | |-------------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------| | Tokenize | `scfm-ft tokenize` | tokenized dataset (Geneformer rank-value / scGPT value-binned) | | Fine-tune | `scfm-ft finetune` | fine-tuned model + class-label map | | Evaluate | `scfm-ft evaluate` | metrics JSON, confusion matrix, predictions | Or run the whole thing: `scfm-ft run --config configs/example_cell.yaml`. ### All CLI subcommands | Command | What it does | |--------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------| | `tokenize` | `.h5ad`/`.loom` → tokenized dataset for the configured backend | | `finetune` | Fine-tune the configured model (runs `tokenize` first if needed) | | `evaluate` | Evaluate a fine-tuned model, write metrics + plots | | `run` | `tokenize` → `finetune` → `evaluate` end to end | | `make-sample-data` | Write a tiny synthetic dataset for CPU smoke tests | | `load-pbmc3k` | Download the real 10x PBMC3k dataset and format it as a loom | | `validate-config` | Parse a config and print the resolved settings | ## How it works - **Config-driven.** Every run is described by one YAML file validated into a typed `Config` (`src/scfm_ft/config.py`). This is the single source of truth for the model preset, input path, label column, and training hyperparameters. - **Tokenize** turns an AnnData/loom matrix into the input the chosen model expects. Geneformer ranks each gene's expression within the cell (rank-value encoding), so the model sees "which genes are most active in this cell" rather than raw counts. scGPT maps genes to its vocabulary and bins their expression values. - **Fine-tune** attaches a classification head and trains it on your labels. Geneformer runs through its maintained `Classifier` API; scGPT runs through its own `TransformerModel`. `training.num_crossval_splits` chooses train-only (`0`), a single held-out split (`1`), or 5-fold cross-validation (`5`). - **Evaluate** renders the held-out metrics, confusion matrix and prediction dump. When `num_crossval_splits >= 1`, finetune has already evaluated on held-out cells and evaluate just renders those results. - **Model selection by preset.** `model.backend` picks Geneformer or scGPT, and `model.preset` picks the pretrained checkpoint. Geneformer weights live under `vendor/Geneformer/` locally or are baked into the training image; scGPT weights are staged in S3 and mounted into the job. ## Models ### Geneformer presets | Preset | Model | Params | Input size | Corpus | |-----------|--------------------|--------|------------|------------------------| | `V1-10M` | Geneformer-V1-10M | 10M | 2048 | ~30M cells | | `V2-104M` | Geneformer-V2-104M | 104M | 4096 | ~104M cells | | `V2-316M` | Geneformer-V2-316M | 316M | 4096 | ~104M cells (default) | ### scGPT presets | Preset | Checkpoint directory | `d_model` | |---------------|----------------------|-----------| | `scgpt-human` | `scGPT_human/` | 512 | | `scgpt-blood` | `scGPT_bc/` | 512 | | `scgpt-cp` | `scGPT_CP/` | 512 | `scgpt-human` is about 51M parameters (12 layers). Unlike Geneformer's public Hugging Face repo, the scGPT weights are not downloaded for you: stage them yourself, one directory per preset (see [scGPT backend](#scgpt-backend--remote-training)). ### Backends (Geneformer + scGPT) The pipeline is **model-agnostic behind a `ModelBackend` interface**. `model.backend` in the config selects which foundation model is fine-tuned; the CLI and the SageMaker entry point dispatch through a registry and never import a model library directly. Two backends ship today: | Backend | `model.backend` | Presets | Tokenization | Image | |--------------|-----------------|------------------------------------------|-------------------------|---------------------------| | Geneformer | `geneformer` | `V1-10M` / `V2-104M` / `V2-316M` | rank-value encoding | `sagemaker/Dockerfile` | | scGPT | `scgpt` | `scgpt-human` / `scgpt-blood` / `scgpt-cp` | gene-vocab value binning | `sagemaker/Dockerfile.scgpt` | The shared `training` block (epochs, learning rate, batch size, `split_sizes`, seed, label column) is honored identically by both backends, so Geneformer-vs-scGPT numbers on the same dataset are directly comparable. Both emit the same held-out metric keys (`accuracy`, `macro_f1`) and a confusion matrix. Both backends run end to end on SageMaker. scGPT fine-tunes PBMC3k on a single T4 (`ml.g4dn.xlarge`); see [scGPT results](#scgpt-results) for numbers and known gaps. scGPT runs from `configs/pbmc3k_scgpt.yaml` (sibling of `configs/pbmc3k.yaml` — only `model.backend`, the preset, and the `scgpt:` block differ). Because scGPT's `flash-attn`/`torch` stack conflicts with Geneformer's (scGPT pins torch 2.0.1), the two backends ship as **separate images** (`Dockerfile.scgpt`), selected by `launch.py --backend` / the buildspec `BACKEND` env var. **Adding a third model** (scBERT, UCE, …) is one new backend module + one registry line — no shared-layer edits. ```bash # scGPT fine-tune on PBMC3k (GPU + the scgpt-ft image): uv run scfm-ft run --config configs/pbmc3k_scgpt.yaml ``` --- ## 4-bit quantization (QLoRA) and where the memory actually goes The Geneformer backend can fine-tune in **QLoRA** mode (`training.quantize: true`): the base model is loaded in 4-bit and only small **LoRA adapter** matrices are trained. This is what lets a 104M/316M model fit on a 24 GB GPU. But the thing people expect — "4-bit makes everything ~8× smaller" — is **only true of the weights**, not of the memory that actually dominates a training step. This section explains where the memory goes, so you can pick a batch size that fits. ### What QLoRA does, concretely In `src/scfm_ft/finetune.py`, `_build_quantize_config` builds the two pieces Geneformer's `load_model` consumes: - **4-bit base** via `BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4", bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True, bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16)` — the frozen pretrained weights are stored packed in the **nf4** (4-bit NormalFloat) format, with a second quantization of the per-block scales ("double quant") shaving a little more. - **LoRA adapter** via `LoraConfig(r=64, lora_alpha=128, lora_dropout=0.1)` — a tiny pair of low-rank matrices added beside each quantized linear. These, plus the classification head, are the **only trainable parameters**. ### Which weights are 4-bit, and which are *not* Quantization replaces each `nn.Linear` with a bitsandbytes `Linear4bit`. That covers essentially the whole transformer mass — but several things stay full precision on purpose, and `_kbit_prep_get_peft_model` (which runs `prepare_model_for_kbit_training`) deliberately upcasts some of them to fp32 for numerical stability: | Component | Quantized? | Stored dtype | Why | |---|---|---|---| | Encoder `nn.Linear` — Q/K/V, attention output, FFN intermediate + output | **Yes, 4-bit** | nf4 (frozen) | The bulk of the parameters; frozen, so 4-bit storage is free accuracy-wise | | **LayerNorm** weights/biases | No | **fp32** (upcast) | Norm stats overflow under low precision (shows up as `loss 0.0, grad_norm nan`); `prepare_model_for_kbit_training` upcasts them | | **Embeddings** (token / position) | No | bf16/fp32 | Not an `nn.Linear`, so never swapped for `Linear4bit` | | **Classification head** (`classifier`, pooler) | No | fp32, **trainable** | Freshly added for the task; pinned via `modules_to_save=["classifier"]` so it trains in full precision | | **LoRA adapters** (r=64, α=128) | No | bf16, **trainable** | The low-rank deltas that are actually learned | So "4-bit" = the frozen encoder linears (≈ the whole 10M/104M/316M mass). Everything that is *trained* — LoRA deltas + head — and everything that must stay numerically well-behaved — LayerNorm, embeddings — is **not** 4-bit. ### Why activations are **not** quantized (the key point) `load_in_4bit=True` controls weight **storage**; `bnb_4bit_compute_dtype` controls the **math**. On every forward pass a `Linear4bit` **dequantizes** its nf4 weights back to `compute_dtype` (here **bf16**) and runs the matmul in that dtype. The tensors flowing between layers — the **activations** — are therefore bf16, *not* 4-bit. Nothing ever makes activations 4-bit. The consequence: **4-bit weights do not reduce activation memory at all.** Activation memory scales with `compute_dtype`, batch size and sequence length, so the lever for fitting a bigger run is **batch size (and sequence length), not weight quantization**. Raising `compute_dtype` to fp32 makes it worse (full-size activations OOM on the first step at batch 32). The code keeps `compute_dtype=bf16` and uses **gradient clipping** (`max_grad_norm=1.0`) as the stability guard, plus optional **gradient (activation) checkpointing** to trade compute for a smaller activation footprint. ### Memory by model size × batch size Rough per-GPU training-memory estimates for the Geneformer QLoRA path, so you can pick a batch size that fits before paying for a GPU. These are **computed estimates, not measured** — the one measured point is noted below the table. **How each column is built** (order-of-magnitude, bf16 compute): - **4-bit weights** ≈ `params × 0.5 bytes` + double-quant/scale overhead (frozen base). - **LoRA + head + optimizer** — trainable params are tiny (LoRA r=64 + fp32 head); their AdamW optimizer state is the bigger share but still small and **batch-independent**. - **Activations** ≈ `layers × batch × seq_len × hidden × bytes × k` — the only column that grows with batch size, and the one that decides whether a run fits. `k` folds in the several intermediate tensors kept per layer for the backward pass; gradient checkpointing cuts this roughly by the layer count at the cost of a second forward. | Model | Seq len | 4-bit weights | LoRA+head+opt (batch-indep.) | Activations @ bs 8 | Activations @ bs 16 | Activations @ bs 32 | **Total @ bs 8 / 16 / 32** | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | V1-10M | 2048 | ~0.1 GB | ~0.3 GB | ~0.9 GB | ~1.8 GB | ~3.6 GB | **~1.3 / 2.2 / 4.0 GB** | | V2-104M | 4096 | ~0.8 GB | ~1.2 GB | ~7 GB | ~14 GB | ~28 GB | **~9 / 16 / 30 GB** | | V2-316M | 4096 | ~2.3 GB | ~2.5 GB | ~13 GB | ~26 GB | ~52 GB | **~18 / 31 / 57 GB** | Read it as the shape of the problem, not exact figures: **weights barely move with batch size; activations dominate and scale linearly with it.** That is why the knob to fit a run is batch size, and why 4-bit weights alone do not rescue a large batch. > **Measured anchor:** V2-104M on `ml.g5.xlarge` (A10G **24 GB**) **OOMs at > `--batch-size 24`** but **fits at `--batch-size 12`** — consistent with the ~16 GB @ bs 16 > / ~30 GB @ bs 32 row above crossing 24 GB between bs 12 and bs 24. The launcher defaults > V2-104M to `--batch-size 12` for this reason. Enable `grad_checkpointing` (scGPT backend) > or lower the batch size to go larger on the same card. --- ## Local setup ### Requirements - Python 3.11–3.12 - [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for environment management - `git` (git-lfs optional — see below) - A CUDA GPU is strongly recommended for fine-tuning and **required for evaluation** (Geneformer's eval forward pass hardcodes CUDA). CPU runs training-only smoke tests; Apple-silicon MPS trains but is slow and cannot evaluate (no CUDA). ### Install Geneformer's pretrained weights are stored as git-LFS files. You can either use git-lfs, or — if git-lfs isn't available — clone the code and fetch just the weights you need over HTTPS via `huggingface_hub`. `scripts/setup.sh` does the latter automatically. ```bash bash scripts/setup.sh # clones Geneformer (code), installs the stack, # and downloads V1-10M weights + gc30M dictionaries ``` Or manually: ```bash # 1. Clone Geneformer code (LFS files land as small pointer stubs — that's fine) GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone --depth 1 \ https://huggingface.co/ctheodoris/Geneformer vendor/Geneformer # 2. Env + project + the Geneformer package (code) uv venv && uv sync uv pip install --no-deps ./vendor/Geneformer # 3. Fetch the real weights + dictionaries over HTTPS (no git-lfs needed) uv run python scripts/fetch_weights.py --preset V1-10M ``` Pinned versions matter. Geneformer itself pins `transformers==4.46`, but that release carries a critical CVE and several remote-code-execution advisories, so this project runs it on transformers 5 (with datasets 5 and fsspec 2026, locked in `uv.lock`). Two small build-time patches in `sagemaker/patches/` make that work: the image and `scripts/setup.sh` apply `geneformer_transformers5.py`, which swaps the four imports transformers 5 removed for a compat module and renames one training argument. Install Geneformer through those, not with a bare `pip install` of the clone, which won't import. `geneformer` is installed from the cloned repo (its token dictionaries live inside the package), so it is not a locked PyPI dependency. ### Quickstart (local) The default config uses **Geneformer-V1-10M** — the smallest model — so you can develop and iterate cheaply (16 GB GPU, or CPU for the smoke test). Promote to V2-104M (A10G/L4, 24 GB) or V2-316M (A100) for real runs by changing `model.preset`. ```bash # Full tokenize -> finetune smoke test on tiny synthetic data, CPU-only, ~1 min. uv run scfm-ft make-sample-data --out data/smoke.loom --n-cells 150 uv run scfm-ft finetune --config configs/smoke_test.yaml ``` This produces a real fine-tuned V1-10M classifier under `outputs/smoke/model/`. To try the real **PBMC3k** example (~2,700 PBMCs with standard cell-type labels): ```bash uv run scfm-ft load-pbmc3k --out data/pbmc3k.loom # fetch + format (needs network) uv run scfm-ft finetune --config configs/pbmc3k_mps.yaml # train-only (CPU/MPS) ``` Evaluation (held-out metrics + confusion matrix) needs a CUDA GPU — see the remote pipeline below, or run on a CUDA machine with `configs/pbmc3k.yaml` (`num_crossval_splits: 1`). ### CPU vs GPU vs MPS - **Training** runs on CPU (slowly), Apple MPS (slowly, memory-hungry), or CUDA GPU. - **Evaluation** (the `evaluate` stage, and `finetune` with `num_crossval_splits >= 1`) requires a **CUDA GPU**: Geneformer's evaluation forward pass hardcodes `.to("cuda")`. The CPU/MPS smoke configs therefore use `num_crossval_splits: 0` (train-only). --- ## Remote training on AWS For real metrics (held-out eval needs CUDA) without a local GPU, the `sagemaker/` directory runs the fine-tune as a managed **SageMaker training job** on a GPU instance. The training image is built on **AWS CodeBuild** (native x86-64) and pushed to **ECR** — this avoids cross-building a CUDA image under QEMU on an Apple-silicon Mac, which crashes `git lfs pull` during the weight fetch. ### Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph BUILD["🛠️ BUILD  ·  one-time, re-runs on Dockerfile/code change"] direction TB repo["📦 This repo

The **build** step reruns only when the Dockerfile or source changes; the **run** step is cheap to repeat with different hyperparameters against the same image. | File | Role | |---|---| | `sagemaker/Dockerfile` | Training image: CUDA 12.1 runtime + Geneformer weights (baked at build time via git-lfs) + the `scfm_ft` package. | | `sagemaker/buildspec.yml` | CodeBuild spec: ECR login, `docker build`, push to ECR (native amd64, no QEMU). | | `sagemaker/sm_entry.py` | Training entry point — maps SageMaker's env/hyperparameters onto a `Config` and runs tokenize → finetune → evaluate. | | `sagemaker/launch.py` | Submits the job via a SageMaker `Estimator`. | ### One-time setup (per account) These resources are created once and reused by every build/run. They require an IAM admin — the automation deliberately does **not** create IAM roles. 1. **Two IAM roles:** - a **CodeBuild service role** — ECR auth/push + CloudWatch Logs + read the source bucket; - a **SageMaker execution role** that the launcher passes as `--role`. Give it the scoped policy in `docs/iam/sagemaker-execution-policy.json` rather than `AmazonSageMakerFullAccess`: it can read the inputs and scGPT weights, write model output (`scfm-ft/output/` in the SageMaker default bucket, and nothing else there), pull the two training images, and write logs and metrics, and nothing else. It has no access to a code prefix because the launcher uploads no job code. Replace `REGION`, `ACCOUNT_ID`, `DATA_BUCKET` and `DATA_PREFIX` (the bucket and key prefix of your `--train-s3` URI, e.g. `pbmc3k` for `s3:///pbmc3k/`; drop the `DATA_BUCKET` entries if you only use `--data-source pbmc3k`). Every S3 grant is limited to a key prefix, and each `s3:ListBucket` carries an `s3:prefix` condition, so the role can't read or list other keys in a shared bucket. The scGPT weights are expected under `scgpt/` in the weights bucket, as in the staging steps below; if yours sit at the bucket root, move them under `scgpt/` (an S3-to-S3 copy) or change both `scgpt/` entries to match. Then use `docs/iam/sagemaker-trust-policy.json` as its trust policy (it limits the role to SageMaker training jobs in your own account via `aws:SourceAccount` and `aws:SourceArn`, guarding against confused-deputy use). **Accepted risks.** Two statements use `"Resource": "*"` because AWS offers no resource-level permissions for those actions: - `ecr:GetAuthorizationToken` returns a registry login token; it grants no image access on its own, and image pulls stay limited to the two repositories by the `PullTrainingImages` statement. - `cloudwatch:PutMetricData` is narrowed by a `cloudwatch:namespace` condition to `/aws/sagemaker/TrainingJobs`, so the role can't write metrics anywhere else. The identity that runs `launch.py` additionally needs `sagemaker:CreateTrainingJob`, `sagemaker:DescribeTrainingJob`, `iam:PassRole` on this role, and write access to look up (and, on first use, create) the SageMaker default bucket. No job code is uploaded. 2. **An ECR repository** for the image, e.g. `geneformer-ft`. 3. **An S3 source bucket** for the build input, e.g. `geneformer-cb-source-`. 4. **A CodeBuild project** (x86-64 Linux, `privilegedMode=true`) whose source is the S3 zip (or a CodeConnections git source) and whose env vars set `AWS_ACCOUNT_ID`, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, `IMAGE_REPO_NAME` (e.g. `geneformer-ft`), `IMAGE_TAG` (e.g. `latest`). > **Names used in the examples below.** ECR repos `geneformer-ft` (Geneformer) and > `scgpt-ft` (scGPT), CodeBuild project `geneformer-ft-build`, source bucket > `geneformer-cb-source-`, SageMaker execution role `GeneformerSageMakerExecution`, > and account `123456789012` in `us-east-1`. None of these are hard-coded requirements; > substitute your own. ## Deploy — build & push the training image Run this whenever the Dockerfile, `sm_entry.py`, or `src/scfm_ft/` changes. It stages the current `HEAD` as the CodeBuild source and triggers a native amd64 build. ```bash ACCT=123456789012; REGION=us-east-1 SRC_BUCKET=geneformer-cb-source-$ACCT CB_PROJECT=geneformer-ft-build # 1. Stage the source zip (CodeBuild reads it as input). git archive --format=zip -o /tmp/geneformer-src.zip HEAD aws s3 cp /tmp/geneformer-src.zip s3://$SRC_BUCKET/geneformer-src.zip --region $REGION # 2. Trigger the build (buildspec.yml: ECR login → docker build → push a unique `b` tag, plus the moving tag while the repository # is still mutable; logs a BUILD_MANIFEST line and the ECR scan report). aws codebuild start-build --project-name $CB_PROJECT --region $REGION \ --query 'build.id' --output text # 3. Watch it (BUILD ~5 min + push ~4 min for the ~11 GB image). aws codebuild batch-get-builds --ids --region $REGION \ --query 'builds[0].{phase:currentPhase,status:buildStatus}' --output table # 4. Confirm the image landed in ECR. aws ecr describe-images --repository-name geneformer-ft --region $REGION \ --query 'sort_by(imageDetails,&imagePushedAt)[-1].[imageTags[0],imagePushedAt]' --output text ``` The resulting image is ~11 GB (CUDA + baked Geneformer weights). > If you have a native x86-64 Docker host, you can skip CodeBuild and `docker build` > locally instead — see `docs/SAGEMAKER.md`. Do **not** cross-build the CUDA image > under QEMU on Apple silicon: `git lfs pull` crashes the build. ## Start a remote run With the image in ECR, submit a training job with `launch.py`. Each run is cheap to repeat against the same image with different hyperparameters. ```bash ACCT=123456789012; REGION=us-east-1; PROFILE=my-training-profile # The newest b tag (the build that passed the scan gate); `latest` no longer moves. source scripts/image_tag.sh IMAGE_URI=$ACCT.dkr.ecr.$REGION.amazonaws.com/geneformer-ft:$(newest_build_tag geneformer-ft $REGION $PROFILE) ROLE=arn:aws:iam::$ACCT:role/GeneformerSageMakerExecution python sagemaker/launch.py \ --image-uri "$IMAGE_URI" \ --role "$ROLE" \ --instance-type ml.g4dn.xlarge \ --preset V1-10M --epochs 10 --batch-size 12 \ --label-column cell_type --num-crossval-splits 1 \ --data-source pbmc3k ``` `launch.py` forwards all hyperparameters to `sm_entry.py`. The fine-tuned model is written to `SM_MODEL_DIR` and SageMaker uploads it to S3 (printed as `estimator.model_data`, e.g. `s3://sagemaker--/scfm-ft/output//output/model.tar.gz`). The launcher uploads no job code: `sm_entry.py` is baked into the image, and `launch.py` passes no `entry_point` or `source_dir`, so nothing under `sagemaker/` leaves your machine and the job cannot be made to run code from S3. The scoped execution policy grants the role access to the output prefix, so if you pass `--s3-prefix` or an `--output-s3` elsewhere, update the policy to match. The SageMaker profiler and debugger hook are turned off; nothing reads their output. ### One-command launcher (recommended) `scripts/do-fine-tuning-job.sh` wraps `launch.py` and packages everything the manual launch needs, so a run is a single command. It: - bootstraps an isolated launcher venv pinned to the SageMaker **v2** SDK (idempotent — created on first run, reused after), so it works from a fresh clone; - takes the training account from `AWS_ACCOUNT_ID` and resolves credentials through a named AWS CLI profile for that account (`--profile`, or `AWS_PROFILE_NAME`; the built-in default is `default`); - fills in the newest `b` build tag of the `geneformer-ft` ECR repository (or `latest` if none is found) and the SageMaker execution role for that account; `--image-uri` overrides it; - picks a sensible **GPU instance and batch size per preset** (V2-104M OOMs on `ml.g5.xlarge` at batch 24 — the per-preset default is **12**); - generates a timestamped job name and blocks until the job completes. Every default is overridable with a flag (`-h` for the full list): ```bash # V2-104M on PBMC3k with held-out eval (the default): scripts/do-fine-tuning-job.sh # Smaller / cheaper: scripts/do-fine-tuning-job.sh --preset V1-10M # Your own data staged to S3 (use your own bucket name): scripts/do-fine-tuning-job.sh --data-s3 s3://amzn-s3-demo-bucket/mydata/ # Largest model, spot pricing: scripts/do-fine-tuning-job.sh --preset V2-316M --instance ml.p4d.24xlarge --use-spot # Preview the exact launch command without submitting anything: scripts/do-fine-tuning-job.sh --dry-run ``` | Flag | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `--preset` | `V2-104M` | `V1-10M` \| `V2-104M` \| `V2-316M` | | `--epochs` | `10` | Training epochs | | `--batch-size` | per-preset (12) | Per-device batch size | | `--num-crossval-splits` | `1` | `0`=train-only, `1`=single split, `5`=5-fold CV | | `--data-source` / `--data-s3` | `pbmc3k` | Self-fetch PBMC3k, or point at your own S3 prefix | | `--instance` | per-preset | Override the GPU instance type | | `--profile` | `default` | AWS CLI profile for the training account | | `--use-spot` | off | Managed spot instances | | `--dry-run` | off | Print the launch command and exit | The sections below document the underlying `launch.py` flags the wrapper forwards. **Choosing the data source:** - **`--data-source pbmc3k`** — the job **self-fetches** the public PBMC3k dataset in-container (scanpy downloads it). No S3 upload needed; fully self-contained. - **`--data-source channel`** (default) — ship a raw `.loom`/`.h5ad` or a pre-tokenized `.dataset` directory to an S3 prefix and pass it with `--train-s3 s3:///pbmc3k/`. Tokenizing once on CPU and uploading the `.dataset` keeps GPU time spent only on fine-tuning. **Running from the launcher environment:** > **SDK note:** `launch.py` targets the SageMaker **v2** Python SDK > (`from sagemaker.estimator import Estimator`). The v3 SDK restructured these modules; > install `sagemaker==2.219.0` (or any 2.x) in a clean environment. Run from a directory > where the local `sagemaker/` folder does not shadow the installed SDK. > > **Credentials:** the SageMaker SDK's boto3 must resolve credentials directly. If a > named-profile session set only via `AWS_PROFILE` is not picked up, vend the > credentials to the **default** profile and run with `env -u AWS_PROFILE`. ### Security options `launch.py` resolves a tagged `--image-uri` to its `@sha256:` digest before submitting, so a job runs exactly the image it printed (`Image:`); `--allow-mutable-image` skips that. Other options (all off by default; details and account setup in [`docs/security/aws-baseline.md`](docs/security/aws-baseline.md)): | Flag | Effect | |---|---| | (default) | A job that reads S3 data (`--data-source channel`) runs under network isolation: no outbound network from the container. `--network-isolation` is still accepted and does nothing extra | | `--allow-network` | Give the container network access (only if the job must download something). `--regulated-data` refuses it. A `--data-source pbmc3k` job always has network access because it downloads its dataset | | `--subnets`, `--security-group-ids` | Run the job in your VPC (give both) | | `--encrypt-inter-container-traffic` | Encrypt traffic between instances of a multi-instance job | | `--volume-kms-key`, `--output-kms-key` | Customer-managed KMS keys for the training volume and the model output. SageMaker rejects a volume key on instance types with local NVMe storage (g4dn, g5, g6, p4d and others), which it encrypts in hardware, so the launcher refuses the flag there and `--regulated-data` does not ask for it | | (default) | Every input channel must carry a `SHA256SUMS` that matches exactly (`scfm-ft checksums ` writes one), or the job stops before reading the data. `--require-input-hashes` is still accepted and does nothing extra | | `--allow-unverified-inputs` | Turn that requirement off, only for data you wrote yourself. A `SHA256SUMS` that is present is still checked. `--regulated-data` refuses it | | `--manifest-sha256 train=` | Pin each channel's `SHA256SUMS` to a hash you recorded outside the bucket (`scfm-ft checksums` prints it), so a file and its manifest can't be swapped together. Required for every S3 input channel (`train`, and `weights` with `--scgpt-weights-s3`); the launcher refuses to start without it | | `--allow-unpinned-manifest` | Launch without a pin; the job then trusts the `SHA256SUMS` in the bucket and the launcher prints a warning. `--regulated-data` refuses it | | `--group-column ` | Split train, valid and test (and CV folds) by this column, usually the donor, so no donor has cells in both training and held-out data. Without it, splits are by cell, which inflates held-out scores on multi-donor data. Each split needs at least one group (a single-donor dataset such as PBMC3k cannot be split this way), and the Geneformer backend supports it with `--num-crossval-splits` 0 or 1 only (scGPT also with 5). The job writes `_group_split.json` listing the groups in each split, and its log shows `[split] by group column ...`. Images built before this option existed ignore it and split by cell, so rebuild the image before relying on it. The wrapper takes `--group-column` directly | | `--privacy-audit` | After training, run a membership-inference audit (`scfm_ft/privacy.py`): score the training cells and the held-out cells with the trained model and test how well a loss threshold tells them apart. Writes `_privacy_audit.json` and prints `[privacy-audit]` lines: ROC AUC with a 95% interval (0.5 means this attack learns nothing), the share of training cells caught at 1% and 0.1% false-positive rate, accuracy and loss on each side, and the same test per donor when `--group-column` is set. It is a lower bound: stronger attacks can do better. Needs held-out cells (`--num-crossval-splits` 1 or 5); the Geneformer backend needs 1 and `--group-column`. Up to 20,000 cells per side are scored. `--regulated-data` turns it on. `uv run scfm-ft privacy-check _privacy_audit.json` applies the release rule for sharing a model trained on human donor data (donor-level AUC at most 0.60, at most 5% of training cells caught at 1% false positives; [aws-baseline.md section 7](docs/security/aws-baseline.md#7-sharing-a-model-trained-on-human-donor-data)), and the job log prints the same verdict. Needs an image built with it: `geneformer-ft` b47 or later, `scgpt-ft` b48 or later | | `--allow-cell-level-split` | With `--regulated-data`, launch without `--group-column`, for example for single-donor data. Printed as a warning | | `--regulated-data` | Everything above for regulated data in one flag: isolation, hash checks and encrypted traffic on (and `--allow-network` refused), and no launch without KMS keys, a VPC, manifest pins and a `--group-column` (or `--allow-cell-level-split`) | | `--max-input-gib`, `--max-cells` | Tighten the input size and cell-count limits | With `scripts/do-fine-tuning-job.sh`, pass these after `--`, for example `scripts/do-fine-tuning-job.sh --data-s3 s3://// --manifest-sha256 -- --max-run 7200` (the wrapper's `--manifest-sha256` takes the bare hash and pins the `train` channel). Every input `.h5ad`/`.loom` is checked from its header for size (4 GiB), cells (1,000,000) and genes (100,000) before it is loaded; set `input.max_file_gib`, `input.max_cells` and `input.max_genes` in the config to change them. The PBMC3k download is checked against a pinned SHA-256. See `docs/SAGEMAKER.md` for the full step-by-step, including the plain `docker` alternative to CodeBuild. ## scGPT backend — remote training The scGPT backend fine-tunes the [scGPT](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scGPT) foundation model instead of Geneformer. The run shape is identical (build an image → launch a job with `launch.py`), with three backend-specific differences: a **separate image** (`Dockerfile.scgpt`, selected by `--backend scgpt`), the **scGPT pretrained weights** (not public like Geneformer's HF repo — you stage them yourself), and **`model.backend: scgpt`** presets (`scgpt-human` / `scgpt-blood` / `scgpt-cp`). > **Why a separate image.** scGPT needs `flash-attn` + a `torch`/CUDA stack (torch > 2.0.1, cu117) that conflicts with Geneformer's, so the two backends ship as > independent images and never share one environment. ### scGPT results 5-fold cross-validation on PBMC3k with the `scgpt-human` preset (~51M parameters, 12 layers, `d_model=512`) on a T4 (`ml.g4dn.xlarge`): 10 epochs, batch 12, lr 5e-5, `max_seq_len=1200`, default FlashAttention path (fp16). Stratified folds cover all 2,638 cells, so every cell is held out exactly once, and each fold picks its genes from its own training cells only. | Fold | Test cells | Accuracy | Macro-F1 | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 528 | 0.951 | 0.918 | | 2 | 528 | 0.919 | 0.841 | | 3 | 528 | 0.928 | 0.842 | | 4 | 527 | 0.934 | 0.880 | | 5 | 527 | 0.932 | 0.918 | | **Mean ± std** | | **0.933 ± 0.010** | **0.880 ± 0.034** | Accuracy is stable across folds. Macro-F1 is lower and varies more, because the rarest cell types have only a few cells per fold and a couple of errors move their F1 a lot. The full 5-fold run takes ~46 min billable on a T4 (2,769 s; five back-to-back fine-tunes; only the last fold's weights are saved). A single-split run (`--num-crossval-splits 1`) takes ~11 min. **Across seeds.** The table above is one seed (42). Repeating the 5-fold run with `--seed 1`, `2` and `3` gives mean macro-F1 of 0.902, 0.891 and 0.882, so the seed alone moves the 5-fold mean by about ±0.01. Pooled over the 4 seeds × 5 folds, scGPT reaches **accuracy 0.933 ± 0.012 and macro-F1 0.889 ± 0.033**; this is the most reliable figure here. Differences smaller than about 0.02 between two single-seed runs are not meaningful. The Geneformer figures above come from a single split, so they are not directly comparable to this cross-validated number; run Geneformer with `--num-crossval-splits 5` for a like-for-like comparison. ### How the scGPT backend prepares its input - **Gene identifiers.** scGPT's vocabulary is keyed by gene symbol, Geneformer's by Ensembl ID. The PBMC3k loader writes both (`gene_symbols` and `ensembl_id` row attributes), so one loom file works for either backend. Your own data needs gene symbols for scGPT. - **Sequence cap.** scGPT treats every in-vocabulary gene as a token, and attention cost grows with the square of that count (~27k genes for PBMC3k). `scgpt.max_seq_len` (default 1200; `--scgpt-max-seq-len`; `0` disables) keeps the highest-variance genes, chosen from the **training cells only** so held-out cells never influence selection. Raising it costs GPU memory quickly. - **FlashAttention.** `use_flash_attn` is on by default. The image ships `flash-attn==1.0.9`, which supports Turing GPUs (T4) and newer. When it is active the backend trains in fp16 mixed precision, because FlashAttention accepts only fp16/bf16. When CUDA or a loadable `flash-attn` is missing, it falls back to standard PyTorch attention in fp32 and logs the real reason. - **Gradient checkpointing.** `--scgpt-grad-checkpointing` recomputes activations in the backward pass to cut memory at some extra compute. - **Class weighting.** `--scgpt-class-weighting` (`scgpt.class_weighting`) weights the loss toward rare cell types: `balanced` uses inverse class frequency, n / (k · count), as scikit-learn does; `sqrt` takes the square root of those weights for a gentler correction. Both keep the loss on the same overall scale. Weights come from each fold's training cells only, and each fold logs them. The default, `none`, is plain cross-entropy, which is what the results above use. See [the class-weighting comparison](#how-the-scgpt-backend-prepares-its-input) below: on PBMC3k neither mode measurably improved results. **FlashAttention vs standard attention.** The same 5-fold run (T4, 10 epochs, batch 12, `max_seq_len=1200`, seed 42, same folds) on both attention paths: | Attention path | Precision | Accuracy | Macro-F1 | Billable time | |---|---|---|---|---| | **FlashAttention (default)** | fp16 mixed | 0.933 ± 0.010 | 0.880 ± 0.034 | **2,769 s (~46 min)** | | Standard PyTorch (`--scgpt-no-flash-attn --scgpt-grad-checkpointing`) | fp32 | 0.934 ± 0.011 | 0.894 ± 0.036 | 15,753 s (~4h23m) | The two paths agree: the differences are well inside the fold-to-fold spread, and neither path wins every fold. FlashAttention is about **5.7× faster** here, so it costs under a fifth as much per run. Part of that comes from fp16 itself, which the T4 runs on dedicated hardware, and part from the standard path needing gradient checkpointing (see below); the pieces can't be separated, because FlashAttention requires fp16. Use the default unless you have a reason to need fp32. **The standard path needs `--scgpt-grad-checkpointing` on a 16 GB T4.** The image pins torch 2.0.1 (required by `flash-attn`), whose standard attention keeps a full fp32 score matrix per layer: 12 cells × 8 heads × 1,200 × 1,200 genes is 528 MiB per layer, and without checkpointing a batch of 12 runs out of memory in the first training step. Checkpointing keeps the same batch and results and trades time for memory. **Class weighting.** Each mode compared with unweighted training under 5-fold CV on the default FlashAttention path. `none` and `sqrt` were run with 4 seeds (42, 1, 2, 3); each seed gives both modes the same folds and starting state, so the comparison is paired fold by fold. `balanced` was run with seed 42 only. | Mode | Seeds | Accuracy | Macro-F1 | Difference vs `none` (macro-F1) | Largest weight | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `none` (default) | 4 | 0.933 ± 0.012 | 0.889 ± 0.033 | — | 1× | | `sqrt` | 4 | 0.931 ± 0.011 | 0.892 ± 0.031 | +0.004 (95% CI −0.010 to +0.018) | ~5.4× | | `balanced` | 1 | 0.926 ± 0.017 | 0.876 ± 0.046 | −0.004 (seed 42 only) | ~22× | Neither mode measurably helps on PBMC3k. `sqrt` changes macro-F1 by +0.004 and accuracy by −0.002, both well inside their 95% intervals; it was better on only 7 of the 20 paired folds, and the per-seed differences were +0.021, −0.013, +0.003 and +0.004. (A single seed-42 run had suggested a +0.02 gain; the other seeds show that was noise.) `balanced` over-corrects: its weights reach ~22× on the rarest type, accuracy drops slightly, and fold-to-fold spread grows. The default stays `none`. Each run takes about 46 min billable on a T4. **Both paths load the same pretrained weights.** The published scGPT checkpoints were trained with FlashAttention, so each layer's attention input projection is stored as `self_attn.Wqkv.*`; standard PyTorch attention calls it `self_attn.in_proj_*`. The loader renames it on the standard path (as scGPT's own `load_pretrained` does) and stops with an error if any `transformer_encoder` weight fails to load, rather than training those layers from random values. Each run logs a line like `[scgpt] loaded N/M pretrained tensors; K left at init (...)`, where only the fresh classification head should be left at init. This relies on the image keeping `flash-attn` loadable. `scgpt==0.2.1` depends on `torchtext` without a version, and an unpinned install replaces the torch that `flash-attn` was compiled against, which silently disables it. `Dockerfile.scgpt` pins `torchtext==0.15.2` and fails the build if `flash-attn` cannot be imported. ### 1. Stage the scGPT weights in S3 scGPT distributes each pretrained model as a folder of three files on the scGPT project's Google Drive (linked from its README → *Pretrained Models*). The whole-human checkpoint `scGPT_human` is what `configs/pbmc3k_scgpt.yaml` uses: ``` scGPT_human/ best_model.pt # weights — rename/copy to model.pt (our loader looks for model.pt) args.json # model hyperparameters (embsize/nheads/d_hid/nlayers) vocab.json # gene vocabulary ``` Download them (Google Drive → local), normalize the weight filename, and upload under a prefix in your training account. The launcher mounts that prefix as a channel and looks for a per-preset subdir under it (`scGPT_human/` for `scgpt-human`): ```bash ACCT=123456789012; REGION=us-east-1 # your training account PROFILE=my-training-profile # AWS CLI profile for that account WEIGHTS_PREFIX=s3://scgpt-weights-$ACCT/scgpt # will contain scGPT_human/... pip install gdown gdown --folder "" -O weights/scGPT_human cp weights/scGPT_human/best_model.pt weights/scGPT_human/model.pt # loader expects model.pt uv run scfm-ft checksums weights # writes weights/SHA256SUMS; record the hash it prints outside the bucket aws s3 mb s3://scgpt-weights-$ACCT --profile $PROFILE --region $REGION # once aws s3 sync weights/ $WEIGHTS_PREFIX/ --profile $PROFILE aws s3 ls --recursive $WEIGHTS_PREFIX/ --profile $PROFILE # expect SHA256SUMS and the scGPT_human/ files ``` ### 2. Build the `scgpt-ft` image (no weights baked) With the weights mounted at runtime (step 3), the image carries **no** weights — it's just the scGPT stack + the shared package. Build with `BACKEND=scgpt` so the buildspec selects `Dockerfile.scgpt`, and set `IMAGE_REPO_NAME=scgpt-ft` too: the buildspec falls back to `scgpt-ft` only when `IMAGE_REPO_NAME` is empty, and a project that sets it (for example to `geneformer-ft`) would otherwise push the scGPT image into the Geneformer repository, where the wrapper's newest-`b` default would pick it up for Geneformer jobs. ```bash git archive --format=zip -o /tmp/scgpt-src.zip HEAD # The key must match the CodeBuild project's S3 source location (geneformer-src.zip). aws s3 cp /tmp/scgpt-src.zip s3://geneformer-cb-source-$ACCT/geneformer-src.zip --region $REGION aws codebuild start-build --project-name geneformer-ft-build --region $REGION \ --environment-variables-override name=BACKEND,value=scgpt,type=PLAINTEXT \ name=IMAGE_REPO_NAME,value=scgpt-ft,type=PLAINTEXT \ --query 'build.id' --output text ``` The build log's first lines show `Backend=scgpt ... Repo=scgpt-ft Tag=b`; stop the build if the repository is wrong. (`flash-attn` builds from source, so this is slower than the Geneformer image.) ### 3. Launch the scGPT training job — weights as a channel (option A) Pass `--scgpt-weights-s3`; the launcher mounts that prefix as a SageMaker `weights` channel at `/opt/ml/input/data/weights` and sets the backend's `model_root` to it, so the checkpoint resolves to `/opt/ml/input/data/weights/scGPT_human`. Change weights later by re-uploading to S3 — **no image rebuild**. ```bash IMAGE_URI=$ACCT.dkr.ecr.$REGION.amazonaws.com/scgpt-ft:latest ROLE=arn:aws:iam::$ACCT:role/GeneformerSageMakerExecution python sagemaker/launch.py \ --backend scgpt --preset scgpt-human \ --image-uri "$IMAGE_URI" --role "$ROLE" \ --scgpt-weights-s3 "$WEIGHTS_PREFIX/" --manifest-sha256 weights= \ --instance-type ml.g4dn.xlarge \ --epochs 10 --batch-size 12 --num-crossval-splits 1 \ --label-column cell_type --data-source pbmc3k ``` `ml.g4dn.xlarge` (T4) is the cheapest instance that runs the default settings. Use `--num-crossval-splits 5` for cross-validated metrics (about 5× the run time). `--seed` (default 42) sets the folds and, for scGPT, the training randomness (head initialisation, dropout, batch order), so two runs with the same seed see the same folds and start from the same state; GPU kernels can still make results differ slightly. Leave FlashAttention on (it is on by default; there is no `--scgpt-flash-attn` flag): the backend falls back to standard attention automatically. `--scgpt-no-flash-attn` forces standard attention. The job log says `FlashAttention enabled` when the fast path is on; see the [FlashAttention note](#how-the-scgpt-backend-prepares-its-input). The job runs the **same** tokenize → finetune → evaluate pipeline and emits the **same** held-out metric keys (`accuracy`, `macro_f1`) + confusion matrix as Geneformer, so the two backends on PBMC3k are directly comparable. Everything else (`--data-s3` for your own data, `--use-spot`) works identically. > **Alternative — bake weights into the image.** Instead of the channel, stage the > preset dirs under `sagemaker/scgpt_weights/` (e.g. > `sagemaker/scgpt_weights/scGPT_human/{model.pt,args.json,vocab.json}`) before the > `BACKEND=scgpt` build; `Dockerfile.scgpt` copies them to `/scgpt`, and you launch > without `--scgpt-weights-s3` (model_root defaults to `/scgpt`). Simpler, but every > weight change means a full image rebuild and a multi-GB-larger image. The weights are > gitignored either way (`sagemaker/scgpt_weights/` keeps only a `.gitkeep` + README). ### scGPT troubleshooting Problems you can still run into with the scGPT backend, by the message you will see. **Your data** - **`None of the input genes are in the scGPT vocab`.** scGPT's vocabulary is keyed by gene **symbol** (`CD3D`, `MS4A1`), not Ensembl ID. Give your matrix a `gene_symbols` row attribute (or symbol `var_names` in an `.h5ad`). Geneformer is the opposite and needs `ensembl_id`; the PBMC3k loader writes both, so copy that pattern if you want one file to serve both backends. - **`torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError` on the first batch.** Attention cost grows with the square of the gene-token count. Lower `--scgpt-max-seq-len` (default 1200), lower `--batch-size`, or add `--scgpt-grad-checkpointing`. Never pass `0` (no cap) on a full transcriptome: PBMC3k uncapped asks for hundreds of GiB. With `--scgpt-no-flash-attn` on a T4, the default settings always need `--scgpt-grad-checkpointing` (the error asks for a 528 MiB block). - **Choosing a gene cap.** The default 1,200 is the only cap measured with the current code. A larger cap costs GPU memory quickly; compare caps under `--num-crossval-splits 5` before changing the default, since single-split differences are mostly noise. - **Good accuracy, poor macro-F1.** Expected on imbalanced data: rare cell types have few cells per split, so their F1 is noisy and low. Use `--num-crossval-splits 5` to get a stable estimate; a single split can swing macro-F1 by several points, and even a 5-fold mean moves by about ±0.01 between seeds, so compare settings with the same `--seed` or over several seeds. Class weighting (`--scgpt-class-weighting sqrt`) did not measurably raise macro-F1 on PBMC3k across 4 seeds; it may still help on data with a stronger imbalance. Avoid `balanced` when one class is very rare; its weights get extreme and make results noisier. **Weights** - **`scGPT checkpoint not found at …` or `scGPT weights not found at …/model.pt`.** The loader looks for `model.pt`, `args.json` and `vocab.json` in a per-preset folder (`scGPT_human/` for `scgpt-human`). scGPT's download names the weights `best_model.pt`; copy or rename it to `model.pt` (the error says so when it finds `best_model.pt`), and check that `--scgpt-weights-s3` points at the prefix *above* `scGPT_human/`. - **`N pretrained transformer_encoder parameters did not load`.** The checkpoint's parameter names or shapes don't match the model being built: usually a checkpoint from a different scGPT preset or version, or a mismatch between `args.json` and `model.pt`. The error lists example parameter names. The backend refuses to continue rather than fine-tune with those layers at random values. **Launching** - **`unrecognized arguments: --scgpt-flash-attn`.** There is no such flag. FlashAttention is on by default; `--scgpt-no-flash-attn` turns it off. - **`unrecognized arguments: --profile` / `--region` / `--no-wait`.** `launch.py` reads credentials and region from the environment (`AWS_PROFILE`, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`) and always blocks until the job ends. Run it in the background (`nohup … &`) for long jobs and follow progress with `aws sagemaker describe-training-job`. - **The job runs different code than you expect.** `launch.py` uploads your local `sagemaker/` folder as the entry point, while the `scfm_ft` package comes from the image. Launch from a checkout at the same commit you built the image from. - **`flash_attn is not installed` in the log.** scGPT prints this for *any* failure to import `flash_attn.flash_attention`, including a `flash-attn` build that no longer matches the installed torch. Look for the backend's own `flash_attn.flash_attention is not loadable (...)` line, which gives the real error. The usual cause is torch being replaced after `flash-attn` was compiled; the `torchtext==0.15.2` pin in `Dockerfile.scgpt` prevents that. Training falls back to standard attention, which on a T4 is about 5× slower and runs out of memory unless you add `--scgpt-grad-checkpointing`. **Building the image** - **Build fails in ~15 s with `429 Too Many Requests` at `FROM nvidia/cuda`.** Docker Hub's anonymous pull limit. Nothing in your code was tested yet; wait a minute or two and start the build again. Repeated 429s need a longer wait (the window is rolling), or an ECR pull-through cache for `docker.io`. - **The build ignores your latest commit.** CodeBuild builds from the zip in S3, not from git. Re-run `git archive` and upload it to the key the project reads (`geneformer-src.zip`). Uploading under any other name leaves the old source in place without an error. --- ## Input data format Geneformer's tokenizer expects an AnnData `.h5ad` (or loom) with: - `adata.var["ensembl_id"]` — Ensembl gene IDs (the tokenizer maps these to tokens), - `adata.obs["n_counts"]` — total read counts per cell (used for normalization), - one or more label columns in `adata.obs` that you want to classify on. `scfm-ft make-sample-data` emits a correctly-formatted synthetic example, and `scfm-ft load-pbmc3k` emits a correctly-formatted real example you can inspect. See `docs/DATA.md` for details. ## Project layout ``` configs/ YAML configs (one per experiment) src/scfm_ft/ the package: tokenizer, trainer, evaluator, CLI config.py typed config schema (backend-neutral + per-backend blocks) tokenize.py .h5ad/.loom -> Geneformer .dataset finetune.py Classifier-based fine-tuning evaluate.py validation + plots datasets.py PBMC3k loader (real data) data.py synthetic sample-data generator cli.py command-line entry point (dispatches via the backend registry) backends/ the ModelBackend seam base.py ModelBackend protocol + neutral result dataclasses + metric keys __init__.py REGISTRY {geneformer, scgpt} + get_backend() geneformer/ GeneformerBackend (delegates to tokenize/finetune/evaluate) scgpt/ ScgptBackend (gene-vocab value binning + own transformer loop) sagemaker/ remote training pipeline Dockerfile CUDA + baked Geneformer weights + scfm_ft Dockerfile.scgpt CUDA + flash-attn + scGPT + scfm_ft (isolated stack) buildspec.yml AWS CodeBuild spec (BACKEND selects the Dockerfile) -> ECR sm_entry.py SageMaker training entry point (backend dispatch) launch.py SageMaker Estimator submitter (--backend) docs/ DATA.md, SAGEMAKER.md tests/ unit tests (config, data, SM entry, pipeline wiring, backends, dispatch) scripts/ setup.sh, fetch_weights.py .dockerignore keeps the build context small (excludes .venv, vendor, data) ``` ## Testing ```bash uv run pytest # config, data, SageMaker entry, and pipeline-wiring tests ``` The tests don't need a GPU or the model weights — they cover config validation, synthetic data generation, and the SageMaker entry-point/launcher wiring. --- ## Current limitations - **Geneformer evaluation requires a CUDA GPU.** Geneformer's eval forward pass hardcodes `.to("cuda")`, so held-out metrics and confusion matrices cannot be produced on CPU or Apple MPS. Local non-CUDA runs are train-only (`num_crossval_splits: 0`). - **Network isolation, VPC and KMS options are untested end to end.** The SDK accepts them and unit tests cover them, but no job has been run with them yet. - **The scGPT image's hash-locked install has not been built.** Restage the source zip and rebuild before relying on it. - **Local MPS training is impractical for real datasets.** On Apple silicon, MPS training thrashes memory and slows dramatically (e.g. ~2s/step rising to ~74s/step under pressure). Use CPU for smoke tests and the AWS GPU path for real runs. - **No local x86-64 image build on Apple silicon.** Cross-building the CUDA image under QEMU crashes `git lfs pull` (git-lfs Go runtime). The CodeBuild path exists precisely to build natively — don't try to build the training image locally on an M-series Mac. - **IAM and data staging are manual by design.** Creating IAM roles and uploading data to S3 are intentionally left to the operator (not automated), so first-time setup has a few human steps. - **Launcher is pinned to the SageMaker v2 SDK.** It won't run against the v3 SDK without edits. - **CodeBuild source delivery.** Reaching a private Git server from CodeBuild needs an OAuth/token connection; the simplest path is an S3 source zip (or a public/CodeConnections git source). Each Dockerfile change requires re-staging that source. - **Docker Hub rate limits on image builds.** Both Dockerfiles pull their CUDA base image anonymously from Docker Hub, and back-to-back CodeBuild runs can hit `429 Too Many Requests` at `FROM`. Waiting clears it; an ECR pull-through cache for `docker.io` would remove it permanently. - **scGPT's standard-attention path is slow on a T4.** It needs gradient checkpointing to fit and takes ~4h23m for 5-fold, against ~46 min on the default FlashAttention path, for the same accuracy. - **scGPT trails on rare cell types.** Macro-F1 is 0.889 ± 0.033 against 0.933 accuracy (4 seeds × 5 folds). Class weighting did not close the gap on PBMC3k. - **Geneformer runs on a patched transformers 5.** Upstream Geneformer pins transformers 4.46, which carries CVE-2026-5241 (critical) and most of the RCE advisories that were once accepted as AR-1 in [`docs/security/accepted-risks.md`](docs/security/accepted-risks.md). The image patches Geneformer's imports instead. It trains the same as 4.46.3: see [transformers 5 validation](#transformers-5-validation). The experimental QLoRA path hasn't been re-run on it. transformers 5 also logs metrics as quoted strings (`'eval_loss': '0.6338'`), so any script that parses training logs needs to accept both forms. - **Single-instance training only.** No distributed/multi-GPU data parallelism is wired up; large presets rely on a single big instance. - **PBMC3k labels are Louvain-derived**, not gold-standard annotations — fine for a benchmark, not a reference for biological conclusions. ## Suggestions for future work - **CPU/MPS-capable evaluation** — patch or wrap Geneformer's eval to honor a device argument so held-out metrics work without CUDA (would make the whole loop runnable on a laptop). - **Infrastructure as code** — a small CDK/CloudFormation stack that provisions the two IAM roles, the ECR repo, and the CodeBuild project in one step, removing the manual setup. - **CodeBuild from git with CodeConnections** — wire the source to the repo via a managed connection so image rebuilds need no S3 re-upload. - **Automated launch after build** — a CodeBuild post-build/EventBridge trigger (or a Step Functions pipeline) that submits the SageMaker job automatically when a new image is pushed. - **Experiment tracking** — integrate MLflow or SageMaker Experiments to log hyperparameters, metrics, and artifacts across runs. - **Other levers for scGPT's rare cell types** — class weighting did not help on PBMC3k; try more epochs for the classification head, oversampling rare classes, or a dataset with more cells of the rare types. - **Hyperparameter tuning** — use SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning over learning rate, batch size, frozen layers, and preset. - **Distributed training** — enable multi-GPU/multi-node for the larger presets and bigger corpora. - **Inference/deployment path** — a `predict` subcommand and a SageMaker endpoint (or batch transform) for applying a fine-tuned classifier to new cells. - **Spot + checkpointing** — resumable checkpoints so `--use-spot` runs survive interruptions on long jobs. - **More datasets and gene-classification examples** — ship additional ready-to-run configs beyond PBMC3k, including a worked gene-classification example. ## Security See [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md#security-issue-notifications) for more information. ## License Code here is licensed under the MIT No Attribution license (MIT-0); see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). This covers this repository only. The training images also install third-party code under its own terms: Geneformer is Apache-2.0 (ctheodoris/Geneformer, cloned at build time and patched by `sagemaker/patches/geneformer_quantize_device_map.py`), and scGPT is MIT. ### Data attribution The PBMC3k example uses the **3k PBMCs from a Healthy Donor** dataset (Cell Ranger 1.1.0, "pbmc3k") by **10x Genomics**, licensed under [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Source: . Please follow the 10x citation guidelines linked from that page when you cite this data. **No data is bundled in this repository.** `scfm-ft load-pbmc3k` (and `--data-source pbmc3k` on SageMaker) downloads it at runtime through [scanpy](https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/scanpy.datasets.pbmc3k.html), which fetches raw counts and Louvain cell-type labels from third-party copies of the 10x data. **Changes made:** cells with fewer than 200 detected genes are dropped, counts are converted to a loom file, and cell-type labels from the scanpy `pbmc3k_processed` object are attached. The accuracy and macro-F1 figures in this README come from models fine-tuned on this data. No fine-tuned checkpoints or per-cell data are published here. 10x Genomics does not endorse this project or the results.

one_liner: Morph2Mol 是一个从 H&E 组织学图像预测单细胞空间转录组的基座模型，通过图像编码器、空间解码器和参考细胞库实现跨模态细胞表征与表达预测，与虚拟细胞/空间组学建模高度相关。

## 是什么
Morph2Mol 是一个从 H&E 组织学图像预测单细胞空间转录组的基座模型。它利用图像编码器、空间解码器和参考细胞表达库，将组织切片图像直接映射为单细胞水平的基因表达预测，无需实测表达数据。

## 亮点
- **端到端预测**：从 H&E 图像直接输出单细胞空间转录组，无需配对表达数据。
- **模块化设计**：图像编码、空间解码、参考库检索和融合权重分离，便于替换和扩展。
- **多器官支持**：覆盖 15 个参考器官，提供 20 种器官/panel 组合的融合权重。
- **高效推理**：支持大切片（SVS/NDPI/MRXS）流式处理，避免全图加载；支持 CPU 推理和 GPU 内存优化。
- **可复现输出**：输出标准 AnnData 格式，包含直接预测、参考表达和融合分数。

## 为何对本课题有用
Morph2Mol 直接面向虚拟细胞/虚拟器官构建中的关键任务：从组织图像推断单细胞空间转录组。它为虚拟器官模型提供了图像到表达的基础映射，可作为生物基座模型的一部分，或作为 Bio Agent 中图像理解模块的预训练组件。其参考库检索机制可迁移到其他组学数据整合场景，融合权重方法可用于多模态数据融合。

## 怎么用
- **主入口**：`predict/predict.py`，运行示例：
  ```bash
  python predict/predict.py --image /path/to/slide.svs --release models/morph2mol --out results/prediction.h5ad
  ```
- **安装**：Python ≥3.10，`pip install -r requirements.txt`（依赖见 `requirements.txt`，含 torch、timm、cellpose 等）。
- **模型下载**：从 Hugging Face 下载 `zchx/Morph2Mol`，需额外获取 `MahmoodLab/UNI2-h` 访问权限。
- **输入**：H&E 图像（PNG/JPEG/TIFF/SVS/NDPI/MRXS），可选 `--mpp` 指定物理分辨率。
- **输出**：AnnData 文件（`.h5ad`），包含 `X`（融合表达）、`layers['A']`（直接预测）、`layers['R']`（参考表达）、`obsm['spatial']`（细胞坐标）等。
- **GPU 需求**：默认 CUDA，支持 `--device cpu`。
- **测试**：`tests/` 下有 `test_gene_table.py` 和 `test_prediction_compatibility.py`，可用于调试。

## 核心 idea
Morph2Mol 的核心方法学是“图像-表达双路径融合”：通过图像编码器提取形态特征，空间解码器建模细胞邻域上下文，再与参考表达库检索结果按基因级权重融合，从而在无实测数据时也能生成单细胞空间表达预测。其创新在于将检索增强与生成式预测结合，并利用器官特异的融合权重提升泛化性。

## 可搬移点
- **空间上下文模块**（`morph2mol/se2.py`、`_se2_arch.py`）：可解耦用于其他空间组学预测任务。
- **参考库构建与检索**（`morph2mol/bank_builder.py`、`bank_io.py`、`retrieval.py`）：可迁移到其他组学数据整合。
- **融合权重拟合**（`train/fit_beta.py`）：可复用于多模态数据融合。
- **图像编码器接口**（`morph2mol/encoder.py`）：可替换为其他预训练视觉模型。
- **License**：README 未明确说明，需确认。

# Morph2Mol: A Foundation Model for Predicting Single-Cell Spatial Transcriptome from Histology Images

Predict spatial single-cell gene expression from H&E images using an image encoder, a spatial decoder, and a reference bank of cells with measured expression.

## Resources

- **Website:** [Morph2Mol portal](https://morph2mol.vercel.app/)
- **Online inference:** [Hugging Face Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/zchx/Morph2Mol-demo)

- **Model:** [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/zchx/Morph2Mol)
- **Paper:** [arXiv:2608.08366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08366)

## Installation

Use Python 3.10 or later and install a PyTorch build suitable for your hardware.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zchxhcz1/Morph2Mol.git
cd Morph2Mol
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

For SVS, NDPI, or MRXS images, install the OpenSlide system library and `openslide-python`. PNG, JPEG, and TIFF images are also supported. Large slide images should use an OpenSlide-readable format to avoid loading the entire image into memory.

## Download the model

Download the checkpoints, fusion weights, gene information, and reference bank from Hugging Face. UNI2-h requires separate access through [MahmoodLab/UNI2-h](https://huggingface.co/MahmoodLab/UNI2-h).

After receiving UNI2-h access, authenticate with your own Hugging Face account:

```bash
hf auth login
python - <<'PYTHON'
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download, hf_hub_download

model_dir = "models/morph2mol"
snapshot_download("zchx/Morph2Mol", local_dir=model_dir)
hf_hub_download("MahmoodLab/UNI2-h", "pytorch_model.bin", local_dir=f"{model_dir}/uni2h")
PYTHON
```

See [model files](weights/README.md) for the directory structure.

## Prediction

Choose your own model, image and output locations in the commands below. Run prediction from a single H&E image:

```bash
python predict/predict.py \
  --image /path/to/slide.svs \
  --release models/morph2mol \
  --out results/prediction.h5ad
```

The command segments nuclei, extracts cell-centered image crops, predicts expression, retrieves reference expression, and combines both predictions. It also saves the segmentation beside the output. The model download includes the fusion weights and reference bank used by this command. The first segmentation run downloads the Cellpose model; use `--segment-model` to provide local segmentation weights.

Spatial prediction uses up to 128 target cells and 64 neighboring context cells per block, with context selected within 137 µm. All cells in the block participate in attention; only target predictions are saved. Every cell is output once. Partitioning is deterministic for a given sample ID and fixed seed.

If the image does not contain physical resolution metadata, supply its actual microns per pixel:

```bash
python predict/predict.py --image /path/to/image.png --mpp 0.25 \
  --release models/morph2mol --out results/prediction.h5ad
```

`0.25` is an example. Use the resolution of your image. Prediction requires no measured expression or precomputed image features for the target slide.

| Option | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `--cells cells.npz` | Use existing cell boundaries instead of automatic segmentation |
| `--prepared /path/to/slide` | Read prepared cell crops and boundaries instead of `--image` |
| `--tissue lung/wide` | Select organ and panel-width fusion weights; `--tissue lung` selects width automatically |
| `--genes all` | Predict all 18,580 model genes; this is the default |
| `--genes genes.txt` | Predict an ordered list of gene symbols, one per line |
| `--save-embeddings` | Save image and spatial features |
| `--workers 4` | Set CPU workers for loading cell crops |
| `--enc-chunk 32 --query-batch 64` | Reduce transient GPU memory use |
| `--sample-id SAMPLE --exclude RELATED_SAMPLE` | Exclude the target and related references when they occur in the bank |

CUDA is the default device. CPU inference is available with `--device cpu --amp fp32`. Prediction matrices are written to disk in batches; output size scales with the number of cells and requested genes. Automatic segmentation produces nuclei; use supplied cell boundaries when available.

## Fusion weights

Fusion weights cover all 15 reference organs: bone, brain, breast, cervix, colon, heart, kidney, liver, lung, lymph_node, ovary, pancreas, prostate, skin and tonsil. The [model repository](https://huggingface.co/zchx/Morph2Mol#fusion-weights) lists all 20 available organ/panel groups, including groups with one reference slide. Fitting retrieves from the other reference slides across tissues, excluding the query reference and its related donor/block samples.

Groups use organ names such as `lung/narrow` and `lung/wide`. `narrow` means fewer than 1,000 measured model genes in the fitting reference; `wide` means at least 1,000. With an organ alone, width is selected from the number of requested output genes. Supply an explicit group to keep that choice fixed when changing the requested gene subset. A missing width uses another available width of the same organ; an omitted or unknown organ uses global weights.

The model download includes the combined `beta.json` used automatically during prediction. Individual gene-weight tables are also available under `beta/ORGAN/WIDTH.json`. Global weights are fitted across the full reference set independently of organ grouping. No target expression is needed.

## Output

```python
import anndata as ad
prediction = ad.read_h5ad("results/prediction.h5ad")
```

| Field | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `X` | Combined gene-expression scores |
| `layers['A']` | Direct predictions in `log1p(mu)` scale |
| `layers['R']` | Reference expression scores; NaN where reference coverage is unavailable |
| `var['beta']` | Applied fusion weight for each gene |
| `var['covered']` | Reference coverage for each gene |
| `obsm['spatial']` | Cell centroids as x,y coordinates in source-image pixels |
| `obsm['X_morph2mol_stage2']` | Stage 2 image embeddings, with `--save-embeddings` |
| `obsm['X_morph2mol_se2']` | Spatial decoder embeddings, with `--save-embeddings` |
| `obsm['X_morph2mol_phase1']` | Stage 1 retrieval embeddings, with `--save-embeddings` |

The combined score is `beta * A + (1 - beta) * R`. Genes without reference coverage or fitted weights use the direct prediction. Combined scores describe variation across cells within each gene; they are not molecule counts.

## Training

[Training instructions](docs/training.md) cover RNA embedding preparation, image–RNA alignment, expression training, reference-bank construction, and fitting fusion weights. Training requires paired H&E images and measured spatial expression.

[Input formats](docs/formats.md) describe image geometry, prepared-slide files, reference-bank inputs, and output coordinates.

# Comparative SAE Atlas

Ten single-cell foundation models, run on the same 6,000 Tabula Sapiens cells, opened with one
sparse autoencoder per layer (172 in all), annotated with one calibrated method, and compared:
what each model encodes, what they share, which to use for a given task, and whether their
features predict biology the models were never shown.

Live atlas: https://avantipova.github.io/comparative-sae-atlas/ (also served from this
repository's `index.html`; open it locally with any static server).

## What is here

```
index.html, data/            the site: a 12 MB page plus the feature maps it fetches on demand
outputs/atlas/comparative/   the 59 result files and 7 figures every number is read from
pipeline/atlas_h100/         the GPU stage: adapters, SAE, extraction, per-model analyses
pipeline/scripts/            the local stage: matrices, controls, prediction tests, assembly, audit
pipeline/atlas_template.html the site's markup; index.html is built from it
pipeline/legacy/             earlier builders, kept for provenance, used by nothing
docs/DECISIONS.md            what was decided, why, what it cost, where it lives
docs/METHODS.md              methods in brief, with pointers into the code
docs/REPRODUCE.md            how to check the numbers, rebuild the site, re-run the analysis, re-extract
docs/RESULTS.md              every result file: written by, read by, what it holds
requirements.txt             the local analysis environment (Python 3.13, NumPy 2.3.4)
```

Not here: the manuscript and supplement (shared separately; the audit needs them dropped into
`outputs/atlas/comparative/`), the per-run feature catalogues and external inputs (1.2 GB,
published as release assets and fetched by `pipeline/scripts/fetch_runs.sh`), and the SAE
weights and activations, which stay on the GPU host (`pipeline/atlas_h100/README.md`).

The catalogues were re-extracted in October 2026 after three faults in the first release were
found: a position cap that let some models see 32 cells and others 6,000, filler genes in the
top-gene lists, and an unseeded SAE. Every number below is from the corrected run; what changed
and why is in `docs/DECISIONS.md` (decision 16).

## Check it

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
export ATLAS_BASE=$(pwd)
cp /path/to/MANUSCRIPT.md /path/to/SUPPLEMENTARY.md outputs/atlas/comparative/
python pipeline/scripts/audit_all.py      # 312 checks: paper, supplement, figures, site
python pipeline/scripts/inject_atlas.py   # rebuilds index.html from the result files
```

## The models

| model | params | layers | reads a cell as | objective | prior | species |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIDO.Cell | 10M | 8 | expression, all genes | MLM | none | human |
| scGPT | ~50M | 12 | binned expression | MLM | none | human |
| tGPT | ~120M | 8 | rank order | autoregressive | none | human |
| scFoundation | 100M | 12 | expression, read-depth aware | MAE | none | human |
| GeneCompass | 104M | 12 | rank order plus value | MLM | knowledge graph | human, mouse |
| MaxToki | 217M | 11 | rank order | autoregressive (Llama) | none | human |
| Geneformer-V2 | 316M | 18 | rank order | MLM | none | human |
| UCE | 650M | 33 | ESM2 protein tokens, sampled by expression | masked | ESM | multi-species |
| C2S-Scale | 2B | 26 | rank-ordered gene names as text | autoregressive | text (Gemma-2) | human, mouse |
| Tahoe-x1 | 3B | 32 | binned expression | MLM | none | human |

Checkpoints and sizes are in `pipeline/atlas_h100/configs/models.yaml` and Table S1.

## What we found

Every number below is audited against the result file that produced it. The controls that
failed are reported alongside the ones that passed.

- **The naive "universal core" is a database artefact.** The permissive annotator (top-5 genes
  against five large databases) reports 1,977 concepts shared by all ten models. Random genes
  share 3,570 under the same construction (z = −24.2); at the mid layer 365 real against 582
  random (z = −4.9). It does not hold.
- **A calibrated backbone is real and modest.** Requiring three of a feature's top-10 genes in
  one curated pathway of at most 200 genes, 96 concepts are shared by at least 8 of the 10
  models: 27.5× the uniform random-gene null and 51.2× a degree-matched one (p < 0.004, 250
  permutations); 55 to 133 concepts at every depth; reproduced on an independent draw of cells
  that shares none with the corpus (Jaccard 0.52 against 0.035, p = 0.02, ten models). By the
  genes behind each match, 42 concepts are one protein-synthesis block, 12 other housekeeping
  and 42 specific programmes (antigen presentation, cytokine signalling, defence, muscle); the
  96 form 37 distinct programmes (`backbone_composition.json`). No concept is in all ten models.
- **Co-expression alone recovers most of it.** A dictionary built from gene-gene correlation in
  the same cells, with no model (a seed gene plus its nine most correlated genes), recovers 73
  to 95 of the 96 backbone concepts per dictionary with random seeds; the models' own middle
  layers recover 23 to 96. The backbone is mostly the co-expression structure of the data, not
  something the models add to it.
- **Geometry agrees without the annotator.** Linear CKA between every pair of models is above
  its cell-shuffle floor (worst pair 43×). The SAE explains more variance than the best rank-32
  PCA subspace in all ten models, by +0.02 (tGPT) to +0.55 (Geneformer-V2). Tissue identity is
  linearly decodable at every depth, with no gain from a non-linear probe. PCA of the raw
  expression decodes tissue as well (0.94 balanced accuracy against 0.85 to 0.96 for the models'
  middle layers).
- **Gene pairs recover known regulation in four of the ten models, but co-expression does about
  as well.** Gene pairs that co-fire in the same features recover TRRUST edges above a null that
  preserves every gene's degree: UCE 10.2×, Tahoe-x1 9.4×, C2S-Scale 5.5×, Geneformer-V2 2.5×
  (p ≤ 0.005); the other six do not. The loose annotation rule uses TRRUST, and the threshold of
  five shared features was chosen after scoring against it. Co-expression from the same cells
  passes the same test; matched for genes and partners per gene, only Tahoe-x1 stays ahead once
  same-family and look-alike pairs are set aside, also within cell types. SAEs that were never
  trained give weaker pair signal, and a Geneformer-V2 with random weights gives none. All four
  hold on an equal budget of 50,707 pairs.
  Pairs predicted by two models independently are 15.3× over the null against 5.0× for one
  (2,000 rewirings, `agreement_curve.py`), a precision of 0.23 %; agreement beyond two models adds
  nothing (none of the 918 pairs shared by five or more models is a known edge).
- **Literature and perturbation give small support.** Co-mention in NCBI gene2pubmed
  2.3× a publication-count-preserving null; in CRISPRi Perturb-seq (genome-wide K562 screen, RPE1 essential-gene screen), knocking down
  one gene moves the other into the top 5 % of responders 1.24× more often than a
  responsiveness-matched null in K562 and 1.33× in RPE1.
- **No new biology, and the reason is the evidence.** Only 98 of 4,272 pairs were never
  co-mentioned, and six of those join two well-studied genes. The models feature 5,953 genes
  with fewer than five papers; the recurrence filter is 7.0× harsher on them, and 732 of the 774
  protein-coding ones are absent from the Perturb-seq screen. Predictive power does not decline
  with how studied a gene is. The atlas ranks testable links; it cannot confirm a link about an
  unstudied gene with these resources.

Also not supported: annotation rate as an interpretability score, "about 100 % of features invisible
to SVD" (true of random directions at this dimensionality), and a "new biology" shortlist that
two nulls showed to be a deficit. Architecture-to-feature associations rest on n = 10 models,
have bootstrap CIs of about ±1, and are reported as descriptive only.

## Credit

Built on the method and single-model atlases of Biodyn-AI
([bio-sae](https://github.com/Biodyn-AI/bio-sae)). This repository is the cross-model extension:
one corpus, one calibrated annotator, a null behind every claim.

## 是什么

CellBench 是一个**冻结骨干（frozen-backbone）单细胞基础模型基准测试框架**，用于系统评估 13 个公开的单细胞基础模型（scFM）检查点以及 3 个无泄漏训练集拟合基线（PCA、UMAP、scVI）在多种下游任务上的表现。它覆盖 12 个静态组织/疾病队列和 4 个 CRISPR Perturb-seq 筛选，共执行 2,304 次表示运行和 192 次扰动运行，并包含直接线性探针、检查点张量核算和预训练来源重叠审计。

## 亮点

- **标准化适配器层**：为所有 13 个 scFM 提供统一的冻结骨干适配器，屏蔽了不同模型架构、输入格式和预处理差异，便于公平比较。
- **全面的评估维度**：涵盖无监督聚类、批次效应评估、监督细胞类型注释、HVG 表达重建、罕见亚型线性探针、连续细胞程序探针以及 Perturb-seq 扰动预测，覆盖了从表示质量到生物学可解释性的多个层面。
- **严格的防泄漏设计**：基线模型仅在训练分割上拟合，并明确区分冻结骨干与可训练头部，避免信息泄漏，确保评估的公正性。
- **可复现的工程化**：提供机器可读的清单（manifests）、下载脚本、SHA-256 校验、隔离环境配置和单元测试，支持端到端复现。
- **预训练来源审计**：包含 208 对预训练重叠审计，揭示模型训练数据与评估数据之间的潜在重叠，增强结果可信度。

## 为何对本课题有用

CellBench 直接服务于**单细胞基础模型**的评估与比较，是构建**虚拟细胞/虚拟器官**模型时不可或缺的验证工具。它提供了：

- **统一的评估协议**：可用来衡量不同生物基座模型（如 scGPT、Geneformer、scFoundation 等）在细胞类型注释、批次整合、扰动预测等任务上的真实能力，为选择或改进模型提供依据。
- **可迁移的评估管线**：其评估引擎（cell_eval）和适配器模式可被复用到自定义的虚拟细胞模型中，用于验证模型在真实单细胞/空间组学数据上的表现。
- **扰动预测基准**：Perturb-seq 评估框架可帮助评估模型对基因扰动的预测能力，这是虚拟细胞模型的核心能力之一，也是 Bio Agent 在药物发现等场景中的关键任务。
- **防泄漏方法论**：其严格的训练/评估分割和来源审计方法，可指导我们在构建生物大语言模型时避免数据泄漏，提高模型可信度。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：`main.py` 和 `scripts/run_full_benchmark.py` 是主要入口，运行完整基准测试。
- **安装与依赖**：使用 `environment-cellbench.yml` 创建 conda 环境，并安装 `requirements-cellbench.txt` 中的依赖；可选运行 `scripts/setup_frontier_environments.sh` 为特定模型（如 CellFM、Geneformer）创建隔离环境。
- **数据与权重下载**：运行 `scripts/download_datasets.py` 和 `scripts/download_weights.py` 下载公开数据集和预训练检查点，并自动校验 SHA-256。
- **输入/输出格式**：输入为标准的 `.h5ad` 单细胞数据文件（包含基因表达矩阵、细胞元数据等）；输出为评估指标（如聚类 ARI、批次熵、注释准确率、扰动预测误差等）和诊断结果（如线性探针系数、生物学信息通道）。
- **GPU 需求**：需要 GPU 加速，尤其是运行大型 scFM 模型（如 UCE、scLong）时。
- **调试与测试**：提供 `scripts/smoke_pipeline.py` 进行冒烟测试，以及 `tests/` 目录下的单元测试，可用于断点调试。

## 核心 idea

CellBench 的核心方法学在于**通过统一的冻结骨干适配器和标准化的评估协议，将不同单细胞基础模型的表示能力转化为可比较的、可解释的生物学指标**，从而揭示模型“保留了什么、遗漏了什么、泄漏了什么”。其创新点在于系统性地结合了多种下游任务、严格的防泄漏设计和预训练来源审计，为单细胞基础模型的公平评估提供了范式。

## 可搬移点

- **适配器模式**（`bio/models/adapters/`）：每个模型的适配器封装了模型加载、预处理和推理逻辑，可被解耦并复用到自定义的虚拟细胞模型中，实现“即插即用”的模型集成。
- **评估引擎**（`cell_eval/`）：包括线性探针、聚类评估、批次整合指标、扰动预测等模块，可直接移植到自定义 Pipeline 中，用于评估任何单细胞表示。
- **数据准备与下载脚本**（`bio/assets/`）：可复用于获取和标准化公开单细胞数据集，节省数据预处理时间。
- **防泄漏评估协议**：其训练/评估分割和来源审计逻辑可被借鉴，确保自定义模型评估的公正性。
- **License**：代码采用 MIT 许可证，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认第三方模型和数据集的许可条款。

# CellBench: Frozen-Backbone Benchmark of Single-Cell Foundation Models

Official benchmark codebase, model adapters, downstream evaluation heads, statistical analysis scripts, and dataset/checkpoint manifests for **CellBench**:

> **What Frozen Single-Cell Foundation Models Preserve, Miss, and Leak**

CellBench evaluates **13 publicly released single-cell foundation model (scFM) checkpoints** in frozen-backbone mode alongside **3 leak-free training-split-fitted baselines** (`PCA`, `UMAP`, and `scVI`) across:
- **12 static tissue and disease cohorts** spanning healthy human organs, human diseases, and matched mouse organs (**2,304 representation runs** across unsupervised clustering, native batch assessment, supervised cell-type annotation, and HVG expression reconstruction);
- **4 CRISPR Perturb-seq screens** (**192 perturbation runs** across unseen two-gene combinations and unseen single-gene knockouts, anchored to zero-change baseline skill $\hat{\Delta}_g = \mathbf{0}$);
- **Direct frozen-embedding linear probes** for rare (<1%) subtypes and continuous cellular programs, **instantiated checkpoint tensor accounting**, and a **208-pair pretraining provenance and overlap audit**.
