# athenabio-technical-brief Ovarian Biology Data - Technical Brief **Intro** The AthenaBIO Ovarian Biology Data project is a 5-year, $30M philanthropic fund. It will produce the open reference data, standards and validated measures that are lacking in ovarian research. These foundations will then enable disease modeling and drug development for the era of AI. AthenaBIO has done a private call for submissions, selected and conducted due diligence on 15 leading ovarian-biology labs across the US and the world. It will maintain a shared knowledge structure, keep the labs on shared protocols and metadata standards, run common reference samples to allow inter-comparability across labs and create an open science infrastructure while also supporting focused research in the field. It will also support research and data collection efforts halted by NIH cuts. Ethical, technical, and administrative aspects of this effort make it a difficult undertaking, but a worthwhile one to advance research not only in female but human health. AthenaBIO, a 501(c)(3) (pending), is the centralized infrastructure that runs diligence, coordination, and data harmonization and generates open science data sets focused on ovarian biology. We are seeking an anchor donor and a coalition of co-funders. Capital milestone against development stage gates below. **Why us:** the AthenaDAO alumni team successfully implemented a novel funding mechanism and deployed more than $1.5M into women's health R&D. From 450 projects diligenced over 4 cohorts, it negotiated 4 IP deals, 1 academic spin-out, and has a global academic and industry network focused on the field of ovarian aging and health. Researchers funded have been published, received NIH awards, as well as brokered pharma deals post-funding by the team. **The bottleneck** Ovarian biology has no validated biomarkers, no standardized clinical endpoints and no reference dataset. Private markets will not build these, because no single sponsor can capture their value. **- No surrogate endpoints.** There is no accepted measure of oocyte quality for ovarian aging. That makes trials slow, costly and hard to justify. **- Low-quality data and data scarcity. **While we improve capturing large population menopause and transition data, which is going to take a long time, it is still hard to have access to whatever currently exists, which is very poor quality. **- No screening infrastructure. **OVARIA, a program we funded, found candidate ovarian-aging targets in UK Biobank data. It must now build its own in vitro screening system, because none exists. **- Incentive alignment. **Academic institutions and labs are not incentivized to build for open science due to current funding and granting structures. Validated biomarkers and shared reference data behave like public goods, given it will be an open science tool. They are expensive to make, useful to everyone, and impossible to monetize alone. Philanthropy is the funder that fits. **Goal and milestones** **Genesis - A foundation multimodal ovarian dataset** The first project would build a uniformly processed, community-shareable multimodal atlas of the aging human ovary by drawing on an existing biobank of cryopreserved tissue from 161 donor ovaries spanning ages 12-19 _Tissue from organ donors without known gynecological pathology is extremely valuable._ Tissue samples (post-mortem donors) from both cortical and medullary compartments would be run through a single standardized pipeline to minimize batch effects: cryosections would be assigned to adjacent-section assays, including high-resolution single-cell spatial transcriptomics to preserve follicle-, stromal-, and vascular-niche architecture, along with H&E and multiplexed immunostained histology to anchor molecular states to tissue morphology. Cells/nNuclei isolated from matched tissue would undergo joint or paired single-cell (scRNA-seq), single-nucleus (snRNA-seq) and chromatin (sn/scATAC-seq) sequencing methodsmodels to link gene expression with chromatin accessibility and gene regulatory programs, and a mass spectrometry-based proteomic arm (bulk or spatially resolved by laser microdissection of cortex versus medulla) would capture the protein-level and extracellular matrix changes, such as fibrosis and inflammaging, that transcripts alone often miss. Study design would balance age, batch, and compartment across runs, including shared reference controls and bridging samples with rigorous QC, so that modalities can be registered into a common coordinate framework at the donor, sample, and cell level. Because the cohort is dense across the 20s through the 40s, when follicle depletion and the transition toward menopause accelerate, the dataset would capture continuous aging trajectories rather than a few age extremes, with the smaller adolescent and >50 groups serving as important anchors. Deposited with open, FAIR-compliant data access, processed objects, and detailed protocols, the resource could serve both hypothesis-driven questions (e.g., which cell states, regulatory programs, or stromal changes track ovarian reserve loss) and the pretraining of a multimodal foundation model of ovarian aging, in which the paired modalities support cross-modal imputation, age-trajectory inference, and biomarker discovery. With this first clear early Genesis deliverable, we will have a foundation to test the feasibility of the larger vision and to build iteratively. By year 2, we will have the largest single ovarian multimodal dataset available and a first version of a common standard for recording ovarian data. By year 5, the goal is to deliver open ovarian data sets, annotated with menopausal status and reproductive history following a single standard, validated candidates, biomarkers, standardized endpoints and screenable model systems. Fund roadmap · 3 phases, 2 gates **Year-5 deliverables:** - Genesis tissue reference released, with a hidden test set for AI models (ovarian biology benchmark) in use by outside groups - Menopause-timing loci mapped to the ovarian cell types and regulatory regions where they act - Tissue-derived blood biomarkers, validated in longitudinal cohorts (e.g., SWAN), with a qualification plan in progress - Preclinical models scored against human ovarian aging, outcome by outcome, for predictive validity - Metadata standard adopted by funded labs and mapped to SWAN and UK Biobank standards **Levers** Five functioning levers. Labs keep their autonomy and stay where they are; AthenaBIO adds the coordination that no single lab can supply alone. Each lever comes with a commitment we can be held to before the first sample is collected. | Lever | What the fund does | What it produces | How we hold ourselves to it | |---|---|---|---| | Regranting | Funds about 15 ovarian-biology labs for 1–4 years, selected through our diligence pipeline | Omics data, biological samples, targeted moonshot projects | Every funded project states its question, its primary endpoint and its power calculation before money is released | | Shared standards | Sets common collection, annotation and QC protocols across all labs | Data that can be pooled and compared across sites | One standard applies to every sample, in every lab (from day one) | | Pooled resources | Negotiates shared access to CROs, biobanks and model systems. Genesis Project. | Lower cost and faster timelines per lab | Projects that can’t reach power alone, can be combined across labs under the shared protocol (harmonization) | | Open data release | Hosts and releases harmonized datasets under one open license | AI-ready reference data for any researcher | Data is released on a fixed schedule after QC, and is not held until a paper/report comes out | | Translation bridge | Flags assets and IP for downstream companies, while keeping data and tools open | Spinouts and licenses that draw private capital | Data and tools stay open, and only discrete inventions are licensed | **What AI-ready means, without fixing a sample count** Every dataset will meet six criteria: standardized (generated under the shared protocols), fully annotated (every sample carries the complete metadata), adequately powered (sample size set or pools samples across labs), longitudinal where possible, linked to clinical outcomes (fertility, menopause timing, disease diagnosis), and open-access. Additionally, we will also build an ovarian biology benchmark from Genesis. Data from 30 of the 161 donors will be withheld, and we will define tasks such as predicting spatial gene expression from tissue images, inferring protein levels and estimating ovarian reserve. External teams can submit models, which we run on the withheld donors and score against standard baselines. Because these donors’ data are never released, no model can be trained on them, making the benchmark an honest test of how well AI models capture ovarian biology. Without this fund, ovarian data will keep being collected lab by lab, on incompatible protocols, and much of it will never be released. The fund's distinct contribution is coordination across labs, validated biomarkers and endpoints, and open release. No single lab or atlas project is set up to deliver those. | Existing effort | What it covers | What it leaves out that this fund delivers | |---|---|---| | Human Cell Atlas reproductive work
(Human female reproductive system cell atlas v1; young vs aged ovary atlases: biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.06.10.731198.full.pdf | Over 2M cells across ovary, fallopian tube, uterus, cervix and vagina, integrated with spatial and chromatin data. Ovary-specific aging atlases compare four ovaries from women aged 23-29 with four from aged 49-54

The metadata accompanying the atlas preprint includes only four donor-related metavariables: ‘Developmental stage’ (fetal = 52 donors, paediatric = 16, pubertal = 10, postpubertal = 1, adult = 22), ‘Age’ (1st trimester = 36 donors; 2nd trimester = 16; 1–10 y.o. = 10; 10–15 y.o. = 13; 19–28 y.o. = 8; 30–35 y.o. = 6; 35–40 y.o. = 3; 40–46 y.o. = 4; 55–56 y.o. = 2), ‘Menstrual stage’ (unknown for all ovarian donors), and ‘Clinical diagnosis’. Anatomical sampling site is specified (frequently this is not the case). | Cross- sectional reference maps from a few donors per age. No longitudinal follow-up, no clinical outcome and no biomarker or endpoint qualification.

No reproductive hormone levels and cycle length are collected, so reproductive staging cannot be detailed or accurate according to the STRAW +10 criteria. Additionally, assignment of ‘perimenopause’ requires menstrual irregularity and/or vasomotor symptom data, as per the European Society of Endocrinology clinical guideline. | | UK Biobank and the ReproGen consortium
https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/
https://www.reprogen.org/ | Genetics and self-reported reproductive history at scale.
ReproGen meta-analysed over 200,000 women and found 290 loci linked to menopause timing. | Ovarian tissue or molecular data. Genetics explains only about 12% of the variation in menopause timing, so the rest has to be found in tissue biology. | | Study of Women’s Health Across the Nation (SWAN)
https://agingresearchbiobank.nia.nih.gov/studies/swan/details | NIH-funded longitudinal cohort following women through the menopause transition, with serum hormones and health outcomes. | Blood and survey data only. No ovarian tissue, no single-cell or spatial omics, and no open omics release. | | Private women's health companies (Gameto, Oviva, Celmatix, cycle-tracking apps) | Proprietary preclinical, clinical, genetic and wearable data. | Not open, mostly not tissue-level and nor harmonized across sources. | | ARPA-H
https://arpa-h.gov/explore-funding/initiatives-and-sprints/sprint-for-womens-health
https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20241023366586/en/Celmatix-Selected-to-Receive-%243.5-Million-Award-from-ARPA-Hs-Sprint-for-Womens-Health | Includes a topic on prioritizing ovarian health, funding companies such as Celmatix, which is targeting anti-müllerian hormone to extend ovarian function, and Gameto, whose $10M award supports an implantable ovarian organoid for menopause.
https://wewillcure.com/insights/womens-health/investment/gameto-awarded-usd10m-arpa-h-funding | Product development by individual companies, no shared reference data, and the data it generates stays with each company. | | PRiSM (Precision, Sex-Based Medicine) at MIT
https://prism.mit.edu/ | A multi-scale, multi-modal project integrating available data sets in with their first model focused on ovaries being released in early 2027. | Working with existing data sets rather than capturing any new data. | We will also fund work that would not happen otherwise. Labs that lost NIH funding are eligible, but only for work that fits the shared standards and data plan. Key Roles, Governance, Accountability **Roles** General Manager (Founder and operating lead) Scientific lead (RNA biologist with specialized training in neuroscience and computational biology) Ovarian Biology Lead (Reproductive Genetics) Due Diligence Lead (Cardiovascular pharmacology) Scientific Chair (Genesis Lead) Software Engineer Computational Biologist/ Data Scientist Project Manager **Lab selection.** Labs enter through our diligence pipeline, then external review by advisors with no conflict of interest. Each lab signs onto the shared data protocol as a condition of funding. **Accountability.** Every lab has annual milestones. Funding continues only when milestones are met. Donors get a portfolio report each quarter. **Governance.** Governance will be established with strategic input from Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe LLP during 501(c)(3) formation, following best practices and standards. **Measuring and sustaining impact** AthenaBIO succeeds if other people use what it produces: researchers download and reuse the data, trials adopt the endpoints, and companies build on the biomarkers. Producing data is not enough. We track impact in three stages, taking into consideration that uptakes take time to appear and early signals should predict later ones. | Stage | Timeframe | What it means | How we measure it | |---|---|---|---| | Delivery | Year 5 | Standards work and the data is reaching the public. | Share of funded projects meeting their pre-registered power target; share samples; time from collection to public release. | | Uptake | Years 6-8 | Data is useful beyond the people who generated it | Downloads and access requests from outside, publications and preprints using data by groups we did not fund, models trained, cross-lab pooled analyses. | | Adoption | Years 9+ | Field and industry are building on what we made | Candidate biomarkers entering formal qualification; report on trials or registries that adopt them; licenses; follow-on capital. | We will publish these numbers every year against targets set in advance, including projects that missed their prior target selection. Where we can, we will report. Dollars spent, samples collected and papers published by funded labs are inputs, not results, and we will not count them as success. **What we measure:** - Data quality and coverage: datasets released, life stages and clinical outcomes they cover, share QC and time from collection to public release. - Standards adoption: labs and datasets using the Genesis metadata standard, external teams submitting to the benchmark. - Biomarker qualification: candidates at each regulatory stage and how many are qualified. - Endpoints: endpoints adopted by trial sponsors or proposed to regulators. - External use: reuse by groups we didn’t fund, including data downloads, citations, models trained and access requests. - Downstream capital: spinouts, licenses and private capital raised on fund-generated IP. **After year 5** **Our goal is to leave a lasting open-science resource for female biology, starting with the ovary, that meets the AI-ready standard and improves both disease modeling and biomarker discovery.** - Data: transferred to a long-term open repository, with maintenance funded for at least 5 years and a standing data access committee for controlled-access data. - Standards: handed to a professional society or consortium to keep current - Network: continues on government and industry funding, using fund data as the base for new grants. - AthenaBIO: sets up the structure for open-access and winds down the operations, sets up an endowment for the upkeep and management of the infrastructure, or continues the work only if a new thesis justifies it. **For more information and date room access :** - hello@athenabio

card:
## 是什么

omicstra 是一个面向空间生物学（spatial biology）的多智能体 MCP（Model Context Protocol）服务器，用于跨模态嵌入对齐（cross-modal embedding alignment）、融合（fusion）以及基于证据的路由（evidence-based routing）。它通过固定科学协议（fixed scientific protocols）暴露工具，并返回证据；客户端持有模型。其核心定位是：将 H&E 组织形态学（由 Virchow2 编码）与空间转录组学（由 Novae GNN 编码）在共享嵌入空间中对齐，并基于记录的证据（evidence）回答生物学问题，当证据缺失时拒绝回答。

## 亮点

- **证据驱动的路由（Evidence-based routing）**：所有回答均基于记录在案的证据（routing_evidence.json），而非模型推断；无证据时明确拒绝，避免幻觉。
- **确定性路由（Deterministic routing）**：服务器不持有模型，路由逻辑由规则（rule）决定，而非模型推断，保证可复现性和可审计性。
- **模块化架构**：清晰分层为协议（protocols）、图（graphs）、模型（models）、度量（measures）、适配器（adapters）等，便于扩展新模态。
- **可恢复的分布式计算**：通过分片（shards）和容错机制（如 `runs_resume`）支持长时间运行的嵌入计算，且基于文件系统状态而非内存状态，支持进程中断后恢复。
- **严格的测试与验证**：1158 个测试，包括对齐一致性、字节级一致性（byte-identity）验证，以及针对路由和证据的单元测试。
- **跨模态对齐的多种策略**：支持对比学习（InfoNCE）、交叉注意力（cross-attention）等，将融合策略作为可配置的实验维度。

## 为何对本课题有用

- **直接对齐虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型**：omicstra 正是为跨模态（H&E 形态学 + 空间转录组学）对齐而设计，其方法（对比学习、交叉注意力）可直接用于构建虚拟细胞模型中的多模态融合。
- **生物基座模型的评估框架**：其 H1/H2/H3 假设（检索、生物学结构保持、通路可解释性）提供了一套可迁移的评估指标（Recall@K、MRR、ARI、CCA 等），可用于评估任何生物基座模型的嵌入质量。
- **Bio Agent 的范式**：其“证据路由”模式（基于记录证据而非模型推断）为生物 Agent 提供了可审计、可追溯的决策框架，避免模型幻觉，这在虚拟细胞研究中至关重要。
- **可插拔的编码器**：编码器（Virchow2、Novae）是冻结的，且通过注册表管理，可轻松替换为其他生物基座模型（如单细胞模型、蛋白质模型），便于在自定义 Pipeline 中集成。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：`pip install omicstra`（核心服务器，无数值计算依赖）；`pip install "omicstra[measure]"`（包含数值计算，用于计算嵌入和评估）。
- **主入口**：命令行工具 `omicstra`（15 个命令），以及 MCP 服务器 `from omicstra.mcp.server import serve; serve()`。
- **配置**：通过环境变量 `OMICSTRA_PROJECT_DIR` 指向项目目录，项目目录包含 `project.json`、`cohort.json`、`routing_evidence.json` 等声明文件。
- **运行流程**：
  1. `omicstra init` 初始化项目；
  2. `omicstra inventory` 检查数据；
  3. `omicstra gate` 检查数据可用性；
  4. `omicstra route <task_family>` 查询路由；
  5. `omicstra run` 执行嵌入、对齐、评估；
  6. `omicstra promote` 生成证据包。
- **MCP 客户端**：可接入 Claude Desktop 或 Claude Code，通过自然语言提问。
- **测试**：运行 `pytest` 执行 1158 个测试，包括对齐一致性、字节级一致性等。
- **数据格式**：输入为 H&E 图像块（tiles）和空间转录组计数矩阵（.h5ad 格式），输出为嵌入向量（.npy 或 .parquet）和评估结果（JSON）。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学洞察：**将科学协议（protocol）与模型分离，通过“证据路由”实现可审计的跨模态对齐**——即所有决策基于记录在案的测量结果（证据），而非模型推断，从而保证可复现性和可解释性。

## 可搬移点

- **证据路由机制**（`src/omicstra/routing.py`、`contracts/routing.py`）：可解耦为独立的决策模块，用于任何需要基于证据回答问题的生物 Agent 系统。
- **对齐模型**（`src/omicstra/models/alignment.py`）：包含对比学习（InfoNCE）和交叉注意力（cross-attention）实现，可移植到自定义 Pipeline 中用于多模态融合。
- **评估度量**（`src/omicstra/measures/evaluation.py`）：包含 H1/H2/H3 的评估函数（Recall@K、MRR、ARI、CCA 等），可直接用于评估任何嵌入质量。
- **分片计算与恢复机制**（`src/omicstra/dispatch/`）：可复用于大规模嵌入计算，支持断点恢复。
- **协议模板**（`MODALITY_TEMPLATE.md`）：为新模态（如单细胞、蛋白质）提供接入模板，可借鉴其设计模式。
- **License**：MIT，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认具体版本（README 标注 MIT，但需确认仓库内 LICENSE 文件）。
readme: # omicstra a multi-agent MCP server for cross-modal embedding alignment, fusion, and evidence-based routing in spatial biology. it exposes fixed scientific protocols as tools and returns evidence; the client holds the model. alignments are evaluated against declared metrics, and questions are routed from a cohort's own recorded evidence, refusing when that evidence is absent. foundation model encoders are pluggable; integration strategy is a configurable experimental dimension, not a fixed pipeline choice. the seed implementation evaluates 92 TNBC patients from [Wang et al. 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-54145-w) using H&E morphology (Virchow2) and spatial transcriptomics (Novae GNN). [![release](https://github.com/teslajoy/omicstra/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/teslajoy/omicstra/actions/workflows/release.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE) [![DOI](https://img.shields.io/badge/DOI-10.5281%2Fzenodo.22754114-1682D4)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22754114) `v1.0.0` · `v1.1.0` · `v1.2.0` · `v1.3.0` · `v1.4.0` · `v1.4.1` `ResearchHub Foundation grant` `Brenden-Colson Center / Sears Lab, OHSU` [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) --- ## using it as a tool omicstra runs as a tool inside Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or any MCP client. connect it once, then ask questions in plain language. **connect** - add to your MCP client config (Claude Desktop: Settings > Developer): ```json { "mcpServers": { "omicstra": { "command": "python", "args": ["-c", "from omicstra.mcp.server import serve; serve()"], "env": { "OMICSTRA_PROJECT_DIR": "/path/to/your/cohort" } }}} ``` **ask** - examples of questions you can ask: - "which method best retrieves matching expression profiles from H&E?" - "does the alignment preserve known tumor microenvironment subtypes?" - "which Reactome pathways are encoded in the shared embedding space?" - "can I use CCA to compare patients across the cohort?" - "what would an H&E encode cost on this machine?" **what you get back** - for each question: the recommended method, the measurement behind it, a confidence interval, and what the evidence cannot support. a question with no recorded evidence returns a refusal with the reason, not a number. ask for a figure with `show me the evidence` or a rerunnable notebook with `generate the analysis notebook`. --- ## analysis pipeline ![cross-modal alignment of histopathology and spatial transcriptomics at niche scale](docs/images/analysis_pipeline.png) **Figure 1 | Cross-modal alignment of histopathology and spatial transcriptomics at niche scale.** A single 16 µm section is stained and imaged for H&E, after which the coverslip is removed and the same section is permeabilised in situ for spatial transcriptomics, so morphology and expression share physical coordinates with no registration error between them (one of three consecutive sections per frozen block; Wang et al. 2024). The unit of analysis is a niche of seven neighbouring spots (100 µm spot diameter, 150 µm centre-to-centre; ~1,200-1,400 cells). **Left** - two measurements yield three representations. Virchow2 encodes seven H&E tiles per niche as a 7 × 1280 matrix; Novae encodes the spatial counts as a 64-d vector; gpath2vec encodes Reactome pathway activity inferred from those same counts as a 512-d vector, concatenated with Novae to a 576-d molecular vector. All encoders are frozen. **Centre** - ten arms differ only in how the two sides are joined. Six are trained contrastively (labelled R) and four are closed-form baselines with no training (labelled B). Five contrastive arms mean-pool the seven tiles into a single 1280-d vector before the two sides meet - four over the full molecular vector (R1, R2, R3, R5) and one with the pathway representation removed (R6) - while a sixth leaves the tiles un-pooled and lets the molecular side attend over them individually (R4, cross-attention). The baselines join the two sides directly by canonical correlation (B1), orthogonal Procrustes rotation (B2), principal components (B3), or a random projection as an untrained control (B4). Inputs, the patient-stratified split (85/15, seed 42) and all downstream evaluation are held identical across arms. **Right** - every arm projects to a shared 512-d space and is evaluated on 35,594 niches from 14 held-out patients: cross-modal retrieval (H1; Recall@K, MRR, median rank, alignment gap, AUC, CKA), preservation of biological structure (H2; ARI, silhouette) and pathway interpretability (H3; canonical correlation against a permutation null). --- ## evidence, defined **Evidence is a measurement of how well a method performs one task on this cohort, scored against a stated reference, compared to a floor, and traced to the artifact that produced it.** Five parts, all required: 1. **Units** - what was scored, and how held out. Here: niches, held out by patient. 2. **Reference** - the ground truth for that question. 3. **Statistic** - the maths applied: area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), adjusted Rand index (ARI), canonical correlation analysis (CCA), or a z-score against a permutation null. 4. **Floor or null** - what the number must beat to mean anything. 5. **Guards** - conditions that would make the number misleading even when it is high. **the reference is per question** | question | ground truth | where it comes from | |---|---|---| | cross-modal retrieval | the known pairing - which haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) niche *is* which spatial transcriptomics (ST) niche | the assay itself, same physical section | | tissue state grouping | `mc_megacluster`, 14-class non-negative matrix factorisation (NMF) label. Normalised mutual information (NMI) 0.539 against patient identity, above the 0.5 bar - so ARI here is diagnostic and cannot rank the aligned methods against each other; the 9-archetype label is worse (0.645) and was dropped | per-spot NMF, molecular | | subject identity suppression | tumour immune microenvironment (TIME) class, defined on global pseudobulk expression, one per patient - so the label is patient-level by construction, which is why only cross-patient pairs are scored and the null permutes labels between patients | expression, patient-level pseudobulk | | morphology decode | tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) gene-signature score | molecular, continuous | | pathway transfer | Reactome pathway membership | curated knowledge graph, no human label | | compartment agreement | pathologist annotation (Wang: 15 categories). Not bound on the seed cohort, so this question routes to compute rather than to evidence | pathologist annotation | Pathologist annotations and molecular clusters are both references - each for the questions where it is the right one. Retrieval needs no label at all, because the correspondence *is* the truth. Pathway transfer uses a knowledge graph and a permutation null instead of a label. **A number without all five parts is not evidence. An ARI with no floor, or one scored against a label that encodes patient identity, is a number, and the guard is what says so.** --- ## using omicstra A question travels in three steps. A model reads the question and picks the task family; a rule does everything after that. The server itself holds no model. ``` human question -> task family -> route(task_id) -> outcome + why (a model) (7 defined) (a rule) (recorded) ``` **ask which method answers a question** > *"Given a piece of tissue image, which method best finds its matching expression profile?"* A model maps that to the family `cross_modal_retrieval` and calls the `route` tool. On the command line: ``` $ omicstra route cross_modal_retrieval --project-id tnbc-92 [RECOMMEND] InfoNCE, cross-attention why: AUC, matched vs mismatched pairs, cross-subarray patient-held-out: 0.8591 [0.8576, 0.8608]. below the floor: random-init projection, unaligned principal components record_id: ccbcf5ec8e9b ``` **name a method, and the evidence can decline it** > *"Can I use canonical correlation analysis to pool across patients?"* That is the family `subject_identity_suppression`, with a method named: ``` $ omicstra route subject_identity_suppression --proposed-method B1_v3 CCA is contraindicated for this task. It scores below what the raw un-aligned modality already achieves: bio/patient ratio 0.071 [0.053, 0.088], below the raw H&E floor of 0.137. patient z 113.0 against raw H&E 36.8. proceed anyway? [y/N] ``` Proceeding is permitted, and is recorded as a decision taken against the evidence. **check the evidence still holds** > *"Do the published numbers still come out of the data?"* ``` $ omicstra run --project-id tnbc-92 --diff projects/tnbc-92/routing_evidence.json ok embed_he ok embed_st ok niche_join ok align ok eval ok promote diff: 1 disagreement - pathway_transfer/B3_v3 absent_from_curated ``` Every routed number traces to a named artifact; this is the check that says so. **ask what a run will cost before spending it** > *"I have my own cohort. What do I need to produce the embeddings, and can this machine do it?"* That is `describe_compute_plan`. Units come from the inventory, seconds and bytes per unit from the encoder's own measurements, free space from the volume being written to. Nothing here is extrapolated: ``` 280 shards, 286,250 tiles, none done yet 5.8 h on mps 1.47 GB out 6.3 GB peak verdict: fits - run it here measured on: the published extraction, 280 subarrays ``` An encoder with no measurement on this device refuses instead of guessing, and a resource the pool declares no value for is reported as unchecked rather than as passed. If the plan says the output will not fit where the cohort declared it, the declaration stops standing and the gate re-opens. **produce the embeddings, and survive the run being interrupted** > *"Run it. What happens if my laptop sleeps four hours in?"* Extraction runs through the same surface a client uses, not through a script around it. Each modality is its own agent, because they ask different questions: the H&E arm asks about gated weights and a tile geometry, the ST arm about the encoder's prototype floor and the edge scale. ``` he_encode(compute=True) -> awaiting_answer: 3 gates runs_resume(run_id, answers={...}) -> submitted, in 0.3 s (submission returns; the run does not) runs_status(run_id) -> running 2/4 missing [sec2, sec3] ``` Gates arrive as interrupts carrying their evidence and what accepting forecloses, so nobody accepts a caution without seeing the diagnostic behind it. An answer already in the cohort's declarations closes its gate without asking. One shard per section, three attempts each, and the output file is the only record of what finished - so resume is decided by the filesystem rather than by a ledger that can disagree with it. Kill the process mid-shard and a second process, given only the `run_id`, reads the missing sections off disk, resumes, and does not rewrite what landed. A shard that fails every attempt is recorded as failed rather than staying indistinguishable from a slow one - one unreadable slide does not cost the other 279. Two executors, and the record names which one ran, because they promise different things: | | what survives a restart | |---|---| | in-process | the output files and the checkpoint. the thread does not; `runs_resume` re-dispatches what is missing | | Temporal | the workflow history. a worker that never met the submitting process finishes the run | **two traces, and only one of them is free** ``` the LEDGER who decided what, on what authority, over which bytes. committed, citable, always on, and it never leaves the machine. `runs_record` is one run's; `runs_trace` is that run as a timeline; the report reads the cohort's LANGSMITH what a node received, how long it took, where it stalled. richer, and it sends node inputs and outputs to a third party ``` LangSmith is **opt-in through the environment and is not a dependency** - it ships transitively with LangGraph, which instruments itself from two variables, so turning it on takes no code: ```bash export LANGSMITH_TRACING=true export LANGSMITH_API_KEY=... ``` That is exactly why there is a guard. Node inputs are cohort content, and `data_contract.json#data_classification` declares per cohort whether content `may_leave_host`. A cohort declared `restricted` - the **default**, so forgetting to declare fails closed - refuses to run with external tracing on, rather than quietly sending it. The classification is a person's statement at `omicstra init` and is never inferred from paths or content. There is a third state, and the SDK provides it: mask the payloads before anything is sent, and a restricted cohort can be traced for **structure** - spans, timings, errors, which node stalled - without its content leaving. ```bash export LANGSMITH_HIDE_INPUTS=true LANGSMITH_HIDE_OUTPUTS=true ``` Both are required; hiding one and sending the other sends the content. What still leaves is run names, timings, token counts and error strings - step ids like `preflight_encode` are the package's vocabulary, not a cohort's - and a project id would travel in metadata, which `LANGSMITH_HIDE_METADATA` masks in turn. On Temporal the submit returns at submission, so something has to be polling the queue. That is the other half of the claim and it ships as a command: ```bash export OMICSTRA_TEMPORAL_ADDRESS=localhost:7233 omicstra worker # until signalled omicstra worker --max-seconds 7200 # inside a job allocation with a wall clock ``` The worker needs no cohort, no project root and no knowledge of the run: a shard carries its own geometry, gene axis, paths and encoder name, and the activity bodies close over nothing. So it may be started before or after the submitter, outlive it, or run on another machine, and because a shard is idempotent on its output file a worker joining a run already in flight re-runs nothing that landed. An encoder a cohort brought itself is made resolvable there with `--preload `. **check the vectors are the ones the published grid used** The 75 GB embedding cache is the oracle, and it is read, never written. A port is verified by diffing against it rather than by re-extracting: ``` 6 shards, 6 accepted, 0 rejected drift 2.2e-06 to 4.7e-06 against a 1e-05 tolerance cosine 0.9999998 knn top-6 set 1.000 ``` Bit-identity is available for alignment - deterministic linear algebra, 13/13 metrics at exactly zero - and is not available for a 631M-parameter float32 transformer across backends. The two backends on one machine differ by as much as either differs from the cache, so the tolerance is declared and the run is labelled a tolerance run rather than an exact one. The dispatcher refuses any shard whose output would land inside a path the cohort declares read-only. **start a new cohort** > *"What can this dataset answer?"* ``` omicstra init --project-dir projects/mine # scaffold the declarations omicstra inventory # what the data is omicstra gate # is it usable omicstra families # what it can answer, and what it cannot ``` A cohort with no evidence of its own is not routable, and the server says so rather than reusing another cohort's winner. **the tools** | tool | answers | |---|---| | `list_task_families` | which questions this cohort can be asked | | `route` | which method answers one question, or why none does | | `describe_data_structure` | what the data is, as declared | | `describe_encoder_fit` | whether the declared encoders were built for this kind of data | | `check_eda_gate` | is the cohort admissible, and on what grounds | | `run_eda_step` | re-run one admissibility check, with its permutation null | | `plot_spatial_autocorrelation` | the spatial signal behind that check, as a figure | | `plot_evidence` | the evidence behind one answer, as a figure | | `decision_record` | what has been decided here, by rule and by person | | `check_compute_gates` | what a compute run would need answered first | | `describe_compute_plan` | what a run would cost, read, write, and leave untouched | | `he_encode` | run the H&E morphology agent; returns a run handle | | `st_encode` | run the spatial-transcriptomics agent; its own gates, not a mode of the above | | `runs_status` | what a run is doing, counted from the output files rather than remembered | | `runs_resume` | answer an open gate, or re-dispatch the sections a dead run left missing | | `runs_record` | the run's half of the ledger: every gate, who answered it, from which declaration | | `runs_trace` | the timeline of a run: every step in order, duration, and which actor decided it | | `align_run` | resolve a cohort's alignment grid from its recorded artifacts, behind a run handle | | `evaluate_run` | return a verdict on H1/H2/H3 for a cohort, behind a run handle | | `evaluate_measure` | compute a verdict from a cohort's own arrays, rather than reading one from a curated pack | | `unit_notebook` | write one analysis unit as a rerunnable notebook plus a markdown trace | **what that lets you do today** ``` 1 point it at a cohort it has never seen hest-breast, 3 sections encoded 2 ask what the data is and whether the declared no compute encoders were built for it 3 run the admissibility checks per section pass / fail / not_run / across the whole cohort, each with its null not_applicable, never a guess 4 ask what an encode would cost no compute 5 start an H&E or ST encode, answer its gates, submission returns in 0.3 s and walk away 6 kill the process, come back, resume by run_id finishes without redoing work 7 read the record: which gate, which answer, and whether a person or a from which declaration client supplied it 8 ask which fusion answers which question tnbc-92 only - a cohort with on the seed cohort, and why no evidence is not routable ``` Two claims in there are separate and are tested separately: **resume** is verified by killing a process mid-shard on both executors, and **byte-identity** by re-encoding sections of the seed cohort and diffing against the published cache - exact on the ST side, within a declared tolerance on H&E. Four of the ten admissibility checks return `not_run` on the seed cohort for want of a cohort declaration, and three are declared in the contract with no implementation registered behind them. The gate reports that rather than reaching a verdict on silence - and a check that finds none of its declared genes returns `not_run` with the missing list, because a check that measured nothing must not read as a pass. **what it cannot do yet** ``` fuse or align on a second cohort v1.4 open item #33: align_run trains through the package, not scripts produce that cohort's own evidence pack v1.4 open item #34: a real second cohort (HEST Visium candidate) produces its own routing_evidence.json registration across sections declared, not built. both cohorts are same-section, so nothing here needs it mitochondrial-fraction exclusion not implemented. a proposal commitment, recorded in open_items.md #18 SLURM not implemented ``` for a full table of supported questions, required data, methods, outputs and limitations per task family, see [docs/capability_matrix.md](docs/capability_matrix.md). tracked in [open_items.md](docs/open_items.md) and [completion_roadmap.md](design/completion_roadmap.md). --- ## hypotheses | | | metrics | |---|---|---| | **H1** | aligned embeddings retrieve better cross-modal matches than any unaligned baseline | Recall@K - MRR - median rank - alignment gap - AUC - CKA | | **H2** | manifold alignment preserves biological structure better than either modality alone | | |     *A* | spatial states cluster more coherently in the aligned space than in either modality alone | ARI - silhouette | |     *B* | alignment quality varies across compartments - morphologically distinct ones (tumour, TLS, necrosis) above ambiguous ones (high- vs low-TIL stroma) | matched-pair cosine per compartment | | **H3** | shared space encodes interpretable biological pathway signals | CCA vs permutation null | early vs late fusion is an experimental variable, not an assumption. --- ## seed cohort results (v3, 10-run grid) evaluated on **35,594 niches across 14 held-out TNBC patients** (zero patient leakage across train / val / test). 6 contrastive runs (R1-R6) + 4 classical baselines (B1-B4): - **H1 (cross-modal retrieval).** R4 wins. AUC 0.859 (95% CI 0.855-0.862). R4 is the only run using cross-attention - the other 5 contrastive runs use late fusion (mean-pooled H&E + independent MLPs). - **H2 (biology preservation).** Split outcome. Late-fusion contrastive (R1, R6) wins K-means MC ARI; R4 still encodes MC biology at linear-probe parity. KMeans-ARI is geometry-biased - load-bearing diagnostic is the linear probe. - **H3 (pathway transfer).** R4 wins again. 15/15 cells BH-FDR < 0.05 cross-patient (Welch z 3.8-5.7). At DAG resolution, R4 stays best (78% sig nodes) on clinically interpretable hits: BTLA checkpoint, IL signaling, IFN regulation, ECM collagen biology. **R4 = the only non-late-fusion run** (cross-attention between the niche's 7 Virchow2 tile tokens and the 576-d ST vector). H1 + H3 both reward keeping local morphological heterogeneity un-pooled. --- ## the loop a **level** is what code is allowed to do (LEVEL 0/1/2 in the tree below); the **loop** is the order a cohort goes through. they are different axes and the words are easy to confuse: ``` layer 0: EDA (gate) is data usable? quality? signal? modalities alignable? -> proceed / proceed with caution / stop layer 1: pipeline (execution) embed -> align -> eval fixed protocol, deterministic with seed layer 2: karpathy loop (outer optimization) editable asset: alignment_config.json scalar metric: Recall@K or MRR (fixed) proposes config -> runs pipeline -> scores -> keeps or discards output: git log of validated decisions + winner.json ``` program.md defines search space, constraints, stopping criteria. embedding dimensions: Virchow2 1280d - Novae GNN 64d (novae_latent) -> shared 512d alignment strategies (experimental variable): ``` late interaction - tiles aggregated per spot (mean/max), then independent MLPs -> shared 512d (InfoNCE) early interaction - tile-level cross-attention between H&E tokens and ST spot before projection (~4M params, local K tiles) comparison: does tile-level morphological detail lost at aggregation matter for cross-modal alignment quality? ``` --- ## repo structure audited against the filesystem 2026-11-17. `·` is built, `○` is named in the design and **not yet built** - kept here because the name is referenced elsewhere, not because it exists. ``` omicstra/ │ · CLAUDE.md # 92 TNBC patients, co-registered ST + H&E WSI. platform: original Spatial Transcriptomics (Stahl et al. 2016, KTH/Spatial Transcriptomics AB) - 1934 spots/array, 100um diameter, 150um center-to-center. | resource | url | |---|---| | processed data | [doi:10.5281/zenodo.14204217](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14204217) (mc-labels release also at [doi:10.5281/zenodo.8135721](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8135721)) | --- ## quick start ```bash pip install omicstra # serves, routes, gates - no numpy, no tensor libraries pip install "omicstra[measure]" # + the numerics, for computing inventory and EDA steps ``` the package ships its contracts and no cohort. point it at one: ```bash export OMICSTRA_PROJECT_DIR=/path/to/projects/tnbc-92 omicstra selftest # start here: asserts the routing rules hold on this cohort omicstra describe # what the cohort declares - platform, encoders, roles omicstra families # which questions it can answer, and which it cannot yet omicstra route cross_modal_retrieval ``` `omicstra --help` lists all fifteen. Four answer *what is this cohort* - `describe`, `inventory`, `gate`, `families`. Four answer *what does it say* - `route`, `selftest`, `decisions`, `report`. Five do the work - `eda`, `align`'s grid through `run`, the whole walk through `chain`, `promote`, and `worker` for the encode queue. One starts a cohort - `init`. One writes the record a reader opens - `notebook`, which emits an analysis unit as a rerunnable notebook plus its trace. **`selftest` first** - it tells a new cohort owner whether their declarations and evidence hang together before they spend time on anything else. **stdio** - the usual client config: ```json { "mcpServers": { "omicstra": { "command": "python", "args": ["-c", "from omicstra.mcp.server import serve; serve()"], "env": { "OMICSTRA_PROJECT_DIR": "/path/to/projects/tnbc-92" } } } } ``` **streamable-http** - `serve(mode="http")`, then note the envelope: ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{"_meta":{ "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion":"2026-07-28", "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities":{}}}}' ``` the `_meta` block is not optional and is the first thing a new http caller gets wrong. protocol revision 2026-07-28 removed the initialize handshake, so the version travels on **every** request rather than being negotiated once. a call without it is refused with `-32602`, naming the two keys it wants. **the modality agents are client-callable, not CLI commands.** `omicstra --help` covers the read path and the chain; `he_encode` and `st_encode` are MCP tools, because each fires gates a client has to answer and returns a run handle a later request resumes. Driving them from a shell would mean inventing a way to answer an interrupt. A worked run, on a cohort the package had never seen - three sections, two gene identifier spaces and three different edge scales in one call: ``` st_encode(platform="original_st", samples=["SPA125","SPA126","SPA99"], compute=True) -> awaiting_answer: encoder_compatibility, platform_floor, capacity runs_resume(run_id, answers={ "encoder_compatibility": "proceed_anyway_recorded_as_dissent", "platform_floor": "run_and_mark", "capacity": "continue"}) -> submitted executor in_process, returns in 0.0 s scale_to_microns [0.6894, 0.6911, 0.6971] per_sample: true gene_axis_route ["ensembl->symbol", "symbol->symbol"] gene_axis_map ensembl_to_symbol.tsv @ 3d6e353cc58391fa runs_status(run_id) -> complete 3/3 runs_record(run_id) -> preflight_encode selection actor=client confirmed_by=null encode_dispatch dispatch actor=system executor=in_process ``` The gates are interrupts carrying their evidence and what accepting forecloses, so nobody accepts a caution without the diagnostic behind it. An answer already in the cohort's declarations closes its gate without asking, and an answer given through the surface is recorded `actor=client` - the server sees a tool call, not a person, and the pack cites gate answers. **Refusals are per section, and they name the missing declaration.** Before this cohort declared a `gene_mapping`, the same call returned: ``` n_shards 2 skipped 1 SPA99 [gene_mapping] section is 'ensembl', encoder needs 'symbol', cohort declares no gene_mapping ``` Two sections encoded, one named what it needed. The alternative is what happened first: the encoder's own `AssertionError: Too few genes (0) are known` from inside a worker, on whichever section happened to be indexed differently. a cohort with no evidence pack is **not routable**, and the compute path refuses rather than improvising: `route` declines instead of inheriting another cohort's winner, and `run_align` raises `ComputeUnavailable` naming the missing artifact and the script that builds it. that refusal is the expected first response on a fresh install, not a failure. --- ## stack | layer | tool | |---|---| | orchestration | LangGraph StateGraph | | model | supplied by the MCP client; the server ships none | | tracing | OpenTelemetry-ready; LangSmith optional via env, not a dependency | | resources | `omicstra://eda-contract`, `routing-contract`, `project/{id}/routing-evidence`, `project/{id}/eda-summary` | | H&E foundation model | Virchow2 (1280-d) | | ST foundation model | Novae GNN | | pathway | gpath2vec + biological pathway embeddings | | alignment | contrastive MLP + cross-attention bridge | | compute | laptop (v1.0); SLURM planned | | interface | Model Context Protocol | --- ## reproducibility every run writes `runs/{project_id}/{run_id}/` - config, QC, embeddings, alignment, evaluation, synthesis. `notebooks/final/` contains the best run as a notebook, drafted with a model from the run trace and reviewed by hand; reruns go top-to-bottom with a fixed seed. --- ## deliverables - [x] v3 10-run alignment grid on TNBC-92 - [x] pip-installable MCP server (MIT) - verified on python 3.11 / 3.12 / 3.14 - [x] alignment checkpoint + model card ([teslajoy/omicstra-r4-v3](https://huggingface.co/teslajoy/omicstra-r4-v3)) - [ ] embeddings and niche join deposited (Zenodo) - [ ] second-modality plug-in via `MODALITY_TEMPLATE.md` (target: CODA or CyCIF) --- ## how the evidence pack is produced The router reads `projects/{id}/routing_evidence.json`. **No script writes it.** ``` eval summaries ──▶ proposed evidence deterministic: winners, margins, refusals ──▶ a person reviews, edits the notes, approves ──▶ routing_evidence.json ``` Deciding which metric answers which task family, what the floors are, and which caveat attaches to which candidate is editorial work - the file's own notes argue with the report in places. Generating it would invent the judgements it records, so `run_eval` scores the grid and **resolves** the pack; it never produces one. **`omicstra promote`** computes the half that is computable - candidates, intervals, floors, guard verdicts and the contract's outcome - and asks a person for the rest. It is a gate rather than a protocol because it pauses, and it refuses a pack in which a measurement was authored. Rebuilding this cohort reproduces every value and interval in the curated pack. The acceptance test for the port is pinned in `tests/fixtures/`: a full-grid rerun with one retrained baseline reproduced every numeric field of the H1 summary, and the fixture is checked against the evidence pack so the router can never quote a number nothing produced. --- ## declared deviation from the proposal The registered report put a model **inside** the orchestration: one model for intent classification and routing, another for hypothesis evaluation, with conditional routing in the graph. **The build moved the model to the client and made routing a deterministic rule over evidence.** The server holds no model, generates no code, and executes nothing a model wrote. A model has three narrow jobs, all on the client side: classify a question into a closed task set, choose among enumerated options at a gate, and write the "why". Everything downstream resolves from lookup tables. The reason is reviewability. A server with no model is portable across clients, has no second router to reason about, and can be reviewed for what it does rather than what it might decide. It also means swapping the model cannot change a route - the same question reaches the same method, because the method came from recorded evidence rather than from inference. **Deliverables, metrics and hypotheses are unchanged.** --- ## team **Nasim Sanati, M.S.** - AI/ML systems - MCP server - agent orchestration - embedding pipelines Brenden-Colson Center for Pancreatic Care / Sears Lab, OHSU --- ## citation ```bibtex @software{sanati2026omicstra, author = {Sanati, Nasim}, title = {omicstra: a multi-agent MCP server for cross-modal embedding alignment and evidence-based routing in spatial biology}, year = {2026}, doi = {10.5281/zenodo.22754114}, url = {https://github.com/teslajoy/omicstra}, license = {MIT} } ``` that is the **concept** DOI - it resolves to the newest archived version and never goes stale. cite it unless you need to pin one release, in which case use that release's own version DOI from the Zenodo record. *funded by ResearchHub Foundation ([doi:10.55277/researchhub.6ou1w3h3](https://doi.org/10.55277/researchhub.6ou1w3h3))* *nonprofit recipient: OHSU Foundation - EIN 23-7083114* *seed cohort: Wang et al. 2024, Nat. ## 是什么

ssl-lab 是一个自监督学习实验室，专注于开发**可生成可信生物数据**的新方法。其旗舰目标是**单细胞扰动预测**：给定一个细胞群体和一种（可能从未实验过的）遗传扰动，生成扰动后的细胞群体——包括哪些基因表达变化、变化幅度以及细胞间的异质性。该仓库的核心方法是将 **JEPA（联合嵌入预测架构）** 从纯表征学习扩展为**可采样的生成模型**，通过添加潜在先验和与数据似然匹配的解码器实现。

## 亮点

- **方法学前沿**：以 JEPA 为起点，通过添加先验和解码器使其具备生成能力，并系统性地绘制了设计空间（四条路线：解码潜在、变分后验、条件扩散、规划）。
- **严谨的实验方法**：所有研究均预先注册，比较同一研究内的不同臂，并报告每个数字的不确定性（联合配对 bootstrap 与 max-t 区间）。
- **模块化架构**：核心原语与薄驱动脚本分离，便于复用和替换。
- **模态无关设计**：核心方法不绑定特定数据模态，通过数据适配器可迁移到单细胞、生理信号、健康记录等。
- **远程训练支持**：通过 `ops/` 包（SkyPilot + RunPod）支持 GPU 集群训练，且与核心库解耦。

## 为何对本课题有用

- **直接对齐**：该仓库正是针对**单细胞扰动预测**这一虚拟细胞核心任务，其方法（JEPA + 条件流先验 + 计数解码器）可直接用于构建**虚拟细胞模型**，预测未实验的基因组合扰动响应。
- **生物基座模型**：JEPA 作为自监督表征学习前沿，其生成化扩展为构建**生物基座模型**提供了新范式，可学习可采样的细胞表征。
- **Bio Agent 支持**：生成模型可作为**Bio Agent** 的模拟器，用于规划实验、进行反事实推理（如“如果增加睡眠会怎样”），减少真实实验需求。
- **空间组学迁移**：虽然当前聚焦单细胞，但其模态无关设计可迁移到空间组学数据，通过适配器处理空间坐标和邻域信息。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：`mamba env create -f environment.yml`，`conda activate ssllab`，`pip install -e .`。
- **主入口**：示例脚本位于 `examples/`，核心库在 `src/ssllab/`。
- **快速运行**：
  ```bash
  python examples/jepa_basics/01_train_jepa_mnist.py --epochs 5
  python examples/jepa_basics/02_linear_probe.py
  python examples/generative_jepa/03_train_decoder.py --epochs 5
  python examples/generative_jepa/04_train_flow_prior.py --epochs 20
  python examples/generative_jepa/05_sample_and_decode.py
  ```
- **数据格式**：单细胞数据使用 Norman 2019 Perturb-seq，通过 `src/ssllab/data/` 中的适配器处理，输出为 token 张量。ECG 数据使用 PTB-XL，通过带校验和的 WFDB 读取器。
- **GPU 支持**：需要 GPU 进行大规模训练，本地 CPU 可用于小规模实验。
- **测试**：`pytest` 运行测试，测试路径在 `tests/` 和 `ops/tests/`。

## 核心 idea

**将 JEPA 从被动表征学习器转变为主动生成模型**：通过引入条件流先验（`v(z, t, c)`）和解码器，使模型能够基于条件（如扰动）生成新的数据样本，同时利用 JEPA 的嵌入预测能力学习丰富的、非坍缩的潜在表征。其关键洞察是：JEPA 的预测器本身就是一个潜在算子，通过将其查询从“位置”提升为“动作”，可以实现干预和反事实推理。

## 可搬移点

- **条件流先验模块**（`src/ssllab/generative/`）：实现条件流先验和 classifier-free guidance，可直接解耦并替换到自定义 Pipeline 中，用于条件生成任务。
- **JEPA 编码器/预测器**（`src/ssllab/models/`）：可复用的 JEPA 模块，支持块掩码和 EMA 目标，可迁移到其他自监督任务。
- **计数解码器**（`src/ssllab/generative/`）：NB/ZINB 计数解码器，适用于单细胞计数数据，可独立使用。
- **评估工具**（`src/ssllab/eval/`）：包括线性探针、效应量、校准和群体指标，以及联合配对 bootstrap，可迁移到任何生成模型评估。
- **数据适配器**（`src/ssllab/data/`）：单细胞和 ECG 适配器，可参考其设计模式来适配新模态。
- **License**：需确认（README 未明确说明）。

# ssl-lab [![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-pleiadian53.github.io%2Fssl--lab-indigo)](https://pleiadian53.github.io/ssl-lab/) 📖 **Documentation site (full math rendering):** ssl-lab develops new methods for **generating biological data that can be trusted like measured data**. Generative models already produce convincing images and video. The goal here is the same capability for experiments: given a biological system and an intervention, generate the dataset the experiment would have produced, accurately enough to explore, prioritize and partly replace work that today needs new sequencing runs or extra assays. The flagship target is **single-cell perturbation data**. Given a population of cells and a genetic perturbation, possibly a combination nobody has run, the model generates the perturbed population: which genes move, by how much, and how much the response varies from cell to cell. The same aim carries to other modalities, including physiological signals, health records and molecular structure. **Reliable is measured, not assumed.** Generated data are scored on the direction and the size of the effects they predict and on whether the generated populations are calibrated, always against strong references: a model of the same task trained from scratch, and a training-free baseline that a useful generator must beat. **The method line: self-supervised representations made generative.** The current build starts from JEPA (joint-embedding predictive architectures), a state-of-the-art self-supervised learner that predicts the *embeddings* of masked regions from their context instead of reconstructing raw data. On its own JEPA learns representations and cannot generate. To sample data the lab adds a **prior** over the latent and a **decoder** back to data space, matched to the data's likelihood. JEPA is the starting point because it is the frontier most worth extending, not a fixed commitment: each component is kept only where it earns its place against those references, and the aim is methods at and beyond the state of the art in both self-supervised learning and generative modeling. A design-space survey of how to make JEPA generative recommends a **conditional flow prior**: generation *given a condition*, such as a perturbation or an intervention, paired with a decoder matched to the data. That conditional architecture is the one shown below. ```mermaid flowchart LR XB(["baseline state x_b"]) --> ENC["JEPA encoder
(frozen)"] P(["intervention p"]) --> EMB["embed e(p)"] ENC -- "z_b" --> COND["condition
c = (z_b, z_p)"] EMB -- "z_p" --> COND NOISE(["noise ε"]) --> FLOW["conditional flow prior

The method is modality-agnostic; its applications (single-cell perturbation, digital phenotyping, and more) and the full design space are the **[Generative JEPA series](docs/generative_jepa/index.md)** and [Research directions](#research-directions) below. This *generative* slice is one of **two complementary extensions of JEPA** the lab pursues. The second turns JEPA from a passive predictor into an *active* world-model, described under [Research directions](#research-directions) below. The two are beginning to **converge**: the condition a generative JEPA samples under can be an *action*, and an action read as a latent **operator** is exactly the world-model line. So "generate the outcome of an intervention" and "plan the intervention" become two faces of one model. ## Why ssl-lab exists ssl-lab is a spin-off of its sibling project [genai-lab](https://github.com/pleiadian53/genai-lab) (generative AI for computational biology). It is where new methods for self-supervised and generative modeling are developed and stress-tested, starting from JEPA and the ideas built around it. The core is kept deliberately **modality-agnostic**, so a method proven on one kind of biological data can move to the next through a data adapter. Methods mature here and return to genai-lab as **genomic generative models** that can stand in for, and help plan, real experiments. ## Research directions JEPA is a *representation learner*: it learns by predicting the embeddings of masked regions from context. ssl-lab pushes it past that in two complementary ways: **1. Generative JEPA: make the representation *sampleable*.** *(method built + de-risked; design space mapped; applications WIP)* Add a prior over the latent and a decoder back to data space. The unconditional slice is verified end to end, with a rich, non-collapsed latent (strong linear-probe accuracy with no pretraining labels) and *genuinely novel* samples. A full **[Generative JEPA design-space survey](docs/generative_jepa/index.md)** then maps four routes for making JEPA generative: decode the latent, a variational posterior, conditioned diffusion, and planning on top. It adds the **conditional flow prior** that unifies them: generation *given an intervention*, with a decoder matched to the data's likelihood. The method is modality-agnostic, and the conditional `v(z, t, c)` path is de-risked as a method; the applications are where it earns its keep: - **Single-cell perturbation response** *(flagship, WIP)*: a staged "cell JEPA": intra-cell pretraining (Stage A) → variational / conditional-flow perturbation predictor (Stage B) → NB/ZINB count decoder (Stage C), on Norman-2019 Perturb-seq, graded on *effect size* (predicting unseen gene combinations) against a from-scratch CVAE baseline. An action-operator transition, an oracle ceiling, a decoder calibration fix and an encoder co-adaptation program have since extended it. Training the encoder together with the decoder brought the full pipeline level with the from-scratch baseline on the size of the predicted change, though not yet on its correlation, and no learned model yet beats the training-free additive reference. The pretraining itself is not shown to contribute at full data, which leaves label- and data-scarce settings as the place where it has to earn its keep. The [results ledger](examples/perturbation_response/docs/results/index.md) tracks every round. - **Digital phenotyping**: e.g. diabetes monitoring and management, where the rollout becomes a *generative personal world model*: a fan of plausible future trajectories under an intervention (this is also where Direction 2's world model meets the generative line). - **Further modalities**: the core is a likelihood-matched conditional generator, so new domains drop in as data adapters; the [data-modalities primer](docs/generative_jepa/appendix-data-modalities.md) surveys single-cell counts, EHR codes, and wearable / CGM streams. **2. Action operators on JEPA: make prediction *active*.** *(research line: tutorial corpus written; theory still developing)* Go from passively in-filling hidden regions to *acting on* them. JEPA's predictor already *is* a latent operator, but its query is a **frozen, blind action**: it says only *where* or *when* to predict, never *what acted*. Promote that query to a **learned operator the model chooses and conditions on**, for both *sensing* ("where should I look?") and *perturbing* ("what happens under this intervention?"), and the passive predictor becomes a controllable **world model**: it can roll futures forward, run counterfactuals ("what if more sleep?"), and surface change that known interventions don't explain. This builds on the **action-operator** formalism from the sibling project [GRL](https://github.com/pleiadian53/GRL), and spans two application poles: continuous behavioral / mental-health monitoring (operator structure *learned*) and protein structure & dynamics (structure *given* by SE(3)). > 📄 **Tutorial series** (full math on the [documentation site](https://pleiadian53.github.io/ssl-lab/)): three parts, read in this order: > - **[Time-Series JEPA](docs/time_series_jepa/index.md)**: the substrate, covering JEPA pointed at time series, multimodal channels, and the one blind spot that motivates operators. Its first runnable instance is the [ECG rhythm study](examples/ecg_rhythm/README.md). > - **[Action Operators](docs/action_operator/00-from-actions-to-operators.md)**: the foundation, covering what an action operator is, why JEPA benefits from one, and a gallery of concrete operators. > - **[Operator World Models](docs/operator_world_models/index.md)**: the synthesis, which conditions the predictor on *what acted* for counterfactual rollout, composable interventions, and a sharpened change signal. > > *Status: an actively developing theoretical line whose operator formalism is still being worked out, not settled. It now reaches into Direction 1. The [Generative JEPA series](docs/generative_jepa/index.md) treats action-conditioning as the bridge: the conditional flow prior's condition can be an action, and Route D's planner is an action operator, so the generative and world-model lines are converging on one substrate.* A concrete motivation in genomics: given an RNA sequence, *sense* to localize candidate splice sites, then *perturb* (in-silico edits / mutations) to learn what they do to splicing. That is the kind of active, hypothesis-driven understanding passive prediction alone can't reach. ## Studies so far Two applied studies have run so far. Each is pre-registered, compares arms within one study, and reports uncertainty alongside every number. Besides their own questions, together they answer a narrower one: what JEPA pretraining buys over training the same model from scratch. - **[Single-cell perturbation response](examples/perturbation_response/README.md)** (Norman 2019 Perturb-seq, twenty held-out two-gene combinations). The task is to generate the perturbed cell population for gene combinations never measured. The generative stack, a JEPA cell encoder with a conditional flow and a count decoder, is graded against a from-scratch conditional NB-VAE and a training-free additive reference. At full data, the from-scratch baseline and additivity lead, and an encoder trained jointly with the decoder from random weights does at least as well as one started from the JEPA weights. The [results ledger](examples/perturbation_response/docs/results/index.md) holds every round. - **[ECG rhythm classification](examples/ecg_rhythm/README.md)** (PTB-XL, 21,799 twelve-lead ECGs). Span-masked JEPA pretraining is compared with the same encoder trained from scratch, at nested label budgets. With labels for 5% of training patients, pretraining adds 0.078 macro AUROC, and the advantage shrinks to a tie when every patient is labelled ([results](examples/ecg_rhythm/results/01-jepa-label-efficiency/README.md)). Read together, the two studies point the same way. Pretraining pays off when labels are scarce and fades when they are plentiful, so label and data efficiency is the axis on which the perturbation study's pretraining is still to be tested. ## Related projects ssl-lab sits in a small constellation of related work: - **[genai-lab](https://github.com/pleiadian53/genai-lab)**: the parent project, focused on generative AI for computational biology. ssl-lab matures methods here and feeds them back to genai-lab for genomic generative models. - **[NMDiff](https://github.com/pleiadian53/nmdiff)**: a **distinct branch of SSL** that sits outside the three classical families. Contrastive (SimCLR/CLIP), predictive (BERT/GPT/MAE), and self-distillation (BYOL/DINO) methods all share one structural property: the labeling function `T` is *fixed*, and only the encoder is learned. NMDiff promotes `T` itself to a domain-parameterized hypothesis `L(·; θ)` and jointly optimizes it with the downstream classifier via an outer-loop cross-view AUC criterion. The labeling function isn't a hyperparameter; it *is* the scientific hypothesis. Call it **hypothesis-driven SSL**: applied to transcript NMD efficiency (where ground-truth labels don't exist), but the pattern generalizes to any label-scarce setting where domain knowledge can parameterize a candidate labeling. Within the 2026 macro-trend of *learning the supervision signal itself*, which also includes self-improving SSL, learned-augmentation SSL, and programmatic weak supervision, NMDiff is the interpretable, low-dimensional, domain-knowledge instance. - **[GRL](https://github.com/pleiadian53/GRL)**: origin of the action-operator formalism that grounds the action-operator research direction above. - **[protein-ml-lab](https://github.com/pleiadian53/protein-ml-lab)** *(sibling, early work in progress)*: new methods for protein modeling and design across the protein-ML stack (ESM, the AlphaFold lineage, RFdiffusion / ProteinMPNN / Chroma). It is the natural home for the action operator's **"given" pole**: there the operators are the rotations and translations of a molecule in 3D space, honest **SE(3)** group elements known in advance, so equivariance is *demanded* rather than learned, and frame-based structure prediction and generation are *operators on SE(3)* made literal (AlphaFold's residue frames, FrameDiff/RFdiffusion flows). Where ssl-lab's operators are **learned** from data, protein-ml-lab's are **known in advance**. These are the two poles of the same expressiveness↔structure dial, in two sibling repos. - **[tabular-icl-lab](https://github.com/pleiadian53/tabular-icl-lab)** *(sibling, early work in progress)*: tabular foundation models and in-context learning (TabPFN) for computational biology, as strong small-data references, evaluation probes and carriers of domain priors. Its first route asks whether a tabular in-context learner can predict what additivity misses in the perturbation study. ## Layout This project follows a use-case-driven R&D convention: reusable primitives in `src/`, thin driver scripts in `examples/`, intuition in `notebooks/`. ``` src/ssllab/ data/ image-proxy, single-cell Perturb-seq and PTB-XL ECG adapters -> modality-agnostic token tensors (signal geometry in physical time; a checksummed WFDB reader) models/ TinyViT backbone, JEPA encoder/predictor, latent decoder jepa/ block masking, EMA target, the assembled JEPA module objectives/ prediction loss + VICReg collapse regularizer generative/ flow prior (unconditional + conditional w/ classifier-free guidance), NB/ZINB count decoder, condition encoder, CVAE baseline, perturbation action operator (+ operator algebra) action_operator/ context-conditioned latent operators — generator bases, exp(M) eval/ collapse diagnostics, linear probe, effect size, calibration and population metrics, interaction scores, joint paired bootstrap with max-t intervals, image-grid viz coadapt.py joint encoder + decoder training (decoder only, joint, joint with the JEPA anchor) anatomy/ step-by-step shape traces of every component, for the architecture viewer utils/ seeding, device selection examples/ jepa_basics/ 01 train JEPA · 02 linear probe generative_jepa/ 03 decoder · 04 flow prior · 05 sample · 06 eval · 07 conditional flow · 08 sample conditional (image proxy) perturbation_response/ cell-JEPA perturbation pipeline (WIP): process Norman -> Stage A pretrain -> count decoder -> conditional flow or action operator -> sample -> effect-size eval (+ CVAE and additive references, ceiling analysis, one scoring script per pre-registered round); co-adaptation/ trains the encoder with the stages that read it ecg_rhythm/ PTB-XL: process -> data card -> labelled-patient subsets -> span-masked JEPA pretraining -> scratch / fine-tune / probe arms -> paired patient-cluster bootstrap -> results page ``` ## Setup ```bash mamba env create -f environment.yml # or: conda env create -f environment.yml conda activate ssllab pip install -e . ``` ## Run the vertical slice ```bash # 1. learn the representation (prints collapse diagnostics each epoch) python examples/jepa_basics/01_train_jepa_mnist.py --epochs 5 # 2. confirm the frozen latent is semantically useful python examples/jepa_basics/02_linear_probe.py # 3. learn to decode the frozen latent back to pixels python examples/generative_jepa/03_train_decoder.py --epochs 5 # 4. learn a sampleable prior over the frozen latent python examples/generative_jepa/04_train_flow_prior.py --epochs 20 # 5. sample z ~ prior, decode -> output/jepa_mnist/samples/samples.png python examples/generative_jepa/05_sample_and_decode.py ``` Artifacts are organized per experiment under `output//`: ``` output/jepa_mnist/ checkpoints/ encoder.pt decoder.pt prior.pt samples/ samples.png recon.png reports/ jepa_train.json probe.json logs/ train.log ``` On a GPU pod this same tree is written under the network volume (`/runpod-volume/ssl-lab/output//`) and rsynced back to the local `output/`: same structure, env-dependent prefix swapped. All scripts share an `--experiment` name (default `jepa_mnist`); pass a new name to keep separate runs side by side. On a GPU pod, the whole chain runs via `examples/generative_jepa/run_pod_pipeline.sh`. ## Remote training Models that don't fit in your local environment train on remote GPU pods. That infra lives in a separate, decoupled package [`ops/`](ops/) (SkyPilot + RunPod) at the repository root: the SSL library never imports it, and it is used from the root without being installed. Quick path: ```bash pip install -e '.[ops]' # PyYAML for compute-check + dry-run python examples/ops/ops_compute_check.py # local vs pod? python examples/ops/ops_run_pipeline.py --gpu a40 -- \ python examples/jepa_basics/01_train_jepa_mnist.py --epochs 50 # dry-run ``` See [ops/README.md](ops/README.md) for the full provision → run → fetch workflow.

one_liner: BCRFoundation 是一个基于单细胞基因表达与BCR序列配对数据的多模态基座模型，支持B细胞特性预测和BCR到RNA的零样本预测，与细胞基座建模方向高度相关，但聚焦B细胞而非通用虚拟细胞/器官。
card:
## 是什么
BCRFoundation 是一个多模态基础模型，基于 scPAIRB 语料库（包含超过 60 万个 B 细胞，每个细胞同时具有单细胞基因表达谱和 BCR 序列）进行预训练。它支持多种下游应用，包括预测 B 细胞特征、抗原特异性，以及直接从 BCR 序列零样本预测基因表达谱。

## 亮点
- **多模态预训练**：同时整合单细胞转录组和 BCR 序列，实现跨模态学习。
- **零样本预测能力**：支持从 BCR 序列直接预测基因表达，无需额外训练。
- **丰富的下游任务支持**：涵盖分类、跨模态预测、特异性预测等，提供多种微调模块。
- **预训练模型直接可用**：仓库包含预训练 checkpoint，便于快速复现和下游应用。
- **文档和教程完善**：提供详细的教程网站，覆盖预训练、分类和零样本预测。

## 为何对本课题有用
BCRFoundation 直接属于“生物基座模型 × 单细胞组学”方向，是虚拟细胞/虚拟器官研究的重要组件。它展示了如何将单细胞转录组与 BCR 序列结合，构建多模态基础模型，这对于理解 B 细胞在免疫反应中的角色、预测抗原特异性以及构建虚拟免疫系统具有直接价值。其零样本 BCR-to-RNA 预测能力可迁移到其他免疫细胞类型（如 T 细胞），为虚拟细胞模型提供跨模态推断的范式。此外，其微调模块（如分类、跨模态）可作为构建 Bio Agent 的工具，用于自动化免疫分析。

## 怎么用
- **主入口**：`BCRFoundation/pretrain.py` 用于预训练，`BCRFoundation/finetune/` 下的模块用于下游任务。
- **安装**：`git clone https://github.com/haotian-zhuang/BCRFoundation.git`，然后 `cd BCRFoundation` 并 `pip install -e .`。依赖见 `pyproject.toml` 和 `requirements.txt`，包括 torch、numpy、scanpy、anndata 等。
- **输入数据**：单细胞基因表达谱（通常为 AnnData 格式）和 BCR 序列（可能为 FASTA 或表格格式）。
- **输出**：预测的细胞特征、抗原特异性或基因表达谱。
- **GPU 需求**：需要 GPU 加速，因为依赖 PyTorch 进行深度学习。
- **调试示例**：`tests/test_cross_modal_zeroshot.py` 提供了零样本跨模态预测的单元测试，可直接运行调试。教程网站提供了具体示例。

## 核心 idea
核心方法学在于通过多模态预训练，将 BCR 序列和基因表达谱映射到共享的嵌入空间，从而捕捉 B 细胞状态与抗原特异性之间的关联。其创新点在于利用大规模配对数据（scPAIRB）进行自监督学习，使得模型能够从序列直接推断转录组状态，实现零样本预测，这为免疫组学中的跨模态推断提供了新范式。

## 可搬移点
- **多模态嵌入模块**（`BCRFoundation/embedding.py`）：可解耦用于将序列和表达数据编码为统一向量，便于集成到自定义 Pipeline 中。
- **零样本跨模态预测模块**（`BCRFoundation/finetune/cross_modal_zerothot.py`）：其逻辑可迁移到其他细胞类型或模态对，实现跨模态推断。
- **微调框架**（`BCRFoundation/finetune/`）：分类、跨模态、特异性预测等模块可逐步替换，适配新任务。
- **License**：MIT 许可，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认具体版本。

# BCRFoundation

[![Version 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.0-blue)](https://github.com/haotian-zhuang/BCRFoundation/blob/main/pyproject.toml)
[![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-tutorials-157d85)](https://haotian-zhuang.github.io/BCRFoundation/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Python 3.11.15+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11.15+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)

BCRFoundation is a multimodal foundation model pretrained on scPAIRB, a curated corpus containing over 0.6 million B cells with paired single-cell gene expression profiles and BCR sequences. BCRFoundation supports diverse downstream applications, including prediction of B cell characteristics and antigen specificity, as well as zero-shot prediction of gene expression profiles directly from BCR sequences.

![Figure 1. Overview of BCRFoundation.](figure/Figure1.png)

## Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/haotian-zhuang/BCRFoundation.git
cd BCRFoundation
pip install -e .
```

The [pretrained checkpoint](pretrain_model/foundation_model_best.pt) is included
for downstream analyses.

## Tutorials

Detailed tutorials are available at this [website](https://haotian-zhuang.github.io/BCRFoundation/).

1. [Pretraining](https://haotian-zhuang.github.io/BCRFoundation/tutorials/01_pretraining.html)
2. [B cell characteristics prediction](https://haotian-zhuang.github.io/BCRFoundation/tutorials/02_classification.html)
3. [Zero-shot BCR-to-RNA prediction](https://haotian-zhuang.github.io/BCRFoundation/tutorials/03_BCR2RNA.html)

See [data and checkpoint requirements](https://haotian-zhuang.github.io/BCRFoundation/data_and_checkpoints.html) before running
the tutorials. Each example uses the settings from the corresponding analysis.

## Citation

Citation information will be added with the corresponding publication.

## Contact

Author: Haotian Zhuang

Report bugs and provide suggestions by sending email to:

Maintainer: Haotian Zhuang (haotian.zhuang@duke.edu)

Or open a new issue on this GitHub page.
